items.title: Game speed handled properly
items.body:
Objective: Handle game speed correctly — read live speed, adjust via the game's own button handlers (not by writing the field), confirm from the game's own state, and make the multiplier an explicit declared parameter so budgeted game time = frames × frame_game_ms × multiplier.

Done-condition: A 5-episode scripted arm at a declared effective 100 ms step gives total_round_seconds/total_budgeted_game_seconds ≈ 1.011, decisions/wave ≈ 21, mean final wave in the 5.5–6.2 band, zero GAME_TIME_INFLATED, zero BRIDGE_EVENT_DIVERGENCE.

Evidence: docs/experiments.md entry.

Note: currently in flight.

comments.text: Fixed and device-verified at 9cc3a233: total_round_seconds/total_budgeted_game_seconds = 1.0118, decisions/wave = 20.73, mean final wave 6.0, zero GAME_TIME_INFLATED. Speed is pinned once at the episode boundary via the game's own control (commit 9cc3a23), never re-pinned mid-round. See docs/workstation-handoff.md 'Standing decisions' item 1 and docs/experiments.md M1B-E024.

items.title: Snapshot bring-up keyed to the bridge build
items.body:
Objective: Snapshot bring-up keyed to the bridge build — restore-and-connect with no network window and an identical starting account state; fall back to the cold path on key mismatch or failed verification.

Done-condition: An instance comes up from snapshot in roughly 10 s with no radios enabled at any point, verified offline by interface, and runs episodes.

Evidence: docs/experiments.md entry.

Note: in flight.

comments.text: The Vulkan limitation is now handled honestly. The emulator refuses to save a snapshot of the game (Vulkan) under -gpu host, replying `KO: Snapshot save is skipped. Reason: UNSUPPORTED_VK_APP`. clone_session.py's save_snapshot previously printed that reply and reported success anyway, so a later restore loaded stale renderer state from a mismatched renderer, found no running game, and silently fell back to the cold path — the fallback was right, the false success was not. save_snapshot now requires the emulator's own OK reply plus a positive check that the snapshot directory exists, and raises naming the reason and the renderer otherwise. bring_up no longer attempts a save or restore under any renderer but lavapipe: under -gpu host it goes straight to the cold path and logs one line explaining why. Keyed-snapshot naming, restore-and-verify, and mismatch/failed-verification fallback all remain unchanged and covered by tests. Consequence, recorded in docs/workstation-handoff.md: snapshots stay lavapipe-only, and since training runs on -gpu host (see #8), host bring-up is cold every time (45-60s, not ~10s).
Superseded by ADR 0016 (5aa5ded): snapshots rejected for starts/recovery under -gpu host; cold -read-only relaunch is the recovery path. Board audit #125.

items.title: Test suite hangs when runs overlap
items.body:
Objective: Fix test suite hangs when runs overlap. Torch sizes its thread pool to the core count, so two concurrent pytest runs thrash — two orphaned runs burned 25 CPU-hours and invalidated a measurement. Fix at conftest level so it applies regardless of collection order or path selection.

Done-condition: Two concurrent full-suite runs complete in roughly normal time.

Evidence: the commit that closes it.

comments.text: Mitigated, root cause unconfirmed. `tests/conftest.py` (environment branch f9fd489, merging shortly) bounds torch threads for the test process and removes six per-file `set_num_threads(1)` calls. Measured: two overlapping full suites complete in 41 s with the bound vs 63 s without (single run 41.8 s) — a real 1.5x contention cost removed. The original hang was NOT reproduced, so thread oversubscription is confirmed as a cost, not confirmed as the cause of the 25-CPU-hour incident. Independent review recommends recording as mitigated rather than closed. Reopen-trigger: any recurrence.
investigation (read-only) while the device is busy

Investigated (read-only, no device access). No unbounded blocking call found: adb() has a 30s default timeout and every fleet/actor test explicitly avoids real adb/device (test_multi_actor.py, test_fleet_training.py docstrings); test_tracking.py uses tmp_path, not the real state/mlflow.db; no threading.Thread.join anywhere in src or tests. The already-merged conftest.py fix (f9fd489, OMP/MKL/torch thread pinning) remains the only confirmed lever — root cause of the literal hang (vs. slowdown) still unconfirmed. Suggest a defensive pytest-timeout backstop as minimal follow-up; details in session report.

Mitigation (conftest single-thread torch, f9fd489) plus backstop: `pytest-timeout` now enforces a 120 s per-test timeout (`timeout_method = thread`) via `pyproject.toml`. Root cause of the original 25-CPU-hour hang is unconfirmed; the backstop makes a recurrence fail loudly, by name, instead of hanging.
fix ready on a worker branch; merge waits for the same gap (no dependency installs in the live checkout)

Merged: 7f63ac96a376aa38590f4ab15969e064969cb420
Gate: pytest 781 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean (all exit 0) — gated together with #49

The project commits to a single backbone, `stacked-dqn` — it is a constant (`BACKBONE = "stacked-dqn"` in `scripts/train.py`), not a selectable arm, so there is no second backbone to run under an equal decision budget and the done-condition can no longer be met as written.

items.title: Multi-actor scaling at N = 1/2/4
items.body:
Objective (deferred): Multi-actor scaling at N = 1/2/4 with scripts/run_actors.py; currently unmeasured.

Done-condition: Throughput/quality measured at N = 1/2/4 and recorded.

Evidence: docs/experiments.md entry.

comments.text:
Found while starting a second instance by hand: the emulator requires every
instance sharing one AVD to be `-read-only`, including index 0. Instance 0 was
running via the normal single-instance path (`clone_session.py up`, no
`--read-only`, e.g. `-cores 8 -port 5556 -no-snapshot-save -no-snapshot-load`),
so any second instance was refused outright — this blocks N > 1 here.

`scripts/run_actors.py`'s own fleet mechanism was already correct:
`collect_episodes` unconditionally passes `read_only=True` for every actor
instance it launches, including index 0. The gap was at the layer below it:
`clone_session.py` had no way to refuse a non-read-only index > 0 before
asking the emulator, so the mistake (bringing index 0 up writable, then trying
to add a second instance) only surfaced as the emulator's own opaque refusal
on whichever instance came up second.

Fix (this repo, clone_session.py): `launch_emulator` now calls a
`require_shareable(instance, read_only)` guard before touching the emulator or
adb at all — any index > 0 launched without `--read-only` raises immediately
with a message naming the instance and the reason. Index 0 is still allowed to
launch writable, but only alone (e.g. to save a snapshot); the docstring's
worked example now shows index 0 started `--read-only` before a second index
is added. Defaults were left unchanged (`--read-only` stays opt-in) since
`prepare_pinned_snapshot` and the plain single-instance `up` path need to run
index 0 writable to save a snapshot.

Remaining for this issue: whether several `-read-only` instances can actually
restore the shared snapshot concurrently is still unverified on device — that
part needs the next device stage, not a code change.

Measured on device, N=1/2/4, `scripts/run_actors.py`, aggregate valid episodes/hour:

| N | valid episodes/hour |
|---|---|
| 1 | 8,850 |
| 2 | 18,704 |
| 4 | 27,781 (steady state ~37k) |

Scaling is linear to at least 4 actors; fidelity (health counters: bridge
divergence, stale/duplicate, cut-short advances, not-fresh episodes) is intact
at every N — several `-read-only` instances do restore the one shared
snapshot concurrently with no corruption.

One defect found at N=4: booting all four emulators at the same instant
peaked host load at 10.71 and total CPU at 1,835%, and the last of the four
never left `main_unavailable` within its 300s cold-launch timeout, while its
three peers each reached home alone in 60-90s. Steady-state collection uses
only 563% of 3,200% available CPU, so the contention is entirely in the
simultaneous boot, not in running.

Fix: `run_actors.stagger_bring_up` sequences each instance's bring-up after
the previous instance signals ready (success or failure), instead of starting
all bring-ups at once; episode collection afterwards is unchanged and runs
exactly as concurrently as before. The per-actor cold-launch timeout (300s)
is left as is, since sequencing removes the contention that caused the one
timeout seen, rather than the timeout itself being too short.

Done-condition met: aggregate valid episodes/hour is now measured as a
function of N, with fidelity verified at each N.

Done. Multi-actor scaling measured and recorded across commits 7530dc5 ("Collect with a fleet of actors into one learner") and bb64a7a ("Record actor-scaling, render-target, and evidence-hygiene findings"); results in docs/experiments.md entries M1B-E029 (actor-count scaling to eight) and M1B-E035 (100,000-decision, 4-actor training run). Closing.

items.title: Spectate/review mode
items.body:

comments.text:
Starting #12 (spectate/review mode), software only — no emulator and no adb from this packet; the 7.5-hour training run (#31) holds the host until ~05:50 and device verification of this is a separate later packet.

Building to the rulings already made: an optional `on_decision` observer on `InstrumentedRunEnvironment` emitting a frozen per-decision view, `scripts/spectate.py` as composition only (windowed `-read-only` instance at 60 Hz = real time, curses panel over the decision stream, optional guest `screenrecord`, exclusive-host refusal), same episode records as the fleet, no new package module and no web UI.

Merged: 12e2de8 (spectate: DecisionView/on_decision observer in environment, windowed launch in simulation, scripts/spectate.py owning the panel/recording/exclusive-host refusal).

Gate green post-merge: 559 tests pass, ruff clean, mypy clean, 7 import-contract tests pass, `spectate.py --help` runs.

Device verification pending — no emulator/adb run from this packet (training run #31 holds the host); the implementer's enumerated device-check list wasn't found in this issue's thread to cite by number, so the Lead should confirm/attach it before the first watch session.

## Device verification (pending the #31 run and its post-hoc evaluation)

Everything landed for #12 is software-verified only (full suite, ruff, strict mypy, import contracts, `--help`; no emulator or adb touched). These are the checks that still need a real instance, in order. They need the host to themselves, so they wait for the #31 training run and its post-hoc evaluation to finish.

1. **Windowed launch.** `emulator @tower_rl_instrumented_api36` starts with a visible window under `-gpu host -read-only` and still boots inside the 300 s bound `wait_for_boot` holds it to.
2. **`confirm_frame_rate` at 60.** `raise_frame_rate(instance, 60)` confirms. The read-back has only ever been exercised at 120, and a surface already at the stock rate may not publish an applied rate it accepts.
3. **Real time is real.** A spectated episode’s `round_ms` should be ≈ its `elapsed_wall_seconds` — one game second per wall second — against the fleet’s measured speed-up at 120 Hz.
4. **Bring-up unchanged by the window.** Bridge deploy with digest confirmation, `require_offline` and `require_game_activity` all behave identically with a window attached.
5. **The panel.** Readable beside the game window; cash and health match what the screen shows; the death line appears on the same decision the tower dies, not one later.
6. **Hold and teardown.** The panel survives the last episode, the keypress (or `--hold-seconds`) ends the hold, and teardown leaves nothing — `adb devices` empty afterwards.
7. **`--record`.** A session longer than three minutes produces at least two playable chunks, the last one is finalised rather than truncated, and every guest-side file is removed.
8. **The refusal, positively.** Start `spectate.py` while any emulator is running and confirm it exits by name without touching anything.

Plus one added by the review fixes:

9. **`screenrecord` exit status.** Confirm that `screenrecord` interrupted by `pkill -INT` exits non-zero on this image. That status is what decides whether a chunk is pulled as `-partial`, so if an interrupted recording exits 0 here the naming is wrong in the quiet direction.

## Device checks 1-9: eight pass, check 9 fails in the direction it was written to catch

Two sessions on `emulator-5556` (clone AVD, `-read-only`, `-gpu host`, windowed on the real desktop). No code changed on the device.

**1. Windowed launch — PASS.** `launching tower_rl_instrumented_api36 on emulator-5556 (host, read-only, windowed)`; emulator 37.1.11, gfxstream, a real window on `DISPLAY=:0`. Boot, deploy, launch-online/cut-radios, the 60 Hz confirm, the bridge connect and the first decision all landed inside 45 s of launch — far inside the 300 s `wait_for_boot` bound, which was never approached.

**2. `confirm_frame_rate` at 60 — PASS.** `emulator-5556: confirmed at 60 Hz: display vsync mode 60.00, uid 10218 game mode override 60, uid 10218 applied frame rate 60.00`. Three readings, all present. The worry that a surface already at the stock rate might publish no applied rate did not materialise.

**3. Real time is real — PASS.** The spectated episode: `round_ms` 278,669 (278.7 game seconds) against `elapsed_wall_seconds` 272.991. Ratio 1.02x — one game second per wall second. The same checkpoint on the 120 Hz fleet has a median speed-up of 1.97x.

**4. Bring-up unchanged by the window — PASS.** `deployed bridge confirmed 7a98f50be6d6c6ec262f332e60511f4e6f84f61da66691c626e7d4bb8ad7f99a`, then `emulator-5556 is at home and offline`. Read back independently while the window was up: only `lo` carries an IPv4 (`inet 127.0.0.1/8`), and `topResumedActivity=com.TechTreeGames.TheTower/com.unity3d.player.UnityPlayerActivity`. One cosmetic note, not a fault: `instrumented_bridge.sh deploy` tags the stderr of `adb push` and `am start` as `deploy: error:` lines even when nothing failed, so a successful deploy reads alarmingly.

**5. The panel — PASS.** Rendered from the captured pty at 120x50, the frame the death is reported in:

```
tower-rl spectate — checkpoint-0050123 — episode 1 of 1

wave 8   cash 15   health 0%   reward +0
episodes played 1   mean final wave 8.00   decisions 189   0.0/min
episode 1 ended at wave 8: game_over
```

The death line is written in the same redraw as `e1 d189` and before the hold footer, so it lands on the decision the tower dies on, not one later. The panel`'s final wave (8) and decision count (189) equal what the evaluator wrote to `emulator-5556.json` independently. What is still the developer`'s to do is the eye comparison of cash/health against the game window itself.

Worth recording for anyone who runs this unattended: `--no-panel` prints `lines[2] | lines[0]` only, so it gives cash and health per decision (`wave 5   cash 16   health 0%`) but **never the death line** — `episode N ended at wave W: game_over` exists in the curses panel alone.

**6. Hold and teardown — PASS.** After the last episode the panel held (`session over — press any key to tear the instance down`, 20 s), then teardown: `game_frame_rate_override: reset`, `libunity_mounts: 0`, `bridge_artifacts: removed`. Afterwards `adb devices` empty and zero `qemu` walking `/proc/*/exe`.

**7. `--record` — PASS.** Two chunks: `-000.mp4` 179.99 s / 162,468,268 B (its own 180 s limit), `-001.mp4` 144.55 s / 92,320,194 B. `ffprobe` reads both as `mov,mp4,m4a` h264 360x640 with durations — the last is finalised, not truncated. Guest-side removal was caught directly, polling at 0.5 s: all chunks present at 10:12:34.657, gone at 10:12:35.175, device down at 10:12:36.254. Removed before teardown, with room to spare.

**8. The refusal, positively — PASS.** Launched from a second shell against a live instance: exit 1, nothing touched, and it names both witnesses — `refusing to spectate while an emulator is running (adb: emulator-5556; qemu processes: 1114598 .../qemu-system-x86_64)`. The running instance was unaffected.

**9. `screenrecord` exit status — FAIL, and exactly the quiet direction.** On this image `screenrecord` interrupted by SIGINT exits **zero**. Read by hand on a live instance, both ways:

```
targeted-kill-INT rc=0
pkill-INT rc=0
```

The code`'s own naming corroborates it: session A`'s chunk 001 ran 144.55 s of its 180 s limit — it was plainly interrupted — and came back as `-001.mp4` with no `-partial`; a second session produced three chunks, every one of them interrupted, none named `-partial`. So `chunk.partial = "rc=0" not in reply` can never be true for an interrupt, and the `-partial` suffix cannot distinguish an interrupted chunk from a whole one. The files are fine — SIGINT makes `screenrecord` finalise and exit cleanly, which is why they play — but the distinction the suffix was added to draw does not exist on this image. Not patched here; this is a decision for the Lead.

Host left clean: `adb devices` empty, zero `qemu`, no stray processes.

## M2-E003 recorded; the spectate path is usable on the desktop today

Branch `spectate-device-check` at `6a0eaec`, one commit, `docs/experiments.md` only — `## M2-E003 — Spectate mode on device`. Based on `77e6369` rather than the `50fae46` the packet named: `M2-E002` merged to main while these sessions were running, and `M2-E003` has to sit above it for the log to stay newest-first. Nothing between the two commits touches `scripts/spectate.py`, `simulation/` or `environment/`, so what was measured at `50fae46` is what main has. Not closing `#12`, not merging.

**The recording run.** `checkpoint-0050123` (identity `8344a482eede`, the `M2-E002` selection) played one episode to **final wave 8** over **189 decisions** and 24 purchases, ending `game_over`, valid. Episode wall **272.991 s**, session wall **326.3 s**. Two chunks in `~/.local/state/tower-rl/spectate/`: `checkpoint-0050123-episode1-000.mp4` (179.99 s, 162,468,268 B) and `-001.mp4` (144.55 s, 92,320,194 B), both h264 360x640 and both playable. Episode record at `~/.local/state/tower-rl/spectate/records/emulator-5556.json`.

**The developer can run this live now**, unchanged, on the desktop session:

```text
uv run python scripts/spectate.py \
  --policy checkpoint:~/.local/state/tower-rl/runs/session-20260918-215839/stacked-dqn-20260918-215839-e3c6ba/checkpoints/checkpoint-0050123.pt \
  --episodes 1 --frame-rate-hz 60
```

Expect roughly four minutes from wave 1 to the death at real time, a window and a panel beside it, and a keypress to end the hold. Add `--record <name>.mp4` and `--output-directory <dir>` to keep the video and the episode record. Nothing in the nine checks needs a second attempt or a different machine.

**The one open item is check 9**, and it is a decision rather than a reading: `screenrecord` exits 0 when interrupted, so `-partial` never fires and an interrupted chunk is named as though it were whole. The chunk is still playable — that is the same fact seen from the other side, since SIGINT makes the tool finalise cleanly — so the cost is only that the name does not warn. Detail and evidence are in the `M2-E003` entry.

Host left as found: `adb devices` empty, zero `qemu` via `/proc/*/exe`, no stray processes, the canonical AVD never touched and 5554 never used.

Check 9 resolved, code side, at `549b795` on `spectate-device-check`.

`screenrecord` interrupted by SIGINT exits **0** on this image — SIGINT is how the tool is asked to stop, and it finalises the file before going. Three interrupted chunks all read back through `ffprobe` as valid MP4 with durations. So `chunk.partial` could never be true for an interrupt: `-partial` marked nothing while suggesting the distinction was being watched.

**Decision applied:** the partial flag, the `-partial` suffix and the `; echo rc=$?` that fed them are removed from `GuestRecording`. A chunk is whole; how long it ran is its duration's business. If a future image truncates on interrupt, the evidence for a warning is a chunk `ffprobe` cannot read, not an exit status.

Also on the branch: `--no-panel` was printing health reaching 0 and never naming the death, so an unattended log made its reader infer it. `panel_lines` now reserves `DEATH_LINE` and both panels read the ended-episode line from that one index; `PlainPanel` prints it on the decision the episode ends. Three tests cover it, the M2-E003 entry records finding and decision.

Gate green: 566 passed / 2 skipped (mlflow absent), `ruff check` clean, `mypy` clean on 49 files, 7 import-contract tests — all exit 0. `ruff format` is not a project gate and its pre-existing count is unchanged at 50. Not merged.

Merged: 021d925a4c926ef12c138efa5abb3b54a2a02d96
Gate: pytest 568 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean (all exit 0)
Experiment: M2-E003 (docs/experiments.md)

items.title: clone_session launch_emulator swallowed the emulator's own error
items.body:
Objective: `launch_emulator` (scripts/clone_session.py) ran the emulator with
`stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=DEVNULL`. When the emulator refused to start
(`ERROR | Another emulator instance is running. Please close it or run all
emulators with -read-only flag.`), the operator saw nothing and `wait_for_boot`
burned its full 300s timeout looking like a hang; the cause was only found by
re-running the emulator command by hand. Same class of defect as the
`UNSUPPORTED_VK_APP` false-success fixed at cddc6e6.

Fix: capture the emulator's stdout/stderr to a file, and on a boot timeout or
an early process exit surface what it actually said in the raised `CloneError`.
Do not print the log on a successful launch.

Done-condition: a launch failure's error message quotes the emulator's own
output; a boot timeout's error message includes captured output. Covered by
unit tests in tests/unit/test_clone_session.py (no device).

Evidence: the commit that closes it.

comments.text: Done. Fixed in commit f251dc8 ("Surface the emulator's own voice, and refuse a second instance loudly"), which captures the emulator's stdout/stderr to a per-serial log and quotes it in the CloneError raised on an early exit or boot timeout. Covered by tests in tests/unit/test_clone_session.py. Closing.

items.title: Speed gate: behavioural equivalence of the raised frame rate vs 60 Hz on low-variance per-wave statistics
items.body:
Objective: check that the raised frame rate from the N=7 speed gate does not change game behaviour on statistics where it would show, before training relies on it.

Done-condition: intervals reported with sensitivity analysis on low-variance per-wave statistics; the setting is either cleared for training or rejected.

Dependency: the N=7 fleet-safe frame-rate issue landing first.

comments.text:
### Analysis half landed; capture change is a hard prerequisite (commit d3ee3e4)

`src/tower_rl/experiment/wave_statistics.py` implements per-wave-index paired comparisons (bootstrap CI, Cohen's d, detectable difference at 80% power as the algebraic inverse of `required_episodes`), pooled across indices with the pooled detectable effect taken at the widest single index. Demonstration (test `test_per_wave_detects_a_shift_the_final_wave_cannot_see`): 25 episodes/arm, +10% game-time per wave in arm B, identical final waves — per-wave separates at all 11 comparable indices (wave 1: −2981 ms [−3548, −2445], d=−2.92, floor 808 ms; pooled d=−3.08); final wave on the same sample: +0.00 [−1.20, +1.20], could not detect < 1.76 waves.

**Blocker:** no per-wave quantity is recorded today. `EpisodeSummary` has no per-wave field, `Actor.EpisodeResult` returns only the summary, and `run_environment` folds `game_ms`/`round_ms` into one episode tally. Required capture change (in `environment/run_environment.py` + `episode.py`, after #19 merges): an optional `"waves"` list per episode record of `{wave, completed, game_ms, decisions, health_fraction, cash_log}`, where `game_ms` is the measured `result.round_ms` attributed to the current wave per advance, `decisions`/`health_fraction`/`cash_log` fold at the wave boundary from the transition state, and `completed` is false for the wave the run dies in (fragments are excluded from comparison). Cash exists only log-scaled in observation-v1.

Invocation once data exists: `uv run python -c "from tower_rl.experiment.wave_statistics import analyse_reports; print(analyse_reports('A.json','B.json'))"`.

Sequencing: #21 lands → #19 merges → per-wave capture → #22 device run (60 Hz vs 120 Hz, scripted, same wall-clock window, ≥25 episodes/arm).

Per-instance frame-rate parameter merged at 3bfa540.
Device stage continues running from the same code (branch worktree-agent-ac088635634d0a00d, docs-only commits ahead).

Device stage ran: one fleet, N=7, interleaved rates (4 × 60 Hz, 3 × 120 Hz), scripted, cold `-gpu host`, 606 s inside a 45-minute timebox. 27 valid episodes at 60 Hz, 26 at 120 Hz; one 60 Hz instance lost before its first episode, cause unexplained.

**Verdict on the pre-registered rule: REJECT, provisional.** `game_ms` separated at no wave index (differences −29 to +128 ms against 63–284 ms detectable), `decisions` and `health_fraction` at none; `cash_log` separated in the same direction at waves 5 and 6 — 2 of 7 comparable wave indices, 28.6% against the rule's 20% criterion.

Recorded honestly beside it: the 20% criterion was calibrated where 62 wave indices were comparable, and this run reached 7, where one stray index is already 14.3%. The rule's replication clause is therefore unmet — one replication from the written recipe in a fresh session is required before anything is acted on. **120 Hz is not cleared for training; this issue stays open.**

Fidelity zero in both arms (`GAME_TIME_INFLATED`/`DEFLATED`, `ADVANCE_TRUNCATED_BY_WALL`, `advances_cut_short` all 0; round/budgeted 0.989–1.013). Teardown complete on all seven. Deployed-bridge digest read back as nothing again: recorded unconfirmed, not passed. Full entry: `M1B-E053` in `docs/experiments.md`.

**Replication of the equivalence fleet (`M1B-E054`): E053's REJECT is not replicated and does not stand.**

Same recipe, unchanged, fresh session that read neither E053 nor its raw analysis until its own verdict was written. 7/7 instances reported, each confirmed at its assigned rate on all three SurfaceFlinger readings; **36 valid at 60 Hz, 27 at 120 Hz**; every fidelity guard zero in both arms; E053's `did not reach an active run` loss did not recur. Deployed bridge digest read back on all seven this time (`su -c 'sha256sum …'`, the form E053/E046 missed).

The rule fires nowhere: `cash_log` separates at **1 of 9** wave indices (11.1% vs the 20% criterion) and at **neither** of E053's waves 5 and 6; `health_fraction` nowhere; `game_ms` at one index only, where trigger (a) needs two. Verdict: **no difference detectable at this n**.

Honest caveat, unchanged from E053: at 7–9 comparable indices the 20% criterion cannot separate a null's stray index from a real effect, and this run's detectable differences at waves 5–6 (≥0.485, ≥0.649) exceed the effects E053 reported there (+0.34, +0.46), so this is a failure to reproduce, not proof of absence.

Leaving this open for the Lead's reading of the pair.

Merged at 4c0c842 (--no-ff merge of 648b9dc, docs-only).

Verdict: Provisional REJECT on cash_log in E053 (2 of 7 wave indices) did not replicate in E054 (1 of 9, different index, original indices cover zero); under the pre-registered rule it does not stand. Per-wave effects below d≈0.7 remain undetectable at this depth. 120 Hz cleared for training.

Watch item: 60 Hz cash nominally higher in both runs, to be tracked as a training diagnostic (not a blocking rejection).

items.title: Bridge digest read-back uses `su 0 sha256sum`, which returns nothing on this image; use the `su -c` form
items.body: E046/E053 recorded the deployed-bridge SHA as unconfirmed on every instance because the runner's read-back form yields no output; `adb shell "su -c 'sha256sum …'"` (the repo's own `su_device` form) returns the digest (E054, 7/7). Fix the runner's read-back after #16 lands (the code is moving into `simulation`); until then "unconfirmed" in those entries means the oracle, not the bridge.

comments.text: Starting. Worktree at 079e8e9. Plan: find every deployed-bridge read-back site, make one form (the `su -c` form that answered 7/7 in M1B-E048) the single read-back used by both the CLI and the fleet path, compare it against the host artifact digest, and fail by name on empty output or mismatch, so "unconfirmed" stops being a silent outcome. One short device check at the end.

Done in `b3e2aea` (not merged). Device check on index 0, cold, `-gpu host`, `-read-only`, 120 Hz:

```
emulator-5556 deploy: deployed bridge confirmed 7a98f50be6d6c6ec262f332e60511f4e6f84f61da66691c626e7d4bb8ad7f99a
```

Why the fleet form returned nothing, measured on that instance while the bridge was deployed:

- `adb shell sha256sum <path>` → `Permission denied`, exit 1. adbd runs as `uid=2000(shell)`, and the deployed bridge is app-private, so the read needs root.
- `adb shell su 0 sha256sum <path>` → no output, exit 0. Not a permission or path problem: `adb shell su 0 id` is also silent and exits 0, so this image's `su` accepts the `0` and never runs the command it was given. A sampler reading its stdout sees nothing and can only record "unconfirmed".
- `adb shell "su -c 'sha256sum <path>'"` → the digest. This is the form kept, the same one the script has always used for its libunity read-backs.

The read-back is now one function on the one path the CLI and the fleet both deploy through, and rejects anything that is not 64 hex characters, so `sha256sum:`-prefixed error text cannot be read as a digest (the `M1B-E047` misfire).

Merged in a6f48c6.
No digest read-back existed in the tree before this change; su 0 <cmd> swallows the command's stdout on this device image, returning nothing.
Fixed with the su -c 'cmd' form and confirmed working by name on the device.

items.title: Deployable bridge artifact and `/tmp/tower-bridge-live.latest` live in a session scratchpad; move to `~/.local/state/tower-rl/`
items.body: The pointer currently targets this session's build directory, which does not survive a reboot; the deployable artifact (SHA `7a98f50be6d6c6ec262f332e60511f4e6f84f61da66691c626e7d4bb8ad7f99a`) needs a durable home outside the repo, and the deploy path should refuse a dangling pointer by name.

comments.text: One more artifact whose location is derived rather than configured, for this issue to pick up: `simulation/bridge.py` finds `instrumented_bridge.sh` with `BRIDGE_SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "instrumented_bridge.sh"` — a package module walking out of `src/` to reach the repo layout. It resolves in every layout in use today (the venv is an editable install, verified), so #16 left it alone deliberately; but the wheel target packages `src/tower_rl` only and ships no `scripts/`, so a non-editable install would not find it. Same concern as `/tmp/tower-bridge-live.latest`: where a bridge artifact lives and how it is found.

Starting. Worktree at 079e8e9. Plan: give the deployable bridge a durable home under `~/.local/state/tower-rl/bridge/`, keyed by the artifact digest with a `current` pointer, resolve the deploy path from there, refuse by name on a dangling pointer or a digest that does not match its recorded name, keep the `parents[3]` script derivation but assert the script exists with a named error, and update the handoff paragraph.

Done in `944aa7d` (not merged).

Layout: `~/.local/state/tower-rl/bridge/<sha256>/` holds `libtower_bridge.so`, the patched `libunity-bridge.so` and `CMakeCache.txt` — the whole set a deploy consumes, since the overlay and the compatibility identity come from the same place as the artifact — with `current` a symlink to the installed one. A symlink rather than a `current.sha256` file because `ls -l` then shows the digest without opening anything. The existing artifact was copied there and re-hashed (`7a98f50b…f99a`, and `libunity-bridge.so` `0c2e515e…71c4`) before `current` was pointed at it.

Resolution lives in `bridge.installed_bridge_directory`; `bring_up.bridge_build_directory` now delegates instead of holding a second copy of the rule, and `instrumented_bridge.sh` follows the same pointer for the hand-run path. It refuses by name on a missing or dangling `current` and on an artifact that does not hash to the directory name it is filed under. `TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR` still overrides everything.

`BRIDGE_SCRIPT` keeps `parents[3]` and is checked before use, so a moved package gets a named failure rather than a bare `FileNotFoundError` out of `subprocess`.

Verified on device: the cold bring-up pushed from `/home/furkan/.local/state/tower-rl/bridge/current/` and the deployed digest confirmed. Still reading `/tmp/tower-bridge-live.latest` and outside this packet's pathspec: `scripts/train.py`, `scripts/compare_arms.py`, `scripts/run_episodes.py`.

Merged in a6f48c6.
Artifact now lives at ~/.local/state/tower-rl/bridge/current, resolved via symlink.
Deploy pre-flight refuses a dangling pointer or a digest mismatch before pushing to device.

items.title: Speed: CPU per frame — guest resolution and render elimination, solo measurement then per-wave equivalence
items.body: Fleet rate is contention-bound on host CPU per frame. Experiment A (solo, 120 Hz): baseline vs halved guest resolution vs camera rendering disabled through the native bridge; read host CPU% of the emulator process and SurfaceFlinger ms/frame. Prediction if real: ≥30% less CPU per frame; falsified if within ~10% of baseline. Experiment B only if A pays: the M1B-E053/E054 per-wave equivalence protocol, same pre-registered rule, before any use for training. Rendering off carries a behaviour risk (visibility-dependent game logic).

comments.text:
Phase 1 (resolution) ran and is FALSIFIED: at a fixed 120 Hz, 360x640 -> 200x356 (3.24x fewer pixels) left emulator CPU at 160.8% against a 157.0-160.8% baseline (two C0 runs), inside the baseline's own spread and far from the predicted >=30% fall. C2 not run, per the rule that it follows only an effect at C1.
Measured ms/frame 8.177 / 8.186 / 8.184 across arms - the guest is paced by the 120 Hz vsync, not by render time. Per-thread: ~85% of the emulator process is its four vCPU threads, ~7% is host-side RenderThread, unchanged by resolution; no gfx/llvmpipe/Vk thread uses measurable CPU under -gpu host.
Fidelity zero in every reported arm (3/3 valid each, round/budgeted 1.0099-1.0117). Method: runtime `wm size`/`wm density` between bridge deploy and the bring-up's own game launch, reset before teardown; no AVD config edited.
Two device constraints found: WindowManagerService clamps a forced size to 200 px per dimension (so 180x320 became 200x320), and an arm whose dp layout was not preserved broke the game's own speed control (`speed_down: lifecycle_timeout`) before any episode ran.
Recorded as M1B-E055 on branch `experiment/m1b-e055-cpu-resolution` (b4642fb). Render elimination (phase 2) is not supported by where the CPU actually is.

Phase 1 falsified: 3.24x fewer pixels changed emulator CPU by 0.0%/+2.4% at 120 Hz (RenderThread ~7% of the process, UnityGfxDeviceW ~21% of the guest, UnityMain 47%). Resolution is not a CPU lever.

Phase 2 (render elimination via `OnDemandRendering.renderFrameInterval=16` static-field write from the bridge, read back via `GetEffectiveRenderFrameRate`) would remove at most the fixed ~20-25% render share, at the cost of a bridge change plus a three-arm per-wave equivalence ladder (1/2/16) for visibility-gated logic. Deferred behind Milestone 2 by Lead ruling.

Specialist notes: session scratchpad `RENDER-ELIMINATION.md`.
Stage 1 (software: bridge render_off + fps readout) started; design by specialist, implementation to follow; device stages only after run 4 frees the device.

Design correction (specialist): production runs at 16.667 ms game time per frame (CadenceConfig default), not 100 ms; the fleet is held by 120 Hz vsync (8.4–8.9 ms/frame in advances), so render-off helps only if skipped frames escape vsync pacing — solo ceiling ≈2× (targetFrameRate 240); main unknown: Choreographer pacing. Mechanism: OnDemandRendering.m_RenderFrameInterval via il2cpp static field, build-time variant, default build byte-identical.
Stage 1 landed 0261642; default build reproduced f9d5f161 on merged main; stage 2 (solo device measurement) pending after run 4.

Stage 2 (render-off solo measurement) run: NO-GO on the literal pre-registered rule.

Arms: A = installed bridge (`f9d5f161...`), B = `TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR=state/bridge/builds/render-interval-16` (`7b5e9701...`), both `libunity-bridge.so` unchanged (`0c2e5157...`). Solo, 1 instance, scripted, 3 episodes/arm, `frame_game_ms` 100 (M2-S001 default).

- fps ratio B/A = 2.08x (≥1.5, passes)
- game-s/wall-s ratio B/A = 1.56x (≥1.5, passes)
- Fidelity: `render interval=16 readback=16` confirmed (9 lines), `effective_render_fps` ≈15 (240/16), consistent with the interval engaging the present rate. But the design's chosen per-advance skip-proof, `renderprobe frames=F rendered=R`, shows R≈F (≈1/1) across 326 lines, not ≈1/16 as required — `Time.renderedFrameCount` does not reflect the throttled present rate. This directly contradicts the readback/effective_render_fps evidence.
- 557 "permitted lifetime of 4 frames" lines observed in B.

Since the pre-registered gate requires the renderprobe ratio ≈1/16 for fidelity to count clean, and it does not, the conjunction fails — dropping per the pre-registered "solo fail is a safe drop" handling. Stage 3 not started. Full write-up in `docs/experiments.md` (#27 stage 2 entry), commit ebb4a9e.

The `renderedFrameCount`-vs-`effective_render_fps` contradiction looks worth a specialist look before any retry of this mechanism design.

Lead finding, 2026-09-24 (on stage 2, ebb4a9e): the pre-registered NO-GO stands as recorded. But the evidence is contradictory, not null: fps went from 122.3 to 254.7, which is above the 120 Hz vsync ceiling the default build is bound by. That suggests presents are being skipped, while the renderprobe renderedFrameCount shows R≈F. Also, effective_render_fps=240/16 is computed from the setting, so it is not independent corroboration. Next step: a desk-only specialist check of which probe is trustworthy, and whether the 557 'permitted lifetime of 4 frames' warnings in B2 signal a behaviour change. Any retry gets a fresh pre-registration. Evidence: scratchpad render-off-B2-logcat.txt, state/records/render-off-20260924/.

Lead finding, 2026-09-24 (specialist desk check; details in the session scratchpad render-off-probe-analysis.md):
- Frames are skipped, so the stage-2 NO-GO was caused by a faulty measurement, not a failed mechanism.
- renderedFrameCount is undocumented and counts player-loop frames, so R≈F is expected whether or not frames are skipped.
- B and B2 are separate runs, and both are 2.1× the 120 Hz vsync ceiling that fps had tracked to within 2%.
- effective_render_fps is computed from the settings, not measured.
- The 557 lifetime warnings all come before the first advance (a known Unity issue when the interval is ≥4).
Plan change: after the #59 recording, run a pre-registered fleet equivalence stage using sequential A-B-A arms via TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR, so no runtime per-instance command is needed. It will use a SurfaceFlinger present-gap probe in place of renderprobe. The fidelity risk to watch is Canvas/UI updates gated by rendering for up to 15 frames.

Stage 3 (fleet equivalence, render-interval-16) done. 7 actors, scripted, A1/B/A2, frame_game_ms 100.

n: A1 28/28 valid, B 24/24 valid (6/7 actors — emulator-5558 lost to a known, previously-documented `RunPortError: the instance did not reach an active run`, not the #59 pattern; n still clears the ≥23 floor), A2 28/28 valid.

**Gate (a) fidelity**: final-wave 95% CI (B − pooled A) = −0.048 [−0.143, +0.071], inside ±0.5. decisions/wave diff 0.036. advances_cut_short: B lower than A. Zero invalid episodes anywhere. A1-vs-A2 drift on final wave: −0.036 [−0.179, +0.107], no baseline drift. The one literal failure — per-wave game_ms ±100ms margin (B−pooledA = 422ms) — is shown non-discriminating: A1-vs-A2 (same build) differs by 181ms against a ~7000ms per-wave SD, so the margin itself doesn't separate signal from same-build noise. Flagged as a pre-registration defect, not overridden.

**Gate (b) skip probe**: `dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --latency` on the BLAST layer returned no frame rows on either B or A2 — reproduces M1B-E053's own prior finding in this project (2026-09-17). No reading obtained either way.

**Gate (c) speed**: B's per-actor steady-state collection rate is 1.92× pooled A's (20.92 vs 10.88 game-s/wall-s), clearing the 1.3× bar comfortably.

Verdict recorded as: every discriminating criterion supports ADOPT, but not declared an automatic ADOPT since gate (a) as literally pre-registered didn't hold in full (the miscalibrated game_ms sub-condition) — left for the Lead's call, same shape M2-S001 used for its own miscalibrated bar. Full write-up + numbers: docs/experiments.md (#27 stage 3 entry), commit e101b77 (also corrects the stage-2 NO-GO attribution per the specialist's instrument finding, commit 3512095).

Host verified clean after every stage (no qemu, no adb device).

Lead decision, 2026-09-24 (on stage 3, e101b77): ADOPT render-interval-16 for TRAINING collection only.
- Fidelity passes on the arbiter: final wave B−A is −0.048 [−0.143, +0.071], inside ±0.5, and decisions/wave, advances_cut_short and validity also pass. The per-wave game_ms ±100 ms margin cannot be met at this n: A1 vs A2 alone differ by 181 ms, against a per-wave SD of about 7000 ms. So that result is not evidence of a difference; it is a defect in the pre-registration.
- The skip probe gave no reading (a repeat of M1B-E053). The mechanism therefore rests on fps at 2.1× the vsync ceiling (solo) and 1.92× per-actor collection (fleet), not on a probe.
- Mitigation: arm EVALUATION stays on the default build, so benchmark numbers stay like-for-like with run 4 and the baselines. Spectate never uses this build.
- Reversible: the build is selected per stage with TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR.

Lead decision recorded in docs/experiments.md and docs/solution.md (commit 6683750): ADOPT render-interval-16 for training collection only; evaluation and spectate stay on the default build; reversible per stage via TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR.

This issue's body also asked for a halved-guest-resolution arm as part of Experiment A (baseline vs halved resolution vs camera-rendering-disabled) — only the render-elimination mechanism (camera-rendering-disabled, via render-interval-16) was built and evaluated in stages 1–3. The guest-resolution halving arm was never run and remains unevaluated. Leaving this issue open (Refs #27, not closing) until that's addressed or explicitly dropped.

Lead, 2026-09-24: closing #27. Render elimination is delivered and adopted for training: e101b77 plus the decision in 6683750, with 1.92× per-actor collection in the fleet.
The halved-guest-resolution part is retired and was not evaluated. With 15 of every 16 frames no longer rendered, resolution only affects the remaining 1/16 of render work, so the most it could gain is too small to justify a device stage. It can be reopened if a future profile shows rendering dominating again.

items.title: Milestone 2: evaluation protocol — checkpoint arms in the fleet runner, numbered checkpoints, IQM with stratified bootstrap, post-hoc two-stage selection
items.body:
Milestone 2 benchmarks one model, `stacked-dqn`, against random and scripted under one protocol. The pieces that do not exist yet:

- **Numbered checkpoints.** During training, a checkpoint every K decisions: `checkpoint-<decisions>.pt` with `CheckpointIdentity`, beside the existing `latest.pt`. K is a `train.py` argument `--checkpoint-every-decisions`, required to be a multiple of `--block-decisions`.
- **Any checkpoint is an arm in the fleet runner.** `scripts/run_episodes.py` / `scripts/run_actors.py` take a policy selector: the existing names (`scripted`, `random`, `wait`) plus `checkpoint:<path>`. A checkpoint policy is greedy (epsilon 0), built from the checkpoint's own resolved config, on CPU, torch threads bounded. Every actor record and the fleet report carry the policy identity.
- **Statistics.** `experiment/comparison.py` gains `iqm(values)` and `stratified_bootstrap(strata, statistic, resamples, seed)` returning a point estimate and a 95% percentile interval, resampling within each stratum. `rliable` is not added as a dependency; the estimator is the one from Agarwal et al. 2021.
- **Post-hoc two-stage selection.** `scripts/select_checkpoint.py` reads one evaluation directory per checkpoint and names the selection by the highest IQM (set A). `scripts/report_arms.py` takes named arm directories and prints IQM with intervals per arm, pairwise bootstrap differences, and the per-wave comparison (set B). Nothing decides a verdict; it prints intervals.
- **Cleanup in passing.** The single-element `"arms"` list in `train_session` is a vestige of a retired multi-arm comparison; the session report names one arm.

comments.text:
Merged at 99ddb95 (eval protocol) + 17ee391 (M2-P001).
`train.py --actors 7 --budget-decisions 1000000 --checkpoint-every-decisions 100000`
`run_actors.py --actors 7 --episodes 2 --policy checkpoint:<path>` per candidate (set A)
`select_checkpoint.py <run> <eval-dirs...>` writes `<run>/selection.json`
`run_actors.py --episodes 9 --policy checkpoint:<selected>` (+ scripted/random) then `report_arms.py <arms...> --mlflow-run <id> --selection <run>/selection.json`
Per-episode metrics now land in MLflow; M2-P001 records the pre-registered protocol before any run started.

items.title: Milestone 2: walking skeleton run (M2-P001 small budget)
items.body:
Device stage: the whole Milestone 2 pipeline end to end at the small budget pre-registered in `docs/experiments.md` `## M2-P001` ("Skeleton first").

Stages: MLflow UI up; `train.py --actors 7 --budget-decisions 100000 --checkpoint-every-decisions 25000 --renderer host`; set A greedy evaluation of the four numbered checkpoints (`--episodes 1`) and `select_checkpoint.py`; set B (`--episodes 2`) for the selected checkpoint and random, then `report_arms.py`.

Purpose is to prove the pipeline and the per-episode MLflow view end to end. Its numbers are not evidence about the model (M2-P001). The developer's approval of the ~7 h budgeted run is contingent on this passing.

Worked from `main` at `ef053ac`; no code changes on the device.

comments.text:
Stage 0 done — MLflow UI is up at <http://127.0.0.1:5000> (HTTP 200), backend store `sqlite:///~/.local/state/tower-rl/mlflow.db`, which is the URI `train.py` resolves from the default `--run-dir ~/.local/state/tower-rl/runs` (`experiment/tracking.py:tracking_uri`). Pre-flight clean: zero qemu processes, `adb devices` empty, `bridge/current` resolves and hashes to `7a98f50b…f99a`.

One deviation forced by the script, before any device work: the pre-registered skeleton's `--checkpoint-every-decisions 25000` is not a multiple of the default `--block-decisions 2000`, so `train.py` refuses it by name. Stage 1 therefore adds `--block-decisions 2500` (the divisor of 25000 nearest the default). It changes only how often the collection loop checks the budget; the 1,000,000-decision run at period 100,000 is unaffected, since that is a whole number of 2,000-decision blocks.

Stage 1 started 17:48:33Z — `uv run --extra tracking python scripts/train.py --actors 7 --budget-decisions 100000 --block-decisions 2500 --checkpoint-every-decisions 25000 --renderer host`. Fleet bring-up is cold under `-gpu host` by design. Expected ≈45 min.

Stage 1 in progress, and it has produced its discriminating signal — one positive, one blocking.

**Fleet: 7/7.** All seven instances (5556-5568, never 5554, never the canonical AVD) report `is at home and offline` and `deployed bridge confirmed 7a98f50b…f99a` — 7 of 7 each. Bring-up took about 5 min, cold under `-gpu host` as designed.

**Positive: the per-episode MLflow view works.** MLflow run `a6f3716dd56c4a34b16ee792fb8527ba` (`stacked-dqn-20260918-195301-dde9c7`), read through the client, carries `episode_final_wave`, `episode_decisions`, `episode_game_ms`, `episode_wait_fraction`, `episode_purchases`, `episode_valid`, `episode_actor`, `episode_epsilon` — every one at count 44, equal to the 44 episodes collected — plus `learner_importance_beta`/`learner_optimisation_steps` and the 17-series 30 s decision-time breakdown.

**Blocking: throughput is about 4x below what M2-P001 budgeted, and one cause is a defect in `train.py`.**

1. `train.py` never calls `raise_frame_rate`. Only `run_actors.py` and `clone_session.py` do, so the *training* fleet collects with SurfaceFlinger's stock per-uid game default override of 60 Hz standing over a 120 Hz display. Read off instance 5556 mid-run: `activeMode=… vsyncRate=120.00 Hz` but `GameFrameRateOverrides … {10218, 0 60}`. This is exactly the silent failure `confirm_frame_rate`'s own docstring describes. Raising all seven to 120 by hand (`raise_frame_rate`, 7/7 `confirmed at 120 Hz` on all three readings) roughly doubled collection: bridge round trip 1,400 ms/decision to 730 ms, 2,500 to ~5,000 decisions/hour per actor. No code was changed on the device; the fix is the Lead's to make.
2. Even at 120 Hz the fleet collects ~30,000 decisions/hour aggregate, against the 129,000-143,000 M2-P001 took from `M1B-E052`. That figure is a *scripted* measurement. Under the learned policy `episode_wait_fraction` is ~0.80, so most decisions advance the world a long way and cost far more wall clock per decision. The scripted throughput does not transfer to a training arm.

Consequence: the 100,000-decision skeleton is ~3.3 h, not the ~45 min expected, and the pre-registered 1,000,000-decision run would be ~33 h, not ~7 h. That is a budget decision, not an implementation choice, so device work is paused for the Lead rather than run out to 100,000 unattended.

Stage 1 ended (option B, per the Lead): stopped at the first numbered checkpoint instead of running the full 100,000.

- Wall: 67 min of process, 60.6 min of tracked run (19:53:02–20:53:38 local); fleet bring-up about 5 min of it, cold under `-gpu host`.
- Collected 25,184 decisions in 247 episodes, **246 valid / 1 invalid** (the invalid one is the episode the interrupt landed in). All seven actor indices 0-6 appear in `episode_actor`. Learner took 5,193 optimisation steps. Mean final wave 4.6 at epsilon annealing to 0.05.
- End-to-end ~24,900 decisions/hour, of which the first ~22 min ran at 60 Hz before the override was raised by hand at about 5,000 decisions.
- `checkpoint-0025184.pt` and its `.sha256` written beside `latest.pt`. Interrupting before the budget means the session report, the arm summary and the post-budget evaluation were not written — the run directory holds `checkpoints/` and `manifest.json` only.
- **The MLflow run ended `FINISHED`, not `RUNNING` or `FAILED`**: `train.py`'s `finally` finished the tracked run through the `KeyboardInterrupt`. Final metric counts: every `episode_*` series at 247, equal to the episodes collected; `learner_optimisation_steps`/`learner_importance_beta` at 247 and `learner_gradient_norm`, `learner_weighted_loss`, `learner_unweighted_mean_absolute_td_error`, `learner_value_fit_correlation` at 202 (they start once warm-up passes).
- Teardown 7/7 on every line: `libunity_sha256 ffc1f3ef…dd0040`, `versionCode=1199`, `versionName=29.0.3`, `installerPackageName=com.android.vending`, `libunity_mounts: 0`, `bridge_artifacts: removed`, `game_frame_rate_override: reset`. Then zero qemu in `/proc/*/exe` and `adb devices` empty.

The frame-rate defect is filed as #30 (board, Status Next).

Stage 2 starting — set A, the one checkpoint, `--episodes 1` on 7 actors.

Stage 2 done — set A and selection.

Set A: `run_actors.py --actors 7 --episodes 1 --policy checkpoint:…/checkpoint-0025184.pt --renderer host --frame-rate-hz 120`, about 12 min including bring-up. **7/7 instances, 7 episodes, 7 valid, 0 invalid**, `advances_cut_short` 0 and `episodes_not_started_fresh` 0 on every record, and 7/7 `confirmed at 120 Hz` on all three SurfaceFlinger readings — which is the contrast with #30: the evaluation runner raises the rate, the training runner does not. Per-instance final waves 1-9, ~23 decisions/wave, speed-up ~2.0.

Selection (one candidate, because the run was stopped at the first checkpoint):

    1 checkpoints of stacked-dqn-20260918-195301-dde9c7
    final_wave:
      checkpoint-0025184.pt        IQM   6.00  [  6.00,   6.00]  n=7
    decisions:
      checkpoint-0025184.pt        IQM 133.80  [133.80, 133.80]  n=7
    selected …/checkpoints/checkpoint-0025184.pt
      logged to tracked run a6f3716dd56c4a34b16ee792fb8527ba

`selection.json` written beside the run, carrying `checkpoint_identity 22867a9ca26e` and `decisions 25184`. With one candidate the interval is degenerate; the mechanism is what this proves, not the number. Teardown 7/7 on every line, zero qemu, `adb devices` empty.

Stage 3 starting — set B, `--episodes 2` for the selected checkpoint and for random, each on its own fleet. Scripted is skipped in the skeleton, as M2-P001 specifies.

Stage 3 done — set B and the report. Scripted is skipped in the skeleton, as M2-P001 specifies; the arms are the selected checkpoint and random.

Two fleets, each brought up and torn down on its own: `stacked-dqn` 21:14-21:22 (8.4 min), `random` 21:31-21:41 (10 min), `--actors 7 --episodes 2 --renderer host --frame-rate-hz 120`. **14/14 valid in each arm, 0 invalid.** 7/7 `confirmed at 120 Hz`, 7/7 bridge digest, and 7/7 on every cleanup line in both, with zero qemu and an empty `adb devices` after each.

`report_arms.py random=… stacked-dqn=… --selection …/selection.json --mlflow-run a6f3716d…` accepted set B against the selection (it did not refuse the arm) and printed:

    final_wave:
      random                       IQM   5.88  [  4.75,   7.00]  n=14
      stacked-dqn                  IQM   6.38  [  5.12,   7.25]  n=14
    pairwise difference in mean final wave:
      random 5.71 vs stacked-dqn 6.21: difference -0.50 [-2.36, +1.36] d=-0.19 n=14/14 — indistinguishable

with the per-wave comparison over `game_ms`, `decisions`, `health_fraction` and `cash_log` for 8 wave indices, and `logged to tracked run a6f3716d…`. **These numbers are pipeline evidence, not model evidence** — one checkpoint at 25,184 decisions, 14 episodes an arm, no scripted arm.

MLflow post-hoc series confirmed through the client, not the UI: `greedy_final_wave_iqm`/`_ci_low`/`_ci_high` = 6.00 at **step 25184**, the checkpoint's own decision count, and `report_random_final_wave_iqm` 5.875 and `report_stacked-dqn_final_wave_iqm` 6.375 with their intervals at **step 0**.

**The pipeline passes end to end** — train → numbered checkpoint → set A → selection → set B → report, with MLflow carrying the live per-episode view and both post-hoc curves. What does not stand is M2-P001's wall-clock budget; see the earlier comment and #30.

Recorded as `## M2-E001 — Walking skeleton: the pipeline runs end to end; the wall-clock budget does not`, committed on branch `m2-e001-skeleton` at **2189763**, off `ef053ac` in a worktree of its own (nothing committed in the main checkout, which has since moved to `215c4c6`).

Stage wall times: MLflow 1 min; training 65 min (19:48-20:53, 4.5 min of it bring-up); set A 7 min plus an instant selection; set B 8.4 + 10 min plus an instant report. Four fleet stages, four clean teardowns, zero qemu and an empty `adb devices` after each. The MLflow UI is **left running** at <http://127.0.0.1:5000> against `sqlite:///~/.local/state/tower-rl/mlflow.db`, training run `a6f3716dd56c4a34b16ee792fb8527ba`.

The device stage overran its 90-minute timebox (about 121 min from first launch), on the Lead's decision to continue to the first checkpoint rather than stop at the throughput finding.

Merged at 08bdd40 (M2-E001, docs/experiments.md); correction commit 3c494b7.

Pipeline passed end to end: train → checkpoint → set A → selection → set B → report, MLflow per-episode view intact, fleet 7/7 up and clean down x4.

Findings: (1) train.py never raised the guest frame rate (#30, fixed in 215c4c6); (2) learned-policy throughput ~28-30k decisions/hour vs the 129-143k scripted premise M2-P001 used.

Re-priced budgeted run approved by developer 2026-09-18: --budget-decisions 200000 --checkpoint-every-decisions 50000 (~7h).

items.title: train.py never raises the guest frame rate; compose simulation.frame_rate.raise_frame_rate/confirm_frame_rate after bring-up as run_actors.py does
items.body:
`scripts/train.py` brings a fleet up and collects without ever raising SurfaceFlinger's per-uid game frame-rate override. `raise_frame_rate` has exactly two callers, `scripts/run_actors.py:353` and `scripts/clone_session.py:189`; the training path has none. Every measured-throughput runner therefore confirms 120 Hz per instance and the *training* runner silently collects at the stock 60 Hz.

Evidence, from the M2 skeleton run (#29, MLflow run `a6f3716dd56c4a34b16ee792fb8527ba`), read off live instance 5556 mid-run:

    activeMode={id=0, … vsyncRate=120.00 Hz …}
    GameFrameRateOverrides=
      (uid, gameModeOverride, gameDefaultOverride)={10218, 0 60}

The display was at 120 (`-vsync-rate` is set by `instance.start`); the game surface was at 60. Raising all seven by hand with `raise_frame_rate` produced 7/7 `confirmed at 120 Hz: display vsync mode 120.00, uid 10218 game mode override 120, uid 10218 applied frame rate 120.00` and roughly doubled collection: bridge round trip 1,400 ms/decision to 730 ms, ~2,500 to ~5,000 decisions/hour per actor.

This is the failure `confirm_frame_rate`'s own docstring names: "a run that quietly collected at 60 would look exactly like one that collected at 240 except in its throughput". Every training run before this one is affected, and no log line in the training path said so.

Fix: raise and confirm the rate per instance after each bring-up in the training path, the way `run_actors.collect_episodes` does, so a training fleet fails by name rather than collecting at half speed. `instrumented_bridge.sh cleanup` already resets the override at teardown, so nothing new is left on the guest.

comments.text:
Merged at 215c4c6.
Call order: bring_up → require_offline → require_game_activity → raise_frame_rate → connect.
Device confirmation expected as `confirmed at 120 Hz` on all instances at the next training bring-up.

items.title: Milestone 2: budgeted training run, 200k decisions (M2-P001 corrected, developer-approved 2026-09-18)

The developer-approved budgeted Milestone 2 training run, at the throughput
re-priced in `M2-P001`'s 2026-09-18 correction after `M2-E001` refuted the
original (scripted-policy) premise.

**Command**

      --actors 7 --budget-decisions 200000 \

items.title: Training resumes from a checkpoint: optimizer state, schedule position, decision counter; replay re-warmed from the loaded policy
items.body:
A numbered checkpoint today holds network weights and CheckpointIdentity only; train.py always starts fresh.

Done-condition: `train.py --resume <checkpoint>` continues a run's decision budget from the checkpoint's decisions with the optimizer state, epsilon/beta schedule position, and numbered-checkpoint cadence restored, and the replay buffer refilled by a warm-up phase under the loaded policy before learning restarts (replay is not persisted; 4,290 sequences at M2 run 1). The MLflow run continues under the same run id (open_run) so the curve is one series; resolved_config records the parent checkpoint.

Motivation: M2 run 1 (issue #31; 200,174 decisions, 4 checkpoints under ~/.local/state/tower-rl/runs/session-20260918-215839/) should be the first segment of a longer run rather than a throwaway.

Known hazard: TrainingReport.decisions_logged must be restored along with report.decisions (comment in experiment/training_report.py).

Evidence pointers: M2-E001, M2-P001 correction block, M2-E002 when it lands.

comments.text:
Starting work (implementer-resume-training, worktree at 50fae46).

Scope: `train.py --resume <checkpoint.pt>` continues a run's decision budget from the checkpoint — optimizer state, schedule position, decision counter, numbered-checkpoint cadence — with the replay buffer re-warmed under the loaded policy, the MLflow run continued under its own run id, and `resolved_config.parent_checkpoint` naming the parent.

One correction to the issue body up front, from reading a run-1 checkpoint (`session-20260918-215839/.../latest.pt`): a numbered checkpoint already carries more than weights and identity. `backbone_state` is `StackedDqnBackbone.state_dict()`, which holds `online`, `target`, `optimizer` (29 stepped parameter states) and `steps`, and `progress` holds `optimisation_steps`, `environment_decisions`, `episodes`, `epsilon` and `importance_beta`. So run 1's checkpoints are resumable with their optimizer moments intact; the only field a resume needs that they lack is the MLflow run id. That is what the format gains, and `load` is widened to accept the old version so run 1 can be continued.

Review of 6d40a11 found five corrections, being made on the same branch before merge.

1. `collection_windows` restarts its `spent` accumulator at zero on a resumed segment, so window metrics land on the parent's tracked run at segment-relative decision keys (a 200->400 split logged its first window at decisions=219). Windows will be cut from the resume point, off the same restored offset the episode axis uses.
2. `TrainingReport.summary` divides restored cumulative counters by the segment's own wall clock, inflating `decisions_per_hour` (6.1M vs 1.78M at comparable wall time). Rates will describe the segment alone; wall time stays unrestored.
3. `resume_point` passes no expected identity to `resume_state`, so `CheckpointIdentity.incompatibilities` never ran and a checkpoint from another profile or schema resumed silently. It will be checked before any device work.
4. The optimizer-absent branch is retracted: optimizer state has been in every checkpoint since aed3cb9, so a file lacking it is truncated and must raise rather than resume on fresh moments. The branch, its flag, its notice and its test come out.
5. `TrainingProgress`'s docstring overstates what is restored - epsilon and beta are derived from the decision counter, and the stored values are informational.

items.title: Plasticity diagnostic across run-1 checkpoints decides whether a reset A/B is worth running
items.body:
## Objective

Run 1 (M2-E002 in `docs/experiments.md`) showed greedy final-wave IQM roughly flat across the
50k/100k/150k/200k checkpoints, with 50k selected. One hypothesis is plasticity loss / primacy
bias (Nikishin et al. 2022; Sokar et al. 2023). Before designing a reset A/B around that
hypothesis, measure its signature offline on the four checkpoints that already exist — minutes of
CPU, zero device time.

`scripts/diagnose_plasticity.py` reports, per checkpoint:

- (a) tau-dormant fraction (Sokar 2023: `s_i = E|h_i| / mean_k E|h_k|` over a fixed observation
  batch; dormant if `s_i <= tau`), at tau = 0.025 and tau = 0.1, on the post-activation outputs of
  `trunk.row_encoder`, `trunk.scalar_encoder` and `core` of `StackedPolicyNetwork`;
- (b) stable rank of the pooled feature matrix (`||F||_F^2 / ||F||_2^2`) and srank at 99% explained
  variance (Kumar et al. 2021) on the `core` output;
- (c) L2 norm of every parameter tensor, plus the total (needs no observations).

Phase 2 captures ~500–1000 real observations from a short device session under the 50k checkpoint
policy; the capture seam is decided by the Lead before it is built.

## Done condition

A `docs/experiments.md` entry carrying the three curves (dormancy, rank, norm) across the four
checkpoints and a stated verdict: plasticity-loss signature **present / absent / inconclusive**.
The entry decides whether the reset A/B is worth its device time.

## Evidence pointers

- Checkpoints: `~/.local/state/tower-rl/runs/session-20260918-215839/stacked-dqn-20260918-215839-e3c6ba/checkpoints/checkpoint-00{50123,100080,150002,200174}.pt`
- Source values and extended reasoning (incl. "Why the offline diagnostic comes first"):
  `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-furkan-Documents-tower-rl/a97626b0-c8ec-4ea6-896e-512eb8c8716d/scratchpad/PRIMACY-BIAS-AB.md`

comments.text:
Phase 2 blocked before the verdict: the device stage cannot produce a durable batch.

The capture seam is built and unit-tested (`run_episodes.py --record-observations`, tip `12df2cb`). Two device attempts, both ending clean (bridge cleanup + emulator killed, zero qemu, empty `adb devices`):

1. run 1 brought the clone up at 120 Hz and tore down correctly; `run_episodes.py` then failed writing the batch — `~/.local/state/tower-rl/m2-run1/plasticity` did not exist.
2. run 2 refused before touching the device: `no checkpoint at .../checkpoint-0050123.pt`.

`~/.local/state/tower-rl` now holds only the directory I created at 10:36 — no `runs/`, no `bridge/`. The same paths listed, loaded and deployed successfully earlier in this session, so this shell and the earlier one do not see the same filesystem. No verdict is possible until the run-1 artifacts are reachable; the phase-1 norm table stands but its JSON is gone with them.

Blocked: run-1 artifacts under `~/.local/state/tower-rl` deleted between 10:12 and 10:36 on 2026-09-19; forensics in progress; capture cannot run until a checkpoint exists.

Dependency: a reachable `checkpoint-0050123.pt` (or a replacement run). The capture seam and the diagnostic are built and green at `12df2cb`; nothing else here is waiting on code.
Unblocked: `~/.local/state/tower-rl` was in Trash and has been restored in place (checkpoint-0050123.pt matches its .sha256; runs/, bridge/current, m2-run1/ present). Resuming the device capture.

Verdict: the plasticity-loss signature is **absent** across the four run-1 checkpoints. A reset A/B has no support from this evidence.

Against a rule written before the numbers (present: dormancy +10 points or stable rank -25%; absent: dormancy within 3 points and rank within 10%):
- tau-dormant fraction **0.000** at tau=0.025 and 0.1, all three layers, all four checkpoints - with headroom, the quietest unit scoring 0.22-0.57 of its layer mean.
- core stable rank **1.097 -> 1.179** (rises), srank_99 98 -> 104 of 128.
- ||theta|| 48.965 -> 49.681 (+1.5%); trained tensors grow ~15%, the identity embedding that carries most of the total falls.

Batch: 800 observations, 8/8 valid greedy episodes of checkpoint-0050123 (identity 8344a482eede), 1,141 decisions at 120 Hz. Entry M2-E004 in docs/experiments.md at `1fb91d5`; JSON under ~/.local/state/tower-rl/m2-run1/plasticity/.

items.title: Per-actor exploration ladder (Ape-X) selectable in train.py, collection metrics split by actor, M2-P002 pre-registered
items.body:
## Why

The learning-signal analysis of run 1 (MLflow run `90d08dac383d4f7d9f48f1a8ca43c189`,
M2-E002/M2-E004) found that the run's binding constraint is exploration, not
replay ratio, reward density or plasticity:

- over 800 real greedy states, **68.3% of decisions are WAIT-only (forced)**;
  the mean valid-set size is 2.03 and only 7 of the 61 `RUN_ACTIONS` are ever valid;
- at the uniform floor epsilon = 0.05 the exploratory action is drawn from the
  valid set, so a choice state deviates with probability 0.76 * epsilon: about
  **1.7 exploratory buys per episode, ~2,300 in the whole 190k post-anneal span**,
  each replayed ~91 times. By the binomial, roughly one episode in the run
  deviated 8+ times - essentially no alternative build order was ever played;
- policy improvement stopped at ~25-27k decisions: after 50k the collection
  curve is statistically indistinguishable from a constant, and
  `learner_value_fit_correlation` drifts *downward*.

Ape-X (Horgan et al. 2018, arXiv:1803.00933) gives each actor i of N a fixed
epsilon_i = 0.4^(1 + 7 i/(N-1)), so a 7-actor fleet spans 0.4 down to 0.00066
and the near-greedy actors still report a readable on-policy curve.

## Done condition

1. `train.py --exploration {uniform,ladder}`, default `uniform` byte-for-byte
   identical to run 1's schedule (regression test), the ladder modelled as a
   domain concept in `learning` and recorded in `resolved_config`; `--resume`
   from run 1's checkpoints works with `--exploration ladder`.
2. Collection windows keep the pooled series and add per-actor mean final wave
   plus a pooled near-greedy series the M2-P002 readout can cite.
3. `M2-P002` pre-registered in `docs/experiments.md` on `main` before any run:
   50k-decision continuation from `checkpoint-0200174.pt` with the ladder, with
   gating thresholds, and the conditional run 2.

No device time is spent under this item; the run itself needs the developer's
approval.

comments.text:
Scope change from the Lead: requirement 3 (the M2-P002 pre-registration) is dropped from this item. The developer approved a change to the decision unit - decide only at choice points - which makes a continuation gate from run 1's checkpoints invalid; the run spec follows that change.
No pre-registration was ever drafted or committed here. Requirements 1, 2 and 4 are unchanged and implemented in 8ed8f7d.
Note on the composition: an actor acts at max(annealed, ladder_i), and the anneal holds at --epsilon-end (0.05), so with run 1's defaults rungs 2-6 of a 7-actor ladder are clipped to 0.05; only --epsilon-end below 0.00066 gives the unclipped ladder.

Correction to my note above, per the Lead: the ladder does not compose with the anneal by max. Each actor anneals linearly from --epsilon-start to its own rung over --epsilon-anneal-decisions and is held there, so a 7-actor fleet reads {0.400, 0.137, 0.047, 0.016, 0.0056, 0.0019, 0.00066} from the end of the anneal on, and no rung is clipped.
--epsilon-end is the uniform schedule's floor only; passing it with --exploration ladder is refused rather than silently ignored. Uniform is unchanged and still pinned against run 1's arithmetic.
Implemented in 27867ff; pytest 611 passed, ruff and mypy clean.

Merged: 6dca4c6dd5fca1293f4443cf81ab3c95525782e8
Gate: pytest 614 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean (all exit 0)
Note: the M2-P002 pre-registration named in the issue title was descoped from this work (see prior comment on #37); pre-registration follows in the run-spec item.

items.title: The environment asks for a decision only at choice points: forced WAIT slices are advanced through, reward and game time accrue to the surrounding decision
items.body:
Run 1's decisions were mostly not decisions. Across 800 real observations from
the M2-E004 checkpoint batch, 68% of the states the agent was asked about had
WAIT as the only legal action: no purchase was affordable, so the only
available action was the one the environment would have taken anyway. That
dilutes n-step returns with forced no-ops and spends exploration on states
where exploration cannot choose anything.

Objective: the environment asks for a decision only at choice points. A choice
point is an observation whose legal set contains at least one purchase. Forced
WAIT slices are advanced through inside `InstrumentedRunEnvironment.step` (and
inside the reset that produces the first observation); reward and game time
accrue to the surrounding decision. Each internal advance keeps the normal
cadence, the normal bridge/host divergence check and the normal wave and
episode tallies - only the *decision* is withheld. The bridge, the fake port,
`CadenceConfig` and `DecisionEvent` are unchanged.

The old behaviour stays selectable as a named policy (`--decision-cadence
every-slice`) for one purpose: reproducing run 1's protocol. It is recorded in
`resolved_config`, in evaluation records and in `CheckpointIdentity`, so a
run-1 checkpoint refuses to be resumed or evaluated under choice points.

Done-condition: `InstrumentedRunEnvironment` emits one transition per choice
point with measured `advances` and `game_ms` for the span it covers; reward
over the span is the wave difference across the whole span; a run ending inside
a span terminates that transition with the accrued reward; `EpisodeSummary`
counts choice points as `decisions` and internal advances as `advances`;
`--decision-cadence {choice-points,every-slice}` (default `choice-points`) is
threaded through `train.py`, `run_actors.py`, `run_episodes.py` and
`spectate.py` and recorded; `CheckpointIdentity` refuses a cross-cadence resume
by name, legacy checkpoints reading as `every-slice`; tests on the fake port
cover the skipped WAIT-only slices, the two-wave broke span's reward, a
termination inside a span, `every-slice` reproducing today's behaviour, the
spectate panel's held game time and the identity refusal;
`docs/environment-contract.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and a new ADR
`docs/adr/0009-decisions-at-choice-points.md` state the contract.

Out of scope: the game-time budget unit, learning-side units, the bridge.

Evidence: M2-E004 observation batch (800 states, run 1 checkpoints).

comments.text:
Review fixes, on `7981379` (rebased onto main 6dca4c6, no conflicts, gate green).

Run 1 hashes to `8344a482eede` again, as `selection.json` cites it; pinned by test. Cross-cadence use is refused by `incompatibilities`, unchanged.

items.title: Observation-v2: the agent observes everything the player sees — tower stats, wave and enemy state, economy, raw upgrade levels, unclipped affordability, round clock; slot labels for humans
items.body:
Developer decision: the agent must observe everything the player sees on the run
screen. `observation-v1` shows the policy only wave, cash, health and a clipped
per-slot cost ratio; the HUD carries far more, and the bridge can read it.

## Done-condition

`observation-v2` replaces v1 end to end: the production bridge reads the tower
stats, wave/enemy state, economy and round clock by name; the Python adapter
parses and range-checks them; `SCALAR_FEATURES`/`ROW_FEATURES` carry them with a
documented per-field transform; the network's input widths derive from those
constants; `CheckpointIdentity` refuses a v1 checkpoint by name; the spectate
panel shows the new block and the per-slot labels; contract, architecture and an
ADR describe what exists.

Raw upgrade `level`/`max_level` are exposed as integers and affordability becomes
unclipped `log1p(cash/cost)`. The `String[]` slot names/descriptions are read once
per session and exposed as labels for `RUN_ACTIONS` — for humans (spectate panel,
evaluation/session records), never in the observation tensor.

Out of scope, deliberately: boss health bar and per-enemy objects (object-graph
reads), and the upgrade "current -> next" preview (not stored as a pair).

## Evidence

Session scratchpad, from #39 and the observation-gap scout:
`OBSERVATION-GAP.md` (what v1 drops and why it matters),
`FIELD-ENUMERATION.md` (920 `Main` fields by name and declared IL2CPP type),
`FIELD-SAMPLES.md` (138 snapshots of observed values and ranges over one episode:
`criticalChance` is percent, `closestEnemyDistance` has a 10000 no-enemy sentinel,
`towerHealth` goes negative on the killing blow).

Value verification against the HUD in spectate is a device stage; the item stays
open until that measurement exists.

items.title: Training budget and checkpoint cadence are expressed in game time, not decisions
items.body:
M2-P001's correction block and ADR 0009 name decisions as a variable-cost unit — a decision now spans a variable slice of game time; game time is the scarce resource the device sells.

Done-condition: the training budget and the numbered-checkpoint cadence are counted in cumulative game seconds across the fleet.

- `--budget-game-seconds` replaces `--budget-decisions`; `--checkpoint-every-game-seconds` replaces `--checkpoint-every-decisions`; numbered checkpoints are named `checkpoint-gs<seconds, 7 digits>.pt`.
- Budget accounting is at episode granularity: a run stops after the episode in which the budget is crossed, and the overshoot (<= one episode per actor) is recorded as `budget_overshoot_game_ms`.
- `environment_decisions` stays a counter (learning-side schedules remain in decisions); the checkpoint gains `environment_game_ms` at format version 3, and a resume from a version 1-2 file onto a game-time budget is refused by name.
- MLflow `step` stays decisions; `learner_game_seconds` and `episode_game_seconds_cumulative` make the curves readable in game time, and `greedy_final_wave_iqm` is logged on both axes.
- `select_checkpoint.py` orders candidates by the game seconds in the file name.

Evidence: the unit suite (budget crossing with overshoot, checkpoint per crossing across a resume split, refusal of format <= 2, select_checkpoint ordering, report fields), plus docs reconciled in `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/setup.md` and a dated note in M2-P001's correction block.

items.title: Training stops early when the near-greedy curve has not improved for two checkpoint periods
items.body:
Developer decision: a training run that has stopped improving should not burn the
rest of its game-time budget. The run watches its own near-greedy learning curve
and stops itself at a checkpoint crossing.

Rule (fixed):

- A *period* is the interval between consecutive numbered-checkpoint crossings
  (`--checkpoint-every-game-seconds`).
- At each crossing, compute the mean final wave of the **near-greedy** actors'
  valid episodes that ended within the period just closed (under uniform
  exploration: all actors).
- Track the best period mean so far. If the closed period's mean is below
  `best + min_improvement` for `patience` consecutive periods, the run stops
  after writing that crossing's checkpoint.
- The first period sets the baseline and cannot trigger a stop.
- A resumed run restores the tracker state from the checkpoint; a resume from a
  checkpoint written before this change starts the tracker fresh and says so in
  the report.

Flags: `--early-stop-patience-periods` (default 0 = off),
`--early-stop-min-improvement` (waves, default 0.2).

Done-condition:

- the two flags exist and are recorded as MLflow params in `resolved_config`;
- tests with the fake fleet cover: plateaued fleet stops after exactly `patience`
  non-improving periods, improving fleet runs to budget, patience 0 never stops,
  the first period cannot trigger, resume restores the tracker across a split;
- the report records `early_stopped`, the stopping period, the best period mean
  and the closing period's mean, and logs
  `checkpoint_period_near_greedy_mean_final_wave` at each crossing;
- `docs/architecture.md` section training describes the rule.
