items.title: M2-P002 run 2 executed: baselines, two seeds, evaluation, recordings, verdict (M2-E007)
items.body:
Execute Milestone 2 run 2 under the pre-registered protocol in `docs/experiments.md` `M2-P002` (option B, two seeds, sequential). The entry is authoritative; nothing here restates or amends it.

**Stages, per the `M2-P002` entry:**

1. **Baselines** — random and scripted arms, 7 instances, choice-point cadence, host renderer, 120 Hz, `--episodes 16` per instance (112 attempted an arm), collected *before* any training so they can set the kill threshold.
2. **Training** — one from-scratch `stacked-dqn` per seed (0 and 1), `--budget-game-seconds 360000`, `--block-game-seconds 4000`, `--checkpoint-every-game-seconds 60000`, `--epsilon-anneal-decisions 2500`, ε ladder, early stopping (`--early-stop-patience-periods 2 --early-stop-min-improvement 0.2`); kill criterion checked once, after the anneal.
3. **Evaluation** — the last numbered checkpoint of each seed, greedy, 112 attempted; `report_arms.py` over random, scripted and each model arm.
4. **Recordings** — one round to death per numbered checkpoint per seed, `spectate.py`, 60 Hz, lavapipe, under `state/recordings/`; not evidence for the verdict.
5. **Verdict** — pairwise IQM difference of final wave, (model − scripted) and (model − random), by `comparison.stratified_bootstrap_difference` with a 95% percentile interval, per seed; "reproducibly" only if a claim fires on both seeds. The reported outcome is one of the six `M2-P002` pre-declares.

**Done-condition:** `M2-E007` on `main` in `docs/experiments.md`, carrying the verdict — the claims made or refused, per seed, with the intervals they rest on, plus whichever of the kill criterion or the early stop fired. items.title: Rounds after the first in a session play behind the previous round's Game Stats overlay: determine whether game state differs and whether the bridge can dismiss it
items.body:
Developer observed it in `state/recordings/observation-v2-check-001.mp4`: the overlay from episode 1's death remains on screen while episode 2 plays beneath it.

Done-condition: a finding on game-state parity between episode 1 (overlay showing) and episode 2 (overlay present, round supposedly fresh) — i.e. whether `Main`'s round/game-state fields (`roundActiveBool`, `gameOverBool`, wave, health, etc.) are genuinely reset and the round is logically fresh despite the visible overlay — plus a recommended fix path (e.g. an additional lifecycle press, a diagnostics-build method enumeration to find a panel-close receiver, or confirmation this is purely cosmetic and out of scope).

comments.text: Investigation (no device, read-only): bridge restart path (tower_bridge.cpp:457-466, 1523-1535) presses `go_home` (Button_GameEndPanelGoHome on Main) then `start_round` (BattlePanelUI.StartNewRound on BattlePanel); both are confirmed via `round_active`/`game_over` on `Main`, which the M1B-E022 investigation already trusts for logical freshness. `Main`'s 920-field inventory (session scratchpad) has no result-panel-visibility field — only `gameEndKilledByInt`, `GameOverEvent`, `gameOverBool`/`roundActiveBool`; the panel's own shown/hidden state lives on an unenumerated UI class, not Main. No doc (solution.md, environment-contract.md, ADR 5-8, M1B entries) mentions a lingering result screen — only settling-time and boundary-cost. Parity conclusion: game-logic state is likely fresh (fields reset, round active) but the panel's *visual* dismissal is not verified by any field the bridge reads — unknown, needs device. Recommended: on the resumed run, extract a frame from episode 2 in the recording to confirm hypothesis, then a diagnostics build enumerating the panel's own class for a close/animate-out method, or check whether go_home's confirmation only reads Main state while the panel plays its own close animation across frames the bridge steps past.
diagnostics prep (code only); device look scheduled between seeds

**Device procedure for the overlay look (~15 min, run between M2-P002 seeds — never while a run holds the emulator).**

Diagnostics build is prepared in code only (`TOWER_BRIDGE_DIAGNOSTICS`), not installed and not deployed: `state/bridge/current` stays at `662cba09…`. Digests of this source: diagnostics `299f1889d88decd007f0cc4571e77fa39b67041114c9e36d0fe73f1416aa4936`, production `06300dfd452fcd8f8405e09207a052e9e52e28e9eeebb143864889eb73878b1d` (worktree build path; a different path gives a different digest, per docs/setup.md).

Standing constraints: instrumented clone only (the script refuses the canonical AVD), clone offline (deploy refuses a routable interface), no device data into the repo, production `current` untouched — deploy via `TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR`.

Off the clock, on the host: configure `native/tower_bridge` with `-C state/bridge/config/profile.cmake … -DTOWER_BRIDGE_DIAGNOSTICS=ON` into `$build`, build, then `cp state/bridge/current/libunity-bridge.so "$build/"` — this CMakeLists does not produce the patched overlay.

1. Capture first: `adb -s $serial logcat -G 16M`, `logcat -c`, then `logcat -s tower_bridge > overlay-logcat-1.txt &`. The scans are verbose (`Panel` matches many methods) and would otherwise roll away.
2. `TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR="$build" scripts/instrumented_bridge.sh deploy $serial`.
3. Connect any host client (one `run_episodes.py` episode, or `spectate.py`): IL2CPP resolves and every scan runs on the **first client connection**, not at launch.
4. Read the capture: `classscan <Namespace.Class> mono|plain` (classes named `GameEnd|Stats|Result|Panel`, and whether `UnitySendMessage` can reach them at all); `scan <Class>.<Method>/<arity>` (now also `Panel Hide Close Dismiss Stats Result Animate Fade`) — a parameterless `mono` match is a pressable candidate; `icall UnityEngine.GameObject::…` and `invoke string_new=… method_from_name=… runtime_invoke=…` (presence only); `transition go_home frame=… us=… active=… wave=… health=… round_time=…`, one line per rendered frame for 2 s after the press.
5. Open the best candidates without a rebuild: push their bare names, whitespace-separated, to `/data/local/tmp/tower_bridge_classes.txt` (same push + `chcon u:object_r:apk_data_file:s0` + `chmod 0444` as #39's `tower_bridge_fields.txt`), `am force-stop` and relaunch the game, reconnect a client → `classlist <Name> mono|plain` plus a full field-and-method inventory per class.
6. Press a candidate with the overlay actually up (right after a death), via the diagnostics-only `send:<GameObject>:<Method>` lifecycle action. The host adapter rejects any action outside `LIFECYCLE_ACTIONS`, so use a raw socket client: length-prefixed `{"type":"command","protocol_version":2,"request_id":"probe1","expected_observation_sequence":<seq>,"kind":"lifecycle","action":"send:<Obj>:<Method>"}`. Screencap immediately before and ~2 s after; the `transition <Method> frame=…` lines cover that window. A control that hides a panel without changing the run reports `ambiguous`/`lifecycle_timeout` — that is not a failed press.
7. Cleanup, mandatory: `adb -s $serial shell su -c 'rm -f /data/local/tmp/tower_bridge_classes.txt /data/local/tmp/tower_bridge_fields.txt'` (the script does **not** remove these), then `scripts/instrumented_bridge.sh cleanup $serial`, then confirm `state/bridge/current` still resolves to `662cba09…` and nothing new was installed under `state/bridge/`. Kill the backgrounded logcat.

**What this cannot answer.** The bridge still cannot read the panel's own visibility: `Main` carries no such field, and a `GameObject.activeSelf`/`Behaviour.enabled` read would need `il2cpp_string_new` (name argument to `GameObject::Find`) plus `il2cpp_class_get_method_from_name`/`il2cpp_runtime_invoke`, on scene traversals Unity documents as main-thread-only — unlike the leaf `Time` accessors the bridge calls from its own thread. The diagnostics build therefore **resolves and reports those bindings without calling any of them**; if the method scan yields no pressable candidate, that report is the input to the next decision rather than something to improvise on the device.
prep done (b0418e2); device look waits for the gap between seed 0 and seed 1 of #46

Retired 2026-09-19 by developer decision: the overlay is cosmetic for training (bridge reads memory) and cannot appear in checkpoint recordings, which are fresh single-episode sessions (spectate --episodes 1). Diagnostics prep remains on branch worktree-agent-a39ea19824de45872 (b0418e2), unmerged, should the question return.

items.title: Recordings carry the agent's action history: spectate logs every decision video-relative, and a renderer composes the guest video with a side panel
items.body:
Developer wants to see, in the recording, what the agent did and when; today only the guest screen is recorded.

Done-condition:
- `scripts/spectate.py --record` writes `<recording-stem>.decisions.jsonl` beside the video: one line per decision with video-relative timestamps (anchored to the monotonic clock at `screenrecord` launch, chunk offsets included), episode/decision/wave/cash/health_fraction, action, slot label, held_s, the v2 HUD readings, and `ended`+reason on the death decision.
- `scripts/render_recording.py --recording <stem>` concatenates the chunks and composes a side panel (header with wave/cash/health/HUD, scrolling last ~12 actions with labels and held times, current one highlighted) into `<stem>-panel.mp4`.
- Unit tests for the jsonl line shape, chunk-offset arithmetic, panel subtitle generation and the assembled ffmpeg argument list; one ffmpeg integration test skipped by name when ffmpeg is absent.
- `docs/setup.md` §9 documents the jsonl, the renderer command and the sync caveat.

comments.text:
Implemented on d0f4cc0 (worktree branch, not merged).

Approximate demo render exists: `state/recordings/observation-v2-check-panel-approx.mp4` (920x640, 257.5s), built from a best-effort track reconstructed out of the OBS2 plain-panel log — that log has no timestamps and no actions, so times are cumulative holds with the unaccounted 24s split between lead-in and the episode gap, and each action is inferred from cash falling. Two observations from it, neither caused by this change: the panel composition renders as intended (header, HUD block, 12-deep history, current highlighted), and the underlying guest picture sits on episode 1's GAME STATS dialog from roughly 35s to past 200s while the session's own log shows episode 2 playing — i.e. that recording's picture does not track the run for most of its length. The deploy path confirms artifacts by digest (`bridge.artifact_digest`, `installed_bridge_directory`, the device read-back), so a path-dependent build breaks the chain between source and installed binary: the digest no longer identifies the source, only the directory it happened to be built in.

Done condition: the production variant, built from the same source in two different build directories at different absolute path depths, produces byte-identical `libtower_bridge.so` — equal sha256 — and `docs/setup.md`'s bridge recipe states the guarantee and how to check it.

comments.text:
## Findings

Full note (ranking table, per-candidate costs, proposed replacement text for `docs/rl-candidates.md` §9, sources) is in the session scratchpad at `SOTA-BACKBONES.md`. No repo file was edited. Summary:

**The ranking in `docs/rl-candidates.md` rests on three premises that the cadence work invalidated.**

1. **§2.4 "shallow search does not reach the reward" is now false.** A wave is 3.2–5.0 decisions (`M2-E007`), so a 5-ply tree spans a whole wave and reaches a reward. With a mean legal set near 2, EZ-V2's 32 simulations are *exhaustive enumeration* to depth 5 here, not a sample of it. This is the argument that demoted the MuZero family to rank 5, and it is gone.
2. **"Replay ratio 0.25, and compute is free, so raise it" is a mis-reading.** `training.py:218` already computes the BBF-comparable unit: 0.25 gradient steps a decision × ~504 learnable transitions a batch = **126 transitions replayed per transition generated**, between SPR's 64 and BBF's 256. Headroom is ~2x, not 32x. The free-compute lever is mostly spent.
3. **§2.2's horizon problem is spent** — ADR 0009 did what §2.2 said was the largest available lever.

**What is actually missing from BBF, measured against `stacked_dqn.py`/`network.py`:** weight decay 0.1 vs our 1e-5 (four orders of magnitude); width (BBF ×4, ours `hidden=128`); shrink-and-perturb resets every 40k grad steps at 50% perturb (absent); n-step anneal 10→3 (fixed 10); γ anneal 0.97→0.997 (fixed 0.99); SPR self-predictive loss (absent); C51 (absent); prioritized replay (built, `priority_alpha=0`). BBF Fig. 8 validates every one of those on **29 ALE games outside** the Atari-100k training set. Note `M2-E004`'s absent plasticity signature was measured in this regime and does **not** license raising width or weight decay without re-measuring.

**Re-cut ranking for this regime.** 1 finish the BBF recipe on the incumbent (3–5 d, low risk); 2 offline bootstrap from the 223 logged baseline episodes, RLPD symmetric sampling — costs **no new device time** and was never built (2–3 d); 3 **Gumbel MuZero / EfficientZero-V2 with full Reanalyse via LightZero (Apache-2.0) — the different-paradigm candidate**, promoted above DreamerV3 (15–20 d); 4 DreamerV3 via `NM512/dreamerv3-torch` (MIT), demoted (8–12 d); 5 recurrent R2D2, demoted further (episodes are ~27 decisions, `history_length=8` already spans a quarter of one); 6 masked PPO as a control.

**Why MuZero over Dreamer now:** EZ-V2's Proprio Control 50k arm (mean 723.2 vs DreamerV3 517.1, SAC 552.0, TD-MPC2 740.9) is the only published vector-observation result at our budget, and Dreamer is the weakest of the three on it; LightZero carries `action_mask` natively in its env interface, while Dreamer needs a bespoke mask head in imagination with no reference implementation; and Reanalyse converts idle compute into better targets on scarce data, which is exactly this project's asymmetry. **Running 100% Reanalyse also removes MuZero's only replay-schema conflict** — stored search policy targets, which `ReplaySequence`/`SequenceBatch` have no field for — since targets are recomputed from the stored trajectory at learn time.

**Not candidates:** SimbaV2, BRO and TD-MPC2 are continuous-action methods (SimbaV2: 57 continuous-control tasks). Their transferable content is normalisation architecture for low-dimensional inputs, which belongs to rank 1 as an ablation. The 2026 pixel world-model line (Simulus, EAWM/EASimulus at a 1.818 Atari-100k mean) is worth reading before ranks 3–4, and is not a candidate for this observation space.

**Proposed runs 3+, each one falsifiable arm under `M2-P002` and all gated on run 2's verdict:** R3 BBF regularisation block; R4 offline bootstrap (cheapest in device time); R5 capacity + resets, paired with a normalisation control; R6 Gumbel MuZero with full Reanalyse, falsified if the search agrees with the raw prior on >95% of decisions.

**Evidence gaps, stated as gaps.** No BBF ablation on vector observations. No Atari-100k-class result for a hard-masked discrete action space. Nothing for sparse integer heavy-tailed episodic return with ~6 reward events an episode, and nothing at ~40k steps for a semi-MDP with variable real decision durations. Every cross-domain expectation above is extrapolation.

**Open for the Lead, not settled here:** whether MuZero is built by lifting LightZero's MCTS and model modules behind `Backbone` (recommended) or by adopting its trainer (conflicts with the fleet, records, cadence and budget accounting).

items.title: stacked-dqn audited against the DQN literature checklist; deviations listed with recommendations
items.body:
Read-only audit of `stacked-dqn` against the value-learning literature (van Hasselt 2016, Wang 2016, Schaul 2016, Horgan 2018 Ape-X, Kapturowski 2019 R2D2, Schwarzer 2023 BBF, Ng 1999) and against the project's own spec in `docs/rl-candidates.md` 3.1.

Two separate questions, answered separately:
1. Is the implementation correct?
2. Are its settings the ones the literature would choose for this problem?

Scope: `src/tower_rl/learning/{stacked_dqn,value_learning,network,replay,actor,training,exploration,policies,backbone}.py`, `environment/features.py`, `environment/episode.py`, `scripts/train.py` defaults, against the `M2-P002` protocol and the run-2 seed-0 attempt-1 numbers in `docs/experiments.md` (M2-E007).

No repo changes, no device, no test run (training is live). Output: defects (if any) first, then configuration deviations ranked by expected effect on the greedy margin, a potential-based shaping recommendation with the exact formula, and what must not change mid-run-2 versus what belongs in a run-3 ablation.

comments.text:
Audit complete. **Correctness: no defect.** Double-Q split, masked bootstrap over the next state's own mask, terminal masking, n-step truncation and the padding/learnable accounting all verified (n-step targets checked numerically against a hand computation). Terminal transitions do reach replay (`next_state` is a valid terminal state), so the death signal is present. One fragility only: an illegal stored action would give `-inf` in `chosen` and NaN the run; nothing can produce one today.

**Configuration: not the recipe `docs/rl-candidates.md` 3.1 specifies.** Ranked by effect on the greedy margin:
1. ε anneal (2,500 decisions) finishes at the same decision as the first gradient step (warm-up 100 sequences = 100 episodes ≈ 2,690 decisions; M2-E007 logs first step at episode 94). 4 of 7 actors then exploit an untrained net. Probe over 12 init seeds: the argmax is near-constant across states (1-5 distinct actions over 200 states; WAIT everywhere in 6/12), head bias beating state-dependence ~3:1 — a constant policy is worse than uniform-random, which is the 3.188 vs 5.495 M2-E007 measured.
2. `n_step=10` fixed (3.1 asks for an anneal 10→3, never implemented). Its docstring still cites run-1's 21.7 decisions/wave; under choice points it is 5.0, so n=10 is 2 waves and 37% of an episode, and 97% of actor-0's 10-step windows contain an exploratory action.
3. Replay ratio 0.25 vs 3.1's "roughly 2 to 8" (run 1 used 2.0). The 126:1 in `training.py:220` is stale run-1 arithmetic; under choice points it is 54:1.
4. `--priority-alpha 0`: PER off, IS weights ≡ 1, β anneal inert, `DEFAULT_PRIORITY_EXPONENT=0.9` dead.
5. Adam eps left at 1e-8 (Rainbow 1.5e-4, R2D2 1e-3) — lands on the advantage heads specifically.
6. Trunk mean-pools all 60 rows though only ~7 are ever valid — the argument `_dueling_masked_q` makes for the advantage centre, not applied to the trunk.
7. `history_length=8`; 3.1's named k=1 ablation never run.

**Shaping (Ng 1999, policy-invariant at γ=0.99 and any n):** Φ(s) = clip(enemies_killed / max(1, enemies_expected), 0, 1), **Φ(terminal) := 0**; r̃ = r + γΦ(s′) − Φ(s), and r̃_T = r_T − Φ(s_T). Telescopes inside the n-step window (Σγ^k F = γⁿΦ(s_{t+n}) − Φ(s_t)), so `n_step_targets` needs no change. Do not put the wave number in Φ. It is a `reward-v2` schema change.

**Mid-run 2, must not change:** the three schema versions and `profile_id` (replay silently rejects), `sequence_length`/`burn_in` (`collate` raises on a mixed batch), `history_length` and any network width (checkpoint will not reload).

Long form: scratchpad `DQN-AUDIT.md` (417 lines), with file:line for every claim and the full source list.

items.title: Every upgrade slot purchasable in-run: availability `all` applied at round start (ADR 0011); first `all` run ends verified clean
items.body:
Developer decision 2026-09-19: unlock every upgrade slot programmatically, not by play. Availability only — do not touch workshop power/levels, which stay at baseline.

Timing: after run 2 (`M2-P002`, board #46).

Done-condition: a new frozen AVD image with all 60 in-run upgrade slots purchasable, saved as a new base image with its own `profile_id`, plus an instrumented clone derived from it and baselines re-measured under `M2-P002`'s structure.

comments.text:
Scout findings (repo `tower-rl` @ e9267f2), read-only, no device.

**1. Purchasability fields.** Per family (attack/defense/utility) on `Main`: `upgradeUnlocked`/`upgradeDefenseUnlocked`/`upgradeUtilityUnlocked` (`Boolean[]`, len 20/slot family — this is what the bridge reads), `upgradeTierUnlocked`/…Tier… (`Boolean[]`), `upgradeMaxLevel`/…, `upgradeCost`/…, `upgradeLevel`. Bridge: `native/tower_bridge/tower_bridge.cpp` `ReadFamilyAvailability` (~L1552) computes `available[index] = active && is_unlocked==1 && is_maxed==0 && cost>0 && cost<=cash` — `unlocked` is the field that actually gates purchasability today. `tier_unlocked` is read (`FamilyFields.tier_unlocked`, ~L361) but a code comment at L2085 records live 29.0.3 evidence that `tier_unlocked` is **always false** for every offered upgrade — tier gating isn't currently exercised, consistent with scratchpad note that `upgrade*TierEverUnlocked` sits beside it. "Slot exists but locked" = `unlocked[i]==0`; "unlocked at level 0" = `unlocked[i]==1`, `level==0`; "tier locked" is a distinct, currently-inert flag. `maxed[i]` is the level-cap flag, separate from `unlocked`. Python side mirrors this: `src/tower_rl/environment/run_state.py` L437-456, `available = active and unlocked and not maxed and priced and cost <= cash`. No evidence these arrays reset per round — `docs/environment-profile.yaml`'s `permanent_workshop_state` block (attack/defense/utility levels, `range_upgrades: locked`, etc.) documents them as **persistent account state**, matching ADR-0001/0008's framing that Workshop unlocks are between-run, not per-episode.

**2. Persistence.** `Main` carries `saveLoad SaveLoad` (an object reference — a second-hop read, not enumerated), plus `playerOptedToSaveResume`, `resumeRoundOnLoadShown`, `cloudInviteSent Boolean` (main-fields.txt L604, 514, 592, 98) — strong save/cloud-save hints but no method names; the diagnostics build (`FIELD-ENUMERATION.md` #47, branch b0418e2) enumerates field names only, not methods, for `Main`/`IntSelect`, though the harness (`LogClassMembers`) *could* list method names/arity with a rebuild. `docs/workstation-handoff.md` has no `/data/data`/`shared_prefs` grep hits; the only save-adjacent artifact is `state/avd-backup-2026-09-18/` (35GB, whole-AVD backup, not an isolated save file) made for a WebView bake, and the v1 bake process (L686-719) never isolated or copied a save file — it snapshot-and-backed-up the whole AVD, so v1 gives no evidence of the save's on-disk format.

**3. Write path — facts vs inference.** Fact: the bridge resolves `il2cpp_field_static_set_value` (L120,162) and uses it exactly twice — `GameSpeedModifier` (L2027) and `IntSelect.upgradeSelect` (L2096, followed by `UnitySendMessage` to trigger the purchase, L2099). Fact: no `il2cpp_field_set_value` (instance-field write) is resolved anywhere — only `field_get_value` (instance) and `field_static_set_value` (static). `Main.upgradeUnlocked` etc. are **instance** fields read via `ReadField`+`field_get_value` on the live `Main` object; writing them needs either resolving instance `field_set_value` or, since array elements are already read via `ReadPrimitiveArray` (L653) doing raw offset arithmetic on the `Il2CppArray*`, a symmetric raw write at the same offsets — both are new C++, not present today. Inference: triggering the game's own save afterward is unproven from this repo — the existing lifecycle `UnitySendMessage` path (L2056, "a lifecycle-style command to a method") is the only send-message-to-arbitrary-method mechanism on hand, but no save-triggering method name is known; alternatively letting the game's natural `go_home`/background save cycle run is plausible but unverified.

**4. Profile identity.** `profile_id` is **not computed from game state** — it's a CMake build-time constant: `native/tower_bridge/CMakeLists.txt` L12 declares `TOWER_BRIDGE_PROFILE_ID` (cache var, default `"unconfigured"`), baked into `CMakeCache.txt` and read by `src/tower_rl/simulation/bridge.py` `compatibility()` (L114-133) as part of `BridgeCompatibility`. Current value in tests/fixtures is `instrumented-training-v1` (`tests/unit/test_migrate_state.py`). `expected_compatibility()` (`bring_up.py` L172-175) calls `compatibility(bridge_build_directory())`. For v2: a new `TOWER_BRIDGE_PROFILE_ID` must be configured for a v2 bridge build; `scripts/migrate_state.py` L65 also carries this key, so migration/inventory tooling references it too. Other v1-id references: `checkpoint.py` (`profile_id` in checkpoint metadata), `replay.py` (`compatibility()` tuple gating replay reuse), `evaluator.py`/`episode.py`/`run_identity.py`/`run_environment.py` all thread `profile_id` through episode and run identity — a v2 id is a new compatibility axis everywhere these compare, and `docs/environment-profile.yaml`'s own top-level `profile_id: m0-dual-host-api36-v2` is a *different*, workstation-hardware profile concept, not the bridge/game profile — worth not conflating the two "profile_id" namespaces when scoping this.

**5. Procedure sketch + risks (post run-2, never on the canonical v1 image).**
- Fresh clone of the canonical v1 base image (never mutate it) → boot writable → apply the programmatic unlock (new bridge write path from §3) → confirm the game's own save persists it (open/close, or explicit save trigger) → snapshot as the v2 base → derive an instrumented clone from that base (mirrors how `instrumented_bridge.sh`/`clone_session.py` derive v1's instrumented clone) → back up per the v1 pattern (`state/avd-backup-...`).
- Risks: save format/encryding unknown (§2) — a raw field/array write may not survive the game's own save round-trip if it validates or checksums state (anti-tamper); `unlocked` vs `tier_unlocked` — since tier_unlocked reads always-false today, forcing `unlocked=true` without touching tier flags may be sufficient, but that's unverified beyond tier 1's evidence; a slot could end up visible-but-unbuyable if some other gate (e.g. `upgrade*WorkshopMaxLevel`, cost arrays, or a UI-side check not on `Main`) also matters; no cloud-save conflict expected while airplane-mode/offline is preserved (ADR-0008 also explicitly forbids any cloud/save *ladder* action — this issue's programmatic-write approach is a deliberate departure from the ladder mechanism, per the 2026-09-19 decision, not a ladder step).
- Verification: an in-run observation (via the existing `ReadFamilyAvailability`/`upgradeUnlocked` read path) showing all 60 slots (20 attack + 20 defense + 20 utility, per `FIELD-SAMPLES.md`'s confirmed slot widths) report `unlocked=true`, sane non-zero costs, and workshop/combat-stat baselines (`docs/environment-profile.yaml`'s `permanent_workshop_state` numbers: damage 3, health 5, etc.) unchanged from v1.

**Unknowns needing the device:** `SaveLoad` class members/methods (not enumerated), the save file's actual location/format on `/data/data/com.TechTreeGames.TheTower/...` (no path found in this scan), whether an instance-field write survives a save/reload cycle, and whether any check beyond `Main`'s arrays (e.g. server-side or anti-tamper) rejects an unlock that wasn't earned.

**Six-slot profile v1: does it cap the final wave?** Extraction script: `state/mlflow.db` (read-only) + per-episode JSON under `state/m2-run1/set-b/*` and `state/records/m2-run2/*`.

| Source (all choice-point cadence, obs-v2, profile `tower-play-29.0.3-rooted-readonly-v1`) | n | mean | p50 | p90 | p95 | max | ≥10 | ≥12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| run1 train, 1st half decisions | 709 | 6.27 | 6 | 9.2 | 10 | 11 | 71 | 0 |
| run1 train, 2nd half decisions | 710 | 6.37 | 7 | 10 | 10 | 11 | 89 | 0 |
| run1 set-B greedy: stacked-dqn | 61 | 6.77 | 7 | 10 | 10 | **11** | 9 | 0 |
| run1 set-B greedy: scripted | 63 | 5.81 | 6 | 8.8 | 10 | 10 | 5 | 0 |
| run1 set-B greedy: random | 62 | 5.79 | 6 | 9.0 | 10 | 10 | 5 | 0 |
| run2 baseline: eval-scripted | 112 | 6.43 | 6 | 9.0 | 10 | 10 | 11 | 0 |
| run2 baseline: eval-random | 111 | 5.50 | 6 | 8.0 | 9.0 | 10 | 3 | 0 |
| run2 seed0 attempt2 (live), near-greedy act3-6 | 567 | 5.25 | 6 | 8.0 | 9.0 | **11** | 18 | 0 |
| run2 seed0 attempt2 (live), exploratory act0-2 | 441 | 4.96 | 6 | 8.0 | 8.0 | **11** | 11 | 0 |

**Headline: ceiling plausible at ~11-12.** Pooled n=2,836 valid episodes across every arm/source above; final waves 1–11 all occur, wave **12 is never once recorded** — the max ever seen on this profile, in any run, is **11**. Only the learned/stacked-dqn policy and the still-running seed0 attempt2 (both explore and near-greedy actors) reach 11; scripted and random cap at 10 in both run1 and run2. So arms mostly die in the same band (mean 5–7, p50=6 everywhere) but the learned tail extends exactly one wave past the baselines' — it doesn't blow through the ceiling, it just reaches it more often.

M1B-E008 (docs/experiments.md, 2026-09-17, scripted, n=149, mean **9.79**, range 5–11) is **not directly comparable**: it predates the choice-point cadence (ADR 0009 / M2-E007) and its speed/protocol differ, so its much higher mean is not evidence against a ceiling — but note its own max is also 11, consistent with the same cap.

Caveats: run2 seed0 attempt2 is a live, in-progress run (partial/exploratory data, no `resolved_config` param found — near-greedy split inferred from `exploration_epsilon_floors` ladder, actors 3–6 at ε≤0.016 vs 0–2 at ε≥0.047); set-B/run2-baseline arms are small (61–112 eps each); M1B-E008 excluded from the pooled ceiling count due to cadence mismatch.

Desk-study findings (no device): the three unlock arrays (upgradeUnlocked / upgradeDefenseUnlocked / upgradeUtilityUnlocked, Boolean[] on Main) are the sole purchasability gate per the bridge's command path (native/tower_bridge/README.md). The bridge can write them: ReadPrimitiveArray already locates the array memory, so a WritePrimitiveArray plus one command is tens of lines. SaveLoad internals (methods, format, checksum, cloud hook) are unenumerated; the bridge cannot invoke a game method on an unnamed GameObject.
Candidate route that avoids SaveLoad entirely: set the arrays true at every app start (memory-only, reproducible, touches no save/cloud; profile id becomes v1+unlock-all in run identity). Validity hinges on one unknown: whether the game recomputes unlocks from workshop counters at load/round start.
Device trial (~30 min, disposable clone, offline, no coin spend, no Settings/Store/Cloud UI) deferred until run 2 (#46) ends. Detail: session scratchpad PROFILE-V2-FEASIBILITY.md.
Bridge write path for the unlock trial; device trial itself waits for #46

Production bridge digest unchanged: b9852e64…76284; diagnostics build: 1a8d2467…7289.

Start: 2026-09-20T08:27:01+02:00

Device trial done at ad50e69, diagnostics bridge 1a8d2467…7289; recorded as M2-E008 (585342d). `state/bridge/current` 662cba09…8902b untouched.
Q1 the write takes: 4/2/0 true before, 20/20/20 read back, confirmed again by `scripts/unlock_trial.py`.
Q2 it survives the round (20/20/20 on the terminal run) but **not a round start**: 7/4/7 after go_home+start_round, and the survivors are only the empty-name tail slots (attack 17-19, defense 18-19, utility 13-19) — every real row reverts to v1 (4/2/0). The game recomputes real rows at round start.

**The base-image route is retired; this item's scope is now "unlock applied at every round start".**

items.title: Explain the scripted baseline's drop from 9.79 (M1B-E008, 2026-09-17) to 6.43 (M2-E007, 2026-09-19) on the same profile
items.body: Scout investigation (scripted-drop). Bounded question: what changed between M1B-E008 (150 ep, scripted, mean final wave 9.79, sd 1.26, 236 ep/h) and M2-E007 stage 1 (112 ep, scripted, mean 6.43, IQM 6.57, choice-point cadence, 120 Hz, host renderer, observation-v2) on the nominal same profile tower-play-29.0.3-rooted-readonly-v1. Findings to follow as a comment.

comments.text:
**Scout finding: the drop predates 09-19 entirely — it happened on 09-17, the same day as E008, when the game-clock mechanism was replaced.**

Ranked by plausibility (fact vs inference marked):

1. **[FACT, primary cause] E008/E009 were measured under a game-clock mechanism since shown to be broken and fully replaced.** `M1B-E008`/`E009` (9.79 / 9.758 mean wave) ran at `requested speed 64` — the old "game speed multiplier" hack (`Main.gameSpeed`/`GameSpeedModifier`), independent of and prior to frame-exact stepping. `M1B-E012` (same day) withdrew the "8x preserves decisions" claim and measured decisions/wave at 12.2 (1x) vs 4.8 (64x) — confirming speed and decision density trade off "by construction" under that mechanism (`docs/workstation-handoff.md` "Standing decisions" #1–#2). `M1B-E016`–`E019` (same day, later) replaced it with frame-exact stepping (`Time.captureDeltaTime`, `frame_game_ms`), and `M1B-E025` pinned the game's own speed at 1x permanently (commit `9cc3a233`). **`M1B-E021`, run later that same 09-17, already under the new mechanism (`--frame-game-ms 100`, commit `86fcf3c`), measured scripted mean final wave 5.565 (sd 2.17, n=23)** — matching the post-mechanism-change regime, not E008. Every later measurement stays in that band: `M1B-E053`/`E054` (09-18, host, 60/120 Hz) final_wave 5.85–5.96; `M2-E002` (09-18/19) scripted IQM 5.94; `M2-E007` (09-19) mean 6.43 / IQM 6.57. **The 9.79→~6 drop is fully explained by a mechanism change on 09-17 itself, not by anything specific to 09-19's cadence/renderer/Hz/observation-v2 changes.**
2. **[FACT, ruled out as primary] Choice-point cadence.** `CheapestFirstPolicy` (added `0664326`) never waits at a choice point — measured directly in `M2-E007`: 0.0% WAIT share. `CadenceConfig`/choice-points landed 09-19 (`7648ed9`, ADR 0009), i.e. *after* the ~5.6–6.0 band was already established on 09-17/09-18 under every-slice cadence. Cadence cannot be the cause of the 9.79→6.43 drop since the drop predates it.
3. **[FACT, ruled out] 120 Hz vs 60 Hz.** `M1B-E053` (REJECT, provisional, cash_log separated at 2/7 wave indices) and `M1B-E054` (replication: rule fires nowhere, REJECT not replicated) compared 60 Hz against 120 Hz only within the same interleaved fleet on 09-18 (n=27/26 then 36/27), never against E008-era numbers, and explicitly *not* on mean final wave ("never on mean final wave, pooled sd 2.27 needs ~324 episodes/arm for half a wave" — E053). Both arms in that equivalence fleet already show final_wave ~5.85–5.96, in the current band, at both rates — Hz is not what separates E008 from E007.
4. **[FACT, ruled out] Renderer.** `-gpu host` vs lavapipe shown equivalent on game-time ratio, decisions/wave and mean wave (workstation-handoff "Done: -gpu host…"); `M1B-E055` falsifies a render-cost/CPU-per-frame hypothesis at 120 Hz. Frame-exact stepping decouples render pacing from game time by construction, so renderer is not a plausible driver of the wave-count difference.
5. **[UNCONFIRMED, low plausibility] Profile/AVD drift.** E008/E009 ran on "the instrumented clone" (singular); M2-E007 ran on 7 fleet clones `emulator-5556`…`5568`. The 09-18 WebView bake attempt did **not** persist to `-read-only` instances (`M1B-E051`: a fresh `-read-only` cold boot still reads the old WebView build). No evidence the base image or save state changed in a way that reaches gameplay between 09-17 and 09-19. Account progression (Workshop) is kept locked/no permanent spend per protocol. Not investigated: whether E008's specific clone's per-episode account state (coins/highest-wave) differed materially from the fleet clones' — plausible but not checked, and secondary to finding 1 regardless.
6. **[NOT VERIFIED] `final_wave`/`EpisodeSummary` definition drift.** Did not diff `episode.py` history for a change to how a wave is counted at death between 09-17 and 09-19 beyond confirming the death-boundary retry logic (`M1B-E007`/`E008`) is unrelated to this. Low priority given finding 1 already accounts for the full gap.
7. **[NOT DONE] Per-episode E008 records vs E007's `game_ms`/wave.** `state/records/m2-run2/eval-scripted*` exists for E007; no equivalent raw per-episode file was found under `state/` for the 09-17 E008 run (only `state/runs/session-20260917-*` training sessions, not the E008 scripted-reliability record) — could not do the game-ms-per-wave distribution comparison item 6 asked for in the time available.

**Cheapest discriminating check for after run 2:** re-run ~20–24 scripted episodes at E008's exact historical settings — `requested speed 64`, pre-frame-exact game-clock path — is not reproducible (that code path no longer exists; `GAME_SPEED` is pinned by construction and asserted by test). The real cheapest check is the inverse: confirm decisions/wave and mean final wave from `M1B-E021`'s exact recipe (`--frame-game-ms 100`, every-slice, scripted, n≈23–24) reproduce today's ~5.5–6.5 band on the current image/fleet. If it lands in that band (expected), it closes this issue by showing the 09-17 mechanism change, not the 09-19 protocol changes, is the cause; E008/E009 should then be marked in `docs/experiments.md` as measured under the superseded speed mechanism and non-comparable to any post-`M1B-E016` figure.

items.title: A device stage runs unattended from one invocation and always ends with the device verified clean
items.body:
## Objective

Every multi-hour device stage — a training seed, an evaluation batch, a recording
session — is currently babysat by an agent that launches the command and then
sleeps and polls its log for hours, running cleanup by hand at the end. That is
expensive, and it puts the safety-critical cleanup in an agent's hands on abort
paths. A script should own the stage lifecycle instead: an agent launches it once
as a background task and is woken when it exits.

`scripts/run_stage.sh` supervises one stage command, and guarantees on **every**
exit path — success, failure, SIGINT, SIGTERM — that each instance is cleaned
through `scripts/instrumented_bridge.sh cleanup`, every emulator is killed, and
the host is verified clean (no qemu process counted via `/proc/*/exe`, no adb
device). Device-safety invariants are refused rather than warned about: only the
`tower_rl_instrumented_api36` AVD, even console ports from 5556, `-read-only`,
offline verified by interface. Never `emulator-5554`, never
`tower_rl_api36_play_x86_64`.

## Done-condition

A device stage runs unattended from one invocation and always ends with the
device verified clean: the script exits non-zero if the stage command failed or
if cleanup/verification failed, and writes one summary line (stage name, stage
exit code, cleanup result, instance count, wall time) to its log under
`state/logs/` and to stdout. Verified without a device by tests under `tests/`
that drive the script against stub `adb`/`instrumented_bridge.sh` on `PATH`,
covering stage success, stage failure, cleanup failure, an instance that is not
live, and SIGTERM during the stage command.

## Pointers

- `scripts/instrumented_bridge.sh` — owns the cleanup post-conditions; this
  script must not reimplement or weaken them.
- `src/tower_rl/simulation/fleet.py`, `instance.py` — where fleet bring-up and
  teardown live today.
- `docs/workstation-handoff.md` START HERE, `docs/setup.md` — the launch
  procedure the change documents.
- `docs/experiments.md` `M2-P002` — the stages this exists to run unattended.

comments.text:
Three findings from building this, one of which limits the done-condition.

1. **The stage runners own their own bring-up**, so the script does not do it: `scripts/train.py:1098` calls `bring_up_fleet` and `scripts/train.py:1113-1114` `tear_down_fleet` in a `finally` (`run_actors.py:453-459` likewise). Only `run_episodes.py` expects an instance already up. The script is therefore a supervisor and an abort-path backstop, not a bring-up wrapper — so the `-read-only`/AVD/offline invariants it enforces bite on instances already live at launch, and on the train.py path the fleet's own invariants (`simulation/instance.py`) are what hold.
2. **`instrumented_bridge.sh cleanup` exits 0 on two of its own failed checks.** The overlay still being mounted is `|| echo "warning: the overlay is still mounted" >&2`, and a frame-rate override that did not reset is `echo ... NOT-reset ... >&2`; neither changes the exit status, and only a surviving bridge artifact does (the final `su_device test`). `run_stage.sh` reads the exit status, so it would report `cleanup ok` in those two cases. Not patched — out of scope here and the Lead's call.
3. **A shell without job control starts async commands with SIGINT ignored**, and a signal ignored on entry cannot be trapped by the child either, so `kill -INT` at a supervised `train.py` would never reach its `KeyboardInterrupt` teardown. `set -m` before the launch is the fix; the SIGTERM test fails without it.

`instrumented_bridge.sh cleanup` now fails when any post-condition fails (`cb5d959`).

- **The identity readbacks were not compared to anything** — `report_identity` printed the libunity SHA-256, the dumpsys `versionName`/`versionCode`/`installerPackageName` lines and the mount count, and nothing checked them. They are compared now.
- **Expectations are read, not written twice**: the digest, `versionName` and `versionCode` come from the private build's own `CMakeCache.txt`, the file `bridge.compatibility` reads and the one place that says which game build this profile is for; on the installed bridge those are exactly `ffc1f3ef…dd0040`, `29.0.3`, `1199`. A build directory that cannot be read is a recorded failure, not a skipped check. `com.android.vending` is the one constant, since the build configuration does not carry it.
- **Every step still runs to the end**: failures accumulate through `fail`, the exit is non-zero iff at least one check failed, and the last line is `cleanup_checks: all passed` or `cleanup_checks: N failed on <serial>`.
- **The `adb` remote-exit-code assumption is refuted for this call, and removed**: adb has propagated the remote status since platform-tools 24, but the artifact check's remote command is `su -c '<test> && <echo>'`, so the status that arrives is su's and depends on the su build. The check now reads the marker the device echoes.
- **Knock-on**: `fleet.tear_down_instance` raises on these failures where it used to pass, so a teardown that leaves an override or a mount behind is now reported per instance. The emulator is still killed regardless — `kill_emulator` is in that function's `finally`.
- Tests (stub `adb` under a stub SDK root): `test_a_cleanup_whose_checks_all_pass_exits_zero`, `test_an_overlay_that_will_not_unmount_fails_after_every_step_has_run`, `test_a_frame_rate_override_that_did_not_reset_fails_the_cleanup`, `test_a_surviving_bridge_artifact_fails_the_cleanup`, `test_an_installer_that_is_not_play_fails_the_cleanup`.

Review found two defects in the abort path; both fixed in `a64a33b`, with one question left for the Lead.

- **`uv run` neither acts on SIGINT nor passes it on.** Measured here, device-free, with the real shape: `kill -INT` at the `uv` of a `uv run python …` left both `uv` and its python child running minutes later; `kill -INT` at the process *group* printed python's `KeyboardInterrupt` and `uv` exited 0. Signalling only the process the script started would have meant every stage sat out its whole 900 s grace, was SIGKILLed, and `train.py`'s own fleet teardown never ran. The interrupt and the final kill now go to the group (`set -m` is what makes it exist). Regression test `test_a_stage_whose_work_is_a_child_process_is_still_interrupted`, confirmed to fail against the old signalling.
- **A shell older than bash 5.1 would clean the device up under a live stage.** `wait -n -p` is what waits on the stage and the grace timer at once; under 5.0 the option is rejected, its variable stays empty, and the script reads that as "the stage finished". Now refused at startup; the workstation runs 5.3.9, and `docs/setup.md` §10 says so.
- **Open, for the Lead:** `finish` clears INT/TERM, so a second signal during teardown kills the supervisor mid-cleanup — reproduced by the reviewer. `trap '' INT TERM` would make teardown uninterruptible, which device safety wants, at the cost of an operator being unable to stop a hung cleanup with anything short of SIGKILL. Not changed on my own initiative.

Two safety holes in the abort path, both closed in `04f140a`.

- **A second signal abandoned the teardown.** `finish` restored INT/TERM to their default so it could not re-enter itself, so a second Ctrl-C or `kill` during cleanup killed the supervisor with the device half cleaned and no summary line. Teardown now **ignores** both. What makes that safe is a bound rather than a promise: each serial's cleanup runs under `timeout -k 10 600`, a timeout is a recorded failure for that serial, and the remaining serials, the kills and the verification still run. Found by test, not by reading: the grace timer is started inside the teardown and inherits the ignored TERM, so it must be killed with SIGKILL — otherwise the wait sits out the whole grace period the stage just saved.
- **Preflight only looked at instances adb answers for**, and those are exactly the ones that *can* be certified offline. It now walks every **attached** instance and refuses `emulator-5554`, a command line naming the canonical AVD, a missing `-read-only`, or any state other than `device`. The teardown's kill sweep likewise never kills an instance whose command line names the canonical AVD at any port; its presence is a recorded failure, not a silent skip.
- Also: `stage_pid` initialised before the trap that reads it; `--shutdown-grace` validated; `check_identity`/`report_identity` share one set of readings; `spectate.py` writes its session record even when `tear_down_instance` raises.
- Tests: `test_a_second_signal_during_teardown_does_not_abandon_the_cleanup`, `test_a_cleanup_that_never_returns_is_given_up_on_and_the_rest_still_runs`, `test_an_attached_instance_that_is_not_answering_is_refused_before_launch`, `test_an_emulator_running_the_canonical_avd_is_never_killed`, `test_a_grace_period_that_is_not_a_positive_number_of_seconds_is_refused` (3 cases). `pytest` 813 passed / 2 skipped, `ruff` and `mypy` clean.
- `M2-P002` carries **Amendment 4** (2026-09-20): stages from seed 1 onward launch through `run_stage.sh`; no measured quantity, threshold or rule changes. Both docs now carry the full seed-1 command instead of an ellipsis.

items.title: M3: SOTA arms under the M2 protocol — DreamerV3, (EfficientZero V2 conditional)
items.body:
Goal from docs/task.md: multiple RL approaches compared under one identical budgeted protocol. Run 3 (M2-P003, #57) gave the first learned policy clearly above scripted under availability `all` (period-2 near-greedy 12.15 vs scripted-all 6.11), with the training recipe at 2015-DQN settings: replay ratio 0.25, PER α=0 (built, off), n-step 10 fixed, γ 0.99 fixed, no resets, ~200k-param net.

Prerequisite: stacked-dqn seed 2 under M2-P003 (reproducibility).

Arm 1 — BBF recipe on the existing stacked-dqn backbone (Schwarzer et al. 2023): replay ratio 8 (host is idle; near-free), PER on (α≈0.5–0.9, β anneal), periodic shrink-and-perturb resets, n-step anneal 10→3, γ anneal 0.97→0.997, weight decay 0.1, wider net. Config + two small features; one exploratory seed at the M2-P003 budget; every deviation from the paper values cited.

Arm 2 — DreamerV3 (Hafner et al. 2023): model-based world model + actor-critic, vector observations and discrete actions natively; new training loop (PyTorch port). One exploratory seed.

Arm 3 (conditional) — EfficientZero V2: only after measuring the per-decision latency budget on the live game; MCTS per action may not fit.

Protocol: interleaved arms via scripts/compare_arms.py, bootstrap intervals, one seed exploratory, second seed only for arms that beat stacked-dqn. Device time ≈ 6 h per arm-seed at run-3 pace. Nothing starts before #57 lands and the developer approves device time.

comments.text: Run 4 (#60) is the first step toward the BBF-recipe arm: replay ratio and n-step on stacked-dqn.

Lead, 2026-09-24: proposed approach, discussed with the developer; not yet started.
- BBF: build it into our stacked-dqn. It is a set of additions to what we already have: head resets, a bigger network, and a replay ratio. Check every value against the paper's hyperparameter table and justify each deviation.
- DreamerV3 and EfficientZero V2: use the official implementations (danijar/dreamerv3; EfficientZeroV2's own repo). Wrap our environment contract in a gym-style adapter so the algorithm is not rebuilt.
- Correctness gate before any game run: the same code path reproduces a published result on a cheap standard task (a known-answer test). Configuration is checked separately against the paper.
- Fairness: the M2 protocol, meaning the same budget, the same default-build evaluation, and pre-registration.

Note from the #69 survey: scripts/compare_arms.py can only play the scripted, random and wait policies, never a checkpoint, and it is being removed under #69. The M3 protocol is the M2 fleet path used for M2-P005: train.py, then select_checkpoint.py for the arm, then report_arms.py for the evaluation and bootstrap_difference. It is not compare_arms.

Developer decision (2026-09-24): Option B, one training run per learner. The comparison table labels each result as a single run; its 95% intervals cover the evaluation episodes of that run's arm, not variation between runs. It states as a limitation the observed between-run spread: near-greedy means at (8k,12k] decisions of 9.87, 10.02 and 8.32 for runs 4, 5 and 5b, same recipe and seed. A 3-runs-per-learner design (Agarwal et al. 2021) was offered and declined. docs/task.md §1.1 gets amended to say this once run 5b's device stage has ended (no main-checkout commits while it is live).
BBF arm started as #70 (developer approved, 2026-09-24). Correction to the body above: under #68 the arm is chosen by the solution.md §9.2b period rule, not by select_checkpoint.py.

DreamerV3 arm done (#79): 12.68 [12.22, 13.13], which is 0.80 below stacked-dqn's 13.48 (#78), CI [−1.47, −0.15]. Both are single runs at 120,712 decisions. EfficientZero V2 (conditional) has not been started; that decision waits for the developer.
Plan (2026-09-27): after M3-P009 (stacked-dqn PER, v2), run DreamerV3 under the same baseline v2 (Workshop L5, availability all, 1M decisions) for a like-for-like comparison. Both are single runs.

Developer decision, 2026-09-27: arms keep the budget in decisions (as pre-registered). Each arm's report also states the game-seconds it consumed, because game time per decision depends on the policy (M3-P010: 2.7 to 5.8 game-s per decision, against ~2.0 for M3-P009). #89 and #90 are done, so this item is unblocked.

Started 2026-09-28 by developer decision.
Evidence: the M3-P015 mid-run probe (#85, comments 5873174841 and 5873219460) found DQN's greedy upgrade choice sits on a top-2 action gap of 0.0005-0.03 against Q values of about 1-9, so its argmax flips between rows across checkpoints.
Decision: stop tuning DQN. M3-P015 finishes as the DQN record. DreamerV3 becomes the main arm, using the same horizon (0.999 per game-second, ADR 0013), the same 1M-decision budget and the same evaluation protocol.
First step: an inventory of the existing Dreamer code path and a spec, derived principle → quantity → our value.

Inventory of the existing Dreamer arm (details: scratchpad dreamer/inventory.md).
- DreamerBackbone is our own PyTorch port of danijar/dreamerv3 at pinned commit e3f02248: size12m, about 10.1M parameters, train_ratio 512, batch 16×64, imagination horizon 15, horizon 333 per decision.
- Prior results: M3-P002 12.68 (n=105); M3-P007 at 1M decisions 15.70, SD 3.53 (n=105), against stacked-dqn's M3-P006 17.01, SD 4.16 (n=104). Both ran under baseline v1 (Workshop L0); Dreamer has never run under v2 (L5).
- Discount: train.py refuses --discount and --discount-per-game-second for Dreamer (STACKED_ONLY_FLAGS), and nothing in the model knows Δt.
- Masking: the action mask is decoded as an observation key in imagination; there is no reference implementation for that.

DreamerV3 settings derivation (specialist, sources arXiv 2301.04104 v1/v2 and code at commit e3f02248; full text in scratchpad dreamer/derivation.md).
- Only the discount is task-specific: γ_s^Δt per transition at 0.999 per game-second, applied through the code's own contdisc continue target, (1−term)·0.999^Δt. The replay λ-return uses the stored d.
- Everything else stays at published values (size12m, train ratio 512, 16×64, H 15, λ 0.95, η 3e-4, percentile return normalisation); each is justified in the derivation.
- Least certain: whether the continue head learns Δt through binary cross-entropy (runtime invariant: implied Δt within 10% of the true Δt), train ratio 512, and size12m for vector inputs.
- The actor's temperature η·S ≈ 1e-3–2.4e-3 turns DQN-size gaps into a stable mixed policy rather than argmax flips; it still fails if critic bias exceeds the gap.

Dreamer game-second discount and survival reward are ready on branch worktree-agent-a00fa7baec71b90a0 (a96d536, 6ad9f14, a4434f0). Not merged: it lands after M3-P015 ends.
- Tier C review found nothing blocking. The hand trace (purchase, 5 s wait, terminal) confirmed alignment and no double discount; old stacked-dqn resumes are unchanged.
- Review fixes applied: a test for evaluating legacy checkpoints, the task-level V_REF/WAVE_SECONDS/game_time_discounts/survival_rewards moved to value_learning.py, and a new dreamer_implied_dt_relative_error diagnostic.
- Gates on a4434f0: pytest, ruff and mypy all exit 0.
- Still untested: the compiled CUDA path. A GPU smoke test runs before the M3-P016 launch.

Landed: merge be0dae5 (Dreamer game-time discount and survival reward, Tier C reviewed) and M3-P016 pre-registration b95c5cd. HEAD == origin/main.
- Gates: pytest 1169 passed; ruff and mypy exit 0.
- GPU smoke test on an idle 4090: Dreamer tests 30 passed, 0 skipped (compiled bf16 path ran); 20 compiled learn steps, median 34.6 ms per update; all dreamer_* diagnostics finite.
- Launch script scratchpad dreamer/launch.sh passes a dry parse. Not launched; waiting for the developer's go.

items.title: Spectate bring-up fails after a fleet run: radio-enable timeout, then bridge stream closed (run 3 arm recording missing)
items.body:
Stage 4 of M2-P003 run 3 (spectate arm recording) failed twice at bring-up:

- `m2-run3-spectate-arm`: radio-enable timeout (25s)
- `m2-run3-spectate-arm-2`: bridge stream closed

Logs: `state/logs/m2-run3-spectate-arm*.log`

The identical spectate path succeeded solo earlier the same day (`m2-run3-diag-solo`), so the failure appears specific to bring-up after a preceding fleet run rather than the spectate path itself. No diagnosis has been done yet.

comments.text: Possibly the same class: M2-P004's first eval lost 5/7 instances to a host gfxstream renderer crash (RenderThread segfault in libgfxstream_backend.so, 'Failed to find ColorBuffer', X connection broken; per-instance logs state/logs/tower-rl-emulator-emulator-<port>.log). Check the spectate stages' emulator logs for the same lines before diagnosing further.

Lead, 2026-09-24: dispatching the run-4 arm recording (checkpoint-gs0240594.pt, session-20260924-030851) via spectate.py --record + render_recording.py. If bring-up fails again, crash lines from the emulator log and logcat are captured here as evidence for this bug (compare with the gfxstream RenderThread crash seen in run-4 eval attempt 1).

Spectate recording of the run-4 arm (checkpoint-gs0240594, sha bc94b628…): two attempts, both failed to produce a usable recording; per the pre-declared one-retry rule, stopped after attempt 2 and did not retry further.

**Attempt 1** (`m2-run4-spectate-arm`, `state/logs/m2-run4-spectate-arm-20260924-*.log`): bring-up succeeded, bridge deployed and connected, game reached wave 1, 7 decisions (all pre-round purchases, 0 game-time elapsed), then the single time-advance was cut off by the bridge's wall-time ceiling after 15.503s of advance wall time for only 1.5 game-seconds budgeted — `invalid_reasons: ["an advance was cut off by the bridge's wall-time ceiling"]` (`ADVANCE_TRUNCATED_BY_WALL`, src/tower_rl/environment/run_environment.py:214). Episode recorded `valid: false, final_wave: 1`. A recording file exists (`m2-run4-arm-000.mp4`, moved to scratchpad, not committed) but plays an invalid episode, not the arm's normal behaviour — not usable evidence of the arm. `run_stage.sh` reported `exit 0, cleanup ok`, host verified clean.

No crash lines and no obvious host cause found for this one; it does not match the #59 ColorBuffer/X-connection GPU-crash signature. Worth noting as a distinct failure class from #59's own pattern, in case it recurs: possibly related to `frame_game_ms=100` (the new M2-S001 default) interacting with spectate's real-time (60 Hz) playback, but that is speculation, not established here.

**Attempt 2** (`m2-run4-spectate-arm-2`, `state/logs/m2-run4-spectate-arm-2-20260924-073202.log`), identical command, fresh instance after full cleanup: failed at bring-up with the #59 pattern — `CloneError: emulator-5556 never became ready: the bridge is not answering on emulator-5556: bridge closed the stream`, after 2 relaunch attempts each logging `the game lost its activity while starting; re-issuing the launcher intent`. Time of failure: ~2026-09-24 07:37:39 UTC (stage started 07:32:02, wall 00:05:37). `state/logs/tower-rl-emulator-emulator-5556.log` tail for this window shows no ColorBuffer/segfault/X-connection/FATAL lines — a normal-looking boot (`Boot completed in 15972 ms`) followed by the game failing to hold its activity; only routine `stop: Not implemented` / Vulkan swapchain WARNING/ERROR lines from teardown, nothing indicating a host GPU crash this time. No logcat was captured for either attempt (not attached in advance; the failures were not anticipated). `run_stage.sh` reported `exit 1, cleanup ok, instances 1/1 cleaned`, host verified clean (no qemu process, no adb device) after teardown.

No recording produced. Stopping per the one-retry rule; not attempting a third run without direction.

Lead, 2026-09-24: two attempts failed, so no further spectate device attempts until a desk diagnosis is done.
- Candidate cause for attempt 1 (my packet error): I asked for frame_game_ms 100. spectate.py is designed for 60 Hz real time, which is the 16.667 ms per frame it used when the run-3 diag-solo recording succeeded on Sep 20. Unconfirmed.
- Attempt 2 is the original bring-up pattern with no crash lines; no logcat was captured.
- A specialist is doing the desk diagnosis now. Device time goes to #27 first.

Lead finding, 2026-09-24 (desk diagnosis; details in scratchpad spectate-59-diagnosis.md):
- Attempt 1 most likely failed because the emulator window drops to about 1 fps when nobody is watching the screen (the display path the emulator window draws through slows to about 1 Hz when the window is hidden). frame_game_ms is not the cause. Sep 20's windowed run at midday was exactly real time; all the failures happened when the desk was unattended.
- The cause of the bring-up game deaths is unknown (Play update window vs frame starvation) because no logcat was captured.
Fix being implemented (tier B):
- spectate pins frame_game_ms to 1000/60 and records it;
- a --no-window option for unattended recording;
- run_stage.sh dumps logcat per serial on failure.
The lavapipe snapshot is deferred until logcat shows Play is the killer. The check is a headless spectate --record after the #27 stage 3 fleet test.

Lead, 2026-09-24: fix is on branch spectate-headless at 9b24179, with 906 tests passing and ruff and mypy clean. The tier B review approved it. The logcat dump is bounded at 20 s per serial; I accept that, since it only happens on failure. The merge waits until the #27 stage 3 device run is finished. After that: a headless --no-window --record of the run-4 arm, which is the device check.

Run-4 arm recorded headless successfully, per the landed spectate fix (2393ed2).

- Command: `scripts/spectate.py --policy checkpoint:.../checkpoint-gs0240594.pt --episodes 1 --no-window --no-panel --record m2-run4-arm.mp4 --upgrade-availability all`, under `run_stage.sh`, default bridge build (no `TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR`), `frame_game_ms` pinned to 16.667 by spectate itself.
- First attempt refused before bring-up (`upgrade_availability differs: 'all' vs 'image'`): the checkpoint was trained under `--upgrade-availability all` (confirmed in its manifest/summary), so spectate's `image` default couldn't play it. Not a device failure — no instance was ever brought up, host verified clean immediately. Re-ran with `--upgrade-availability all`.
- Second attempt: bring-up, episode, and teardown all succeeded. Stage exit 0, cleanup ok, host verified clean afterward.
- Episode ended at wave 11 (game_over), 99 decisions recorded.
- Output: `state/recordings/m2-run4-arm-{000,001,002}.mp4` (3 chunks, screenrecord's 180s limit), decisions at `state/recordings/m2-run4-arm.decisions.jsonl`.
- Rendered panel: `state/recordings/m2-run4-arm-panel.mp4`, 920x640, duration 418.4s (ffprobe). Extracted frame at t=45s confirms the decision panel (episode/decision counter, stats, last-12-decisions list) is composited beside the game view as intended.

No recording files committed, per repo policy. Closing #59: the spectate real-time/headless fix is landed and validated end-to-end against a real checkpoint.

items.title: Speed: frame_game_ms 100 under the M2 setup (M2 runs silently used 16.667) — equivalence and fleet throughput
items.body:
Scout finding: every M2 run (M2-E001 onward, including run 3) trained and evaluated at frame_game_ms=16.667, the CadenceConfig / add_cadence_arguments default, although M1B-E018 (commit 705836e) adopted 100 and M1B-E038 validated 100 (powered, round-clock fidelity) and rejected 150/200. The M2 pre-registrations never pinned the value, so the default rode through silently. 16.667 has no powered fidelity evidence. The fleet is vsync-bound (~118 fps), so game-s per wall-s scales with frame_game_ms: 100 could be up to ~6x faster per actor.

M2-S001: frame_game_ms 100 under the M2 setup — equivalence + throughput. Design pre-registered in docs/experiments.md before running.

comments.text:
M2-S001 run, 2026-09-23. Verdict: **equivalent, throughput inconclusive against the bar as pre-registered — no automatic GO.**

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

items.title: Stage failure evidence: per-actor failure timestamps, pre-stage host snapshot with memory, emulator crash lines surfaced
items.body:
M2-P004's eval stage lost 5/7 emulators to a host gfxstream renderer crash. Diagnosis took three rounds because of three observability gaps:

1. `scripts/run_actors.py` prints actor failures only in its final summary, so all failures carry the summary's timestamp instead of the moment each actor's exception was caught. Fix: log each actor's exception at catch time (via `timestamped_print`), with actor index, serial and exception type/message.

2. `scripts/run_stage.sh` `log_host_load` — verify it takes one snapshot right after preflight (before the stage command starts) and one at finish; add memory to it (`free -m` one-liner + swap used), guarded `|| true` (teardown must never abort).

3. On stage failure (non-zero exit), `run_stage.sh` should print, per instance, the last matching lines of that instance's emulator log (`state/logs/tower-rl-emulator-emulator-<port>.log`) for patterns `ColorBuffer|segfault|X connection|FATAL|ERROR` (tail <= 5 matching lines each), guarded `|| true`.

comments.text: Landed cc0ea4d merged as aefc294; gates pytest=0 (902 passed), ruff=0, mypy=0.

items.title: M2-P005: run-5 arm beats the run-4 arm (18.14) on the default-build evaluation
items.body:
Objective: better performance. Recipe: run 4's recipe (DER-rate gradient steps, BBF n-step anneal, frame_game_ms 100) with 2x the decision budget, render-interval-16 used for training collection only (#27, 6683750), and kill bars derived from run 4's near-greedy curve.

Done-condition: the run-5 arm evaluated on the DEFAULT build (n=105, run 4's eval procedure) beats the run-4 arm, i.e. the 95% bootstrap CI lower bound of the difference is > 0. Otherwise the result is recorded as not better. Either outcome is recorded in docs/experiments.md M2-P005 (pre-registered before launch).

comments.text:
**M2-P005 result: NOT BETTER.** Pre-registered `docs/experiments.md` (`fe17cdd`), results recorded (`30a6193`).

Training stage (`m2-run5-train-seed0`, `render-interval-16` collection build, budget 480,000 game-s = 2x run 4's): kill bar **K2 fired** at fleet decision 24,355 (160,108 game-seconds spent, 33.4% of budget) — near-greedy window mean over (8000,24328] decisions was 10.344 against the bar of 10.6 (derived from run 4's own curve at the same window via `round(mean - 3.5*SE, 1)`, the same method M2-P004 used from run 3's curve). K1 passed (10.102 vs 9.2). Run stopped itself after period 2 only.

Arm = the only eligible checkpoint, `checkpoint-gs0120026.pt` (period 2, sha256 `2c55b4a0...50fdde`→`2c55b4a0501c276a10d9dab2d404f37d98203ea983b375dfe1b871984fb7dbc4`), evaluated on the default bridge build per the task packet's instruction that a kill-bar stop still gets an arm evaluation.

Evaluation (default build, n=105, 7/7 actors, 0 invalid, no retry needed): mean 7.657 (sd 1.770).

- vs run-4 arm (18.143, n=105): **-10.486 [-11.267, -9.686]** — **NOT BETTER**.
- vs scripted-all (6.105): +1.552 [+1.200, +1.886] — beats scripted.
- vs random-all (3.556): +4.102 [+3.640, +4.552] — beats random.

This is read as the kill bar doing its designed job (stopping a run tracking below the reference run's own early trajectory at matched decisions), not as evidence against the 2x-budget or `render-interval-16` changes themselves — the run never got past period 2, well short of where either change could compound. Full detail, including the kill-bar derivation reproduction and throughput numbers, in `docs/experiments.md` under `M2-P005`.

Host left clean (no qemu, no adb device) after both stages. Board item left as-is per instructions (only closed/moved to Done on a BETTER verdict).

Lead finding, 2026-09-24 (on 30a6193):
- Run 5 was stopped by kill bar K2 at 33% of its budget, and its early (period-2) checkpoint scored 7.66 on the default build. Comparing that with run 4's FINAL arm says nothing about the recipe.
- The real finding is per decision: run 5 learned slower than run 4. Its near-greedy mean at 24k decisions was 10.34, against a bar of 10.6.
- Warning sign: near-greedy on the render-interval-16 build was 10.3, but the greedy eval on the default build was 7.66. Stage 3 (#27) tested only the scripted policy.
Diagnostic pre-registered next:
- H1: render-off changes the game for a learned policy. Test: evaluate the run-4 arm on the render-interval-16 build, n=35, against 18.14 with an equivalence margin of ±2.0.
- H2: budget-scaled schedules.
- H3: seed variance, because the kill-bar SE is within-run noise only.
Render-off for training is suspended until H1 is settled.

**M2-P005 diagnostic result: build FAITHFUL for a trained policy; root cause narrowed, not fully resolved.** Pre-registered `cd840f3`, results `8741245`.

**(a) Schedules vs budget.** Epsilon-anneal (8000 decisions) and the n-step anneal (10,000 gradient steps) are both absolute — identical at matched decisions between run 4 and run 5. Beta (PER importance exponent) **is** a fraction-of-budget schedule (missed in M2-P005's own pre-registration) — beta 0.698 (run 4) vs 0.600 (run 5) at matched decision ~24k — but `priority_alpha=0.0` in both runs, so beta's practical effect on the gradient should be negligible.

**(b) Run 4's window mean, same (8000,24328] decisions:** 11.158 (sd 1.627, SE 0.152, n=114) vs run 5's 10.344 — a 0.814-wave gap, ~5.4x run 4's own SE.

**(c) Game-s/decision, matched decision range (8000→~24,330]:** run 4 4.423, run 5 6.975 — **1.58x**. This is policy-specific: #27 stage 3 found decisions/wave unaffected by the build for the *scripted* policy. Strongest desk signal, points at H1, though confounded with policy strength (stronger play naturally spends more game-time before an episode ends).

**(d) `advances_cut_short`, matched range:** run 4 20.1% (44/219), run 5 23.1% (81/351) — a much smaller gap than the uncorrected whole-run comparison in the first write-up implied (that comparison is corrected in the doc).

**Device stage:** run 4's arm (`checkpoint-gs0240594.pt`) evaluated on `render-interval-16`, n=35, 35/35 valid, no retry needed. Mean 17.857 (sd 4.008) vs run 4's own default-build 18.143 (n=105): bootstrap 95% CI **−0.286 [−1.800, +1.190]**, entirely inside ±2.0 → **FAITHFUL**.

**Net:** M2-P005's NOT BETTER verdict is unchanged. The build itself is faithful for a trained, greedy policy, which weakens H1 at evaluation time but doesn't rule out a narrower version affecting near-greedy *collection* with exploration noise on a mid-training network — where (c)'s effect was actually measured. H2's mechanism (beta) is real but inert given alpha=0. H3 (seed variance) is neither confirmed nor excluded by this diagnostic (no second seed run). Full detail in `docs/experiments.md` under "M2-P005 diagnostic."

Host clean after the device stage (no qemu, no adb device). Board item left open, unchanged.

Lead, 2026-09-24: closing as answered, NOT BETTER (30a6193; diagnostic cd840f3, 8741245, d3c92a4).
- H1 (render-off) is rejected. The run-4 arm scores −0.29 [−1.80, +1.19] on the render-interval-16 build. For the same policy, the B/A ratio of game-s per decision is 1.039 [0.954, 1.140].
- H2 (beta scales with the budget) is present but inert, because alpha is 0.
- H3 (seed variance) remains the likely explanation for the 0.81-wave gap per decision. The kill-bar margin (3.5 × within-run SE) ignores variance between runs, which is a design defect.
- Second defect: a game-seconds budget does not fix the amount of learning. The '2×' budget would have reached only about 1.21× run 4's decisions.
Any successor run budgets in decisions and uses a collapse-only kill rule.
