items.title: M2-P006: run-5b arm (2x run-4 decisions) beats the run-4 arm (18.14) on the default-build evaluation
items.body:
Successor to #64 (closed NOT BETTER; its diagnostic found two design defects: a game-seconds budget and a within-run-SE kill bar).
Recipe: run 4's hyperparameters, render-interval-16 for training collection (shown faithful: run-4 arm -0.29 [-1.80, +1.19]), budget = 2x run 4's decisions (about 120.7k), collapse-only kill bars (run 4's bars: 12000:8000:8.6 and 26262:8000:10.2), and checkpoints every 15,000 game-s (feeds #65). Approved by the developer 2026-09-24; about 4-4.5 h.
Done-condition: the run-5b arm evaluated on the DEFAULT build (n=105) has a 95% bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 against 18.143. Otherwise it is recorded NOT BETTER and closed with the reason.

comments.text: Lead finding, 2026-09-24: the launch was stopped before any device work because train.py only budgets in game-seconds. I decided to add --budget-decisions, mutually exclusive with --budget-game-seconds; the default is unchanged. Tier B, on branch decision-budget. I am also checking whether arm selection is coupled to the checkpoint cadence. Launch follows review and landing.

Blocked on #68. The developer decided on one progress unit, decisions, replacing the game-seconds axis rather than adding a second one. Run 5b launches once #68 lands, with --budget-decisions 120712 --checkpoint-every-decisions 5000 and 15,000-decision selection periods.

Unblocked: #68 landed (3b12cd5). Next: simplify batch 1 (#69) is rebased, reviewed and landed first, so nothing merges during the device run. Then M2-P006 is pre-registered and run 5b launches with --budget-decisions 120712 --checkpoint-every-decisions 5000.

M2-P006 pre-registration drafted; not committed yet. The kill-bar fields are still fleet-cumulative decisions under #68, so 12000:8000:8.6 and 26262:8000:10.2 are unchanged. Lead decisions:
- If the 5 h cap is hit before the budget is spent, the stage stops cleanly, keeping its checkpoints, and is resumed from latest.pt to finish the budget. Only the completed budget gets a verdict.
- A kill-bar stop means no evaluation.
- Power at n=105: the minimum detectable difference at 80% power is about 1.45 waves.
The run launches after simplify batch 1 (#69) lands.

M2-P006 pre-registered in 88a0fc4 (pushed). Run 5b training launched 2026-09-24T11:45:01+02:00 under run_stage.sh (stage m2-run5b-train-seed0) with TOWER_BRIDGE_BUILD_DIR=render-interval-16 for training only, --budget-decisions 120712, --checkpoint-every-decisions 5000, --selection-period-decisions 15000, and the collapse-only kill bars. Preflight clean. 5 h wall cap; projected about 4.1 h.

M2-P006 run 5b: **KILLED, no evaluation.**

Pre-registered (88a0fc4), launched under `run_stage.sh` (`m2-run5b-train-seed0`, `render-interval-16` collection), then stopped by kill bar K1 (`12000:8000:8.6`) at 12,223 decisions: near-greedy mean final wave over (8000, 12000] was 8.409 (66 episodes), below 8.6. K2 never reached, no selection period closed. Training wall ≈24.4 min; stage wall 00:33:15, well inside the 5h cap. Host cleanup verified (no qemu, empty `adb devices`).

Per the pre-registration's arm-selection rule, a killed run's arm is not evaluated — no comparison to run 4 (18.143) is produced by this run. Full results in `docs/experiments.md` (41aca74). Board item not moved; awaiting the Lead's call on retry/next step.

Run 5b was killed by K1 at 12,223 decisions: near-greedy mean 8.409 over (8000,12000] (66 episodes) against the 8.6 bar. There is no evaluation, per the pre-registration. Cleanup verified; results recorded in 41aca74. This was the first device run on the #68 and #69 code, so before any retry a timeboxed (30 min) read-only diagnosis is testing three explanations: a regression from the refactor; schedules that anneal as a fraction of the budget, so a 2x budget explores more early on, which departs from DQN, Rainbow and DER's fixed-step annealing; and noise within the between-run spread. No relaunch until then.

Diagnosis of the run-5b K1 kill (specialist, read-only; detail in the session scratchpad):
- A regression is ruled out. exploration, _learn, warm-up, the n-step anneal, the target EMA and the learning rate are unchanged by #68, and #69 touches no training code. At matched decisions, gradient steps per decision are 0.774 / 0.779 / 0.781 (runs 4 / 5 / 5b), and loss and value-fit are within the run 4–5 range.
- The schedules are ruled out. epsilon uses a fixed 8,000-decision horizon, matching published practice. beta is the only budget-fraction schedule and has no effect at priority_alpha=0.
- Run-to-run variance is the supported explanation. (8k,12k] near-greedy means: run 4 9.87±0.23, run 5 10.02±0.13, run 5b 8.32±0.10, run 3 9.24±0.16. All used seed 0 and still diverged, because emulator timing is nondeterministic. Run 5b was not behind at (4k,8k], at 6.78.
Lead decisions:
1. Defect: the 8.6 bar was not collapse-only. It sits 2.5 waves above the scripted baseline (6.105), so it rejected a healthy run.
2. Retry as M2-P006b: unchanged recipe, seed 1, with the only kill bars at the scripted floor (--kill-bar 12000:8000:6.1 --kill-bar 26262:8000:6.1).
3. The between-run spread is now the main uncertainty for every comparison in this benchmark. The multi-run design goes to the developer.

M2-P006b pre-registered in b452ac1 (pushed), and the diagnosis appended to the M2-P006 Results. Training launched 2026-09-24T12:26:11+02:00 under run_stage.sh (stage m2-run5b-retry-seed1) with --seed 1 (recorded in the manifest), render-interval-16 for training only, and scripted-floor kill bars 12000:8000:6.1 and 26262:8000:6.1. Preflight clean. 5 h cap.
Developer decision: one run per learner (Option B). M2-P006b's verdict stays a comparison of two policies, this run's arm against run 4's arm, as pre-registered.

M2-P006b run 5b retry (seed 1, scripted-floor kill bars): **WORSE than run 4's arm.**

Both kill bars passed by a wide margin (K1 mean 10.732 vs 6.1 floor; K2 mean 11.24 vs 6.1 floor) — budget completed cleanly, 121,781 decisions, 8 selection periods. Arm by §9.2b: `checkpoint-d0105078.pt` (period 7 close, near-greedy mean 15.679). Evaluated on the default build, n=105: mean 15.590, sd 3.830.

`bootstrap_difference` (seed 0, 10,000 resamples):
- vs run 4 (18.143, n=105): **−2.552 [−3.552, −1.514]** → **WORSE**
- vs scripted (6.105, n=105): +9.486 [+8.762, +10.200] — beats scripted
- vs random (3.556, n=90): +12.035 [+11.251, +12.814] — beats random

Per this entry's own caveat: this compares two individual trained policies, not the recipe against itself — run-to-run spread is not measured, consistent with `M2-P006`'s diagnosis that runs 4/5/5b already diverge under matched decisions with a healthy, non-collapsed learner throughout. Full results in `docs/experiments.md` (7b480f9). Host cleanup verified clean throughout. Board item not moved — awaiting the Lead's call on next steps.

Done: the pre-registered experiment ran to a verdict. M2-P006b (seed 1) completed 121,781 decisions. The arm, checkpoint-d0105078, scored 15.590 (n=105, default build), WORSE than run 4's arm by −2.552 [−3.552, −1.514]. It beats scripted by +9.486 and random by +12.035. Results are in 7b480f9 and the Lead reading in 5835e6a: the curves are identical to 45k decisions and diverge at 45–60k, after which run 5b plateaus at about 15.5, so run-to-run divergence is the supported explanation and render-interval-16 stays the training build. task.md §1.1 now records one run per learner, fixed by pre-registration.

items.title: Training progress is measured in decisions only: budget, checkpoint cadence, selection periods, schedules and reports
items.body:
Developer decision, 2026-09-24: one unit of progress, independent of game speed, so that runs and learners are comparable. Decisions are that unit. game-seconds and wall time are reported as secondary statistics, never as the budget. The game-seconds progress machinery is removed rather than kept alongside. Old run records stay readable. Motivation: the M2-P005 diagnostic showed a game-seconds budget does not fix the amount of learning.
Done-condition: train.py and TrainingRun take only a decision budget and a decision checkpoint cadence; arm selection keeps run 4's semantics expressed in decisions; tests, ruff and mypy are green; solution.md and architecture.md are reconciled; it lands on main.

comments.text: The implementation is on branch decision-unit at feb5731 (worktree, not merged): 21 files, +1014/-975. Gates are green (pytest 911 passed, ruff 0, mypy 0). The game-time flags, the blocks loop, budget_overshoot and episode_budget are removed; checkpoints are named checkpoint-d<decisions>, and old checkpoint-gs files still load. The tier C review is in progress. Open questions for that review: whether the arm rule matches run 4 and run 5, including the no-arm-on-kill case; whether the unrequested select_arm() duplicates select_checkpoint.py; whether --budget-decisions should be required; and whether game-time-era checkpoints should be refused on resume.

The tier C review accepted it with fixes; the core is verified correct (budget, crossings, beta, resume arithmetic, old readers). Lead decisions, now being applied:
- Checkpoint format 4; resuming anything older is refused, while old files still load for evaluation.
- --budget-decisions is required, with no default.
- The unrequested select_arm/_arm is deleted, leaving one arm rule, stated as text in solution.md §9.2b (best selection period among periods 2 and later, ties to the earlier period). A kill-bar stop doesn't change which checkpoint is the arm; the pre-registration decides whether it is evaluated.
- advance() is folded into run() if that is simpler.
- Doc and comment corrections.
Finding: select_checkpoint.py implements a different, older rule (greedy-evaluation IQM) that runs 3 to 5 did not use. It is kept as a checkpoint-evaluation tool, not as the M2 arm rule.
Landed in merge 3b12cd5 on main, pushed. Gates on the merged main: pytest 911 passed, ruff 0, mypy 0. The public scan is clean. HEAD == origin/main.

items.title: BBF arm: stacked-dqn with the BBF recipe passes a known-answer check and a paper configuration check, ready for a game run
items.body:
Sub-item of #58 (Arm 1). Developer approved the start on 2026-09-24.
Done-condition: the BBF recipe is built into stacked-dqn as configuration of the one existing training path, not a second learner. The same code path passes a known-answer check against a published result on a cheap standard task. Every hyperparameter is checked against the BBF paper (Schwarzer et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.19452) and the official code, and every deviation is justified in docs/solution.md. No device time until this is done; the game run is pre-registered separately.
Motivation: the run-5b curve plateaued at about 15.5 from 45k to 121k decisions (M2-P006b); BBF's resets target loss of plasticity. The developer notes the plateau may also be natural, because the account has no permanent upgrades. Run 4's greedy arm reached 18.1 on the same account state, however, so 15.5 is not the account's ceiling.

comments.text:
Design settled (specialist design in the session scratchpad bbf-design.md; primary sources: arXiv 2305.19452, BBF.gin, spr_agent.py). Lead decisions:
- BBF is configuration fields on StackedDqnConfig, one training path; the defaults keep run 4's recipe exactly.
- Arm values: 4x width; 1 update per decision (2 if #72 allows); a shrink-and-perturb reset every 40k gradient steps (0.5/0.5 on the trunk; fresh core, heads and target; AdamW state cleared for reset layers only), with no reset in the last 40k; n 10→3 and gamma 0.97→0.997 over 10k steps per cycle; target EMA 0.005; AdamW lr 1e-4, wd 0.1 (skipping 1-D params), eps 1.5e-4; epsilon annealed to 0.
- Accepted deviations, to be named in the arm's label and in solution.md: no SPR (the paper's ablation puts it at about 6% IQM at ratio 8, while an action-conditioned model over 61 masked actions is large); no C51 (stacked-dqn has no distributional head); the replay ratio is 1–2 rather than 8 (per the paper's Fig. 6, BBF keeps its lead at ratios 1–2). The arm is labelled 'stacked-dqn + BBF recipe (no SPR, no C51)'.
- Known-answer gate: layer A is unit tests of each BBF component against fixtures from the official code; layer B is MinAtar (Young & Tian 2019), 2 games x 3 seeds, through the real backbone, with pass bands pre-registered from the published curves. A tests BBF's additions; B tests the shared learner. Both are required.
- Still open, and resolved in the configuration check: the BBF replay prioritisation compared with our sequence-level PER.
- Early-stop patience must span a reset cycle.
Order: #72 (learner speed) → BBF config → MinAtar harness (built in parallel, run after #72) → configuration-check document.

Finding and Lead decision on the known-answer gate. MinAtar cannot run through the real learner. The network is a domain row-scorer (action_count == row_count + 1, 42 scalars plus 60×9 rows, a 61-action mask), and Actor and TrainingRun are typed on the game's environment and waves. Making the network shape-generic would add complexity only to host a foreign benchmark. Decision: layer B is an ANALYTIC known-answer check. It is a small synthetic run in the game's own vocabulary under the real environment, actor, TrainingRun, replay and backbone, with Q* solved exactly by dynamic programming. It passes when the greedy policy is optimal on all reachable states and |Q−Q*| is within a stated tolerance. It must provably fail on at least 4 injected bugs (bootstrap not cut at terminals, n-step gamma off by one, mask ignored in the target max, reward error). A published-benchmark reproduction still applies to the external learners (DreamerV3, EfficientZero V2), which bring their own networks.

Retired by developer decision (2026-09-24): 'Just do the correct implementation and start training. We don't have to do the check.' The known-answer gate (the analytic MDP, and MinAtar before it) is dropped for BBF. The implementation still gets unit tests of each component against values from the official code, and the configuration is still checked against the paper, with deviations documented. The work continues as a single item that implements BBF and trains it.

Partial result recorded before the stop (not committed; the files were deleted). The synthetic known-answer run through the real path learned the OPTIMAL greedy policy at all 34 decisions. max |Q−Q*| levelled off at 0.65–0.70 (Q* scale 4.69), all of it underestimation on exploratory branches. That is the bias expected from uncorrected n-step returns (n=3) on off-policy replay, not evidence of a bug; an exact Q match would have needed n=1.

items.title: The learner trains on the GPU (RTX 4090) by default; CPU-saved checkpoints still load
items.body: Developer direction (2026-09-24): the host has an RTX 4090 and it should be used by default. Training has been learner-bound at about 120 ms per synchronous gradient step (M2-P005/M2-P006; about 0.78 gradient steps per decision). Done-condition: device selection defaults to CUDA when available; old checkpoints load; tests pass; and the measured gradient-step time and effective replay ratio on the GPU are recorded in docs/experiments.md. Note: a faster learner raises the effective replay ratio relative to run 4's measured ~0.78, which is a recipe change to state explicitly. The design comes from the #70 specialist (package 1).

comments.text:
Finding (specialist, #70 design): the premise is wrong. Training already runs on the 4090: train.py:1178 selects cuda, run 5b's manifest records device cuda, the actors' acting copies are on the same GPU, and checkpoints load with map_location=cpu.
- Measured learner step: 61 ms in run 5b and 77 ms in run 4, about 90% of it CPU-side Python overhead. The microbenchmark on an idle 4090 gives 35 ms: collate 12 ms, learn 22.5 ms, of which the n_step_targets Python loop is 17.6 ms.
- The replay ratio is enforced exactly (0.962 in run 4, 0.982 in run 5b, against 1.0 configured); the earlier 0.78 figure was warm-up-weighted. So a faster learner changes wall time and actor waiting (12% of actor time), not the recipe.
The earlier Lead claims of a ~120 ms step and 0.78 steps per decision were wrong. They are being corrected in docs/experiments.md, and this item closes once that is recorded. The speed-up itself is a new item.

Done: verified that the condition already held before this item. Both run manifests record device cuda, train.py selects cuda by default, and checkpoints load with map_location=cpu. The profile is recorded in 42dfc3f (docs/experiments.md 'Learner profile (2026-09-24)'): replay ratio 0.962 in run 4 (58,046/60,356) and 0.982 in run 5b (119,589/121,781); step time 61–77 ms, mostly Python overhead. The old ~120 ms and 0.78 figures are annotated as corrected. The speed-up continues in #72.

items.title: Wave 20–21 wall: can in-run cash alone beat it, or does it need permanent upgrades?
items.body:
Every run and learner so far: 0 of 255 arrivals at wave 20 passed wave 21, and no episode reached wave 22. We have no game-state data past wave 11 (#75 diagnosis).

Hypotheses:
- **H1, policy or training:** the cash earned by wave 20, spent well, can beat the wave-20 boss. The policy banks cash; median cash at wave-20 entry is about 76.
- **H2, structural:** even the best spending of all in-run cash cannot beat it at this account's base stats, so only permanent upgrades could.

Done when:
- per-decision state is recorded through death at wave 20–21 for the run-4 arm;
- a feasibility bound supporting H1 or H2 is recorded in experiments.md.

Refs #58

comments.text:
Recording map, from the scout.
- scripts/spectate.py records per-decision tower stats, cash, wave base enemy HP and damage, and the boss flags.
- It does NOT record boss HP, upgrade effect magnitudes, or the full per-slot upgrade table (only the acted-on row).
- There is no interest mechanic among the observed fields.
- An episode to wave 20 takes about 11–12 min of real time.

A specialist is now working out how far existing data gets toward a feasibility bound, and what the minimal discriminating device stage would be.

Specialist analysis of existing data. The scripts are in the session scratchpad, wall80-*.py.

Facts:
- The wall is one event starting at wave 20. All 181 eval arrivals at wave 20 died 1.5–58 s after wave 20 started.
- Death timing differs from the wave-10 boss gate: wave-20 deaths have a median of 22.7 s; wave-10 boss deaths come 64–75 s in. Reading this as ordinary enemies out-scaling defence rather than the boss is an inference.
- Survival past wave-20 start rises continuously with policy strength (Spearman 0.67 with purchases). No threshold appears in the data.
- Growth fitted over waves 1–11 cannot pin wave-20 enemy stats: equally good fits disagree by up to 2.6×.
- With `--upgrade-availability all`, all 48 rows are available in-run, including Thorn Damage, Interest / Wave and the Enemy Attack and Health Level Skip rows. The run-4 arm's most-bought row by wave 11 was Defense Absolute.

Verdict:
- Narrow H1 (spend the ~76 banked cash) is unlikely: that buys about one level.
- Broad H1 vs H2 (reallocate all income from wave ~12 on) is undecided from existing data.
- More training alone is unlikely to break the wall: both M3 curves are flat over 60k–120k decisions, and 0 of 5,398 training episodes passed.

Next stage, the lead's decision:
- Widen the per-wave eval record: live fields, the row table and purchases.
- Add an eval-only handoff policy: the checkpoint plays until wave N, then a scripted rule buys the cheapest affordable upgrade in its set.
- Arms: the run-4 arm as control, handoff@12:turtle (Defense Absolute plus Thorn Damage, the developer's strategy), and handoff@12:damage.
- 35 episodes per arm.
- Any episode reaching wave 22 or later falsifies H2. If both handoff arms fail, the widened logs give a needed-vs-available bound.

Developer decision: no scripted turtle or handoff arm. Turtle (Defense Absolute plus Thorns) is the established Tier-1 strategy and is known to work. The implementer has been stopped. The question now is why the learners do not find it.

Workshop research (specialist, web sources, mostly game-vault wiki from Oct 2024 to Jul 2025, which predates 29.0.3).

- A Workshop level becomes the starting level of that row in every run. The in-run price for the next level is unchanged, and the cap is shared: our in-run max levels match the wiki's Workshop maxes (Thorn 99, Defense % 99, Defense Absolute 5000).
- Workshop coins mainly **unlock rows** (Defense 75, Thorns 500, Multishot 400 … Level Skip 1B). `--upgrade-availability all` already gives the agent every row, far more than a real fresh account, so the only thing the harness lacks is starting levels.
- 53 coins buys one level of a free row, worth about 5–10 in-run cash against the ~1,200–1,600 earned by wave 20. Negligible.
- A Workshop build that would matter, e.g. Defense Absolute ~50 plus Thorns 11%, costs thousands of coins; this is an inference.
- The likely wall mechanism (sourced): enemy damage grows 1.04× per hit landed (heat-up), and bosses have 20× HP. No source says a zero-Workshop account cannot pass wave 20.

Verdict: uncertain, leaning **the Workshop is not needed**. Spending the 53 coins would change nothing. The wall is most likely in-run strategy and cash allocation against boss heat-up.

Developer direction: investigate why the learners do not find a winning build. The areas are reward, exploration, and planning horizon or credit assignment. A specialist is running the analysis offline on existing runs, evaluation records and checkpoints, with no device use. Output: ranked causes with evidence, plus the cheapest discriminating experiment.

Learner diagnosis (specialist, offline; details in the scratchpad, wall80-diag-*).

Corrections to the premises (facts):
- Decisions per wave are about 2–4 early but **16–21 late**; waiting while saving cash creates extra stops.
- **The M3 learners never reach wave 20**: 0 of 105 evals each, maxima 19 and 17. They die at the wave-10 boss (deaths at 11–12) and at 15–16. Only the older run-3/4/5b policies reach the wave-20 wall.

Ranked causes:
1. **No learning signal past the boss.** 0 of 255 arrivals passed, and the exploring actors die before wave 20: actor 0 at ε=0.4 reaches at most wave 11–12. Uniform per-decision dithering spends the cash a committed build needs. P(3 or more extra buys of one row, waves 12–20) is at most 0.04.
2. **The stacked-dqn discount is per decision, not per unit of game time.** γ=0.99 at about 20 decisions per wave gives a horizon of about 5 waves late in an episode. The +1 for passing the boss is weighted 0.13 at wave 12, below the TD noise of 0.20. This deviates from semi-MDP practice (Bradtke & Duff 1995; Sutton, Precup & Singh 1999), and long-horizon agents use γ=0.997. DreamerV3 (γ=0.997) is fine on this point.
3. Open precondition: whether any in-run build passes wave 20 on the 53-coin baseline.
4. Reward v1 carries no graded signal inside a boss wave; potential-based shaping (Ng et al. 1999) would restore one.
5. Dreamer spends immediately, with cash about 5 at every wave; it never saves.
6. Observability is adequate, with minor gaps: wave enters only as log(wave), heat-up is unobserved, and row levels are unscaled.

The specialist proposed scripted takeover arms (E1). They are **not adopted**: the developer has ruled that the agent must discover builds itself, with no scripted builds. The candidates are learning-side changes, pending the developer's choice.

The Workshop question is deferred. It is only decidable once a learner can plan across boss intervals and explore in committed ways. The developer has chosen learning-side fixes, guided by published practice, starting with #81 (semi-MDP discount). This item stays open, moved to Backlog; its done-condition (a feasibility bound) is not met.

Developer (2026-09-25): a small amount of Workshop help to break the plateau mathematically is acceptable (the account has no Lab research and no active cards). Hypothesis: the economy rows (cash bonus, cash per wave) alone break it, and the agent then learns the right in-run upgrades. A specialist is researching the minimal Workshop set and its coin cost. No purchase until a concrete plan is approved.

Developer's own play (2026-09-25): with Workshop, active cards and Lab, Tier 1 plateaued at about wave 1000. That is the ceiling for a strong account; a Workshop-only account is expected to plateau lower.

Workshop research (specialist, 2026-09-25; working files ws-*.py/txt in the session scratchpad):
- The enemy damage formula (towerstats, v29) matches our HUD readings for waves 1–11 exactly. The HP formula matches within 0.03% with exponent 2.08.

items.title: stacked-dqn: discount by game time (semi-MDP) instead of per decision
items.body:
From the #80 diagnosis: stacked-dqn applies γ=0.99 per decision, and decisions are event-driven. Late in an episode there are 16–21 per wave, so the effective horizon is only about 5 waves and shrinks further when the policy saves cash. Standard practice for variable-duration actions is to discount by elapsed time, γ^Δt (Bradtke & Duff 1995; Sutton, Precup & Singh 1999).

Plan:
1. Design, grounded in literature: the choice of per-second γ, n-step composition with a variable Δt, the target-network and PER interplay, and what changes in replay.
2. Implement.
3. Tier C review.
4. Pre-registered comparison against stacked-dqn M3-P001, with the seed count set per Agarwal et al. 2021. Multi-hour device runs need developer approval.

This is change A of three; the next candidates are potential-based shaping (Ng et al. 1999) and temporally-extended ε (Dabney et al. 2021).

Refs #80

comments.text: Developer decision: one seed per arm. Each comparison is a single pre-registered run per setting and is labelled "single run". Within-run signals serve as supporting evidence.

The design is settled; the full spec is semi-mdp-design.md in the session scratchpad.

Design:
- Per-transition discount d = γ_s^Δt, using the `game_ms` already measured. Reward is credited at the span's end.
- Purchases take zero game time, so d = 1. Today they cost a factor of 0.99 each, which is about the size of the whole boss signal.
- γ_s = 0.997 per game-second: a 333 s horizon, about 9.5 waves, the shortest that covers the boss interval (Jiang et al. 2015).
- n-step bootstrap uses the product of the ds; `ReplayStep.game_ms` becomes required.
- It ships as the flag `--discount-per-game-second`. DreamerV3 is untouched.

Lead decisions:
- D1: adopt on "theory plus no gross harm".
- D2: reuse M3-P001 as the control (3.3 h of device time).
- D3: add a resume guard for a discount-mode mismatch.
- D4: add an end-of-span counter to the summary.

Pre-registered rule (n=1):
- ADOPT if the run is healthy and the eval mean is at least 11.14.
- Record "suggestive improvement" only if, in addition, the mean exceeds 18.14 or P(reach 20) is at least 0.10, with pre-boss spending up.

The implementation has been dispatched on Opus with tier C review.

Implementation is on the worktree branch worktree-agent-a19d7414a30f547be at eaf3ddb.
- Tests T1–T9 are in place, and flag-off is bit-identical to the old scalar path (T1, 300 batches, zero tolerance).
- The D3 resume guard and the D4 end-of-span counter are in.
- Gates: pytest 0 (984 passed), ruff 0, mypy 0.
- dreamer.py has a one-line call-site change with identical values.

The tier C review is running.

- The D4 counter was removed and the bounded bias is documented in §9.4d.

items.title: stacked-dqn: potential-based reward shaping on game-time survival (change C)
items.body: Waves last a fixed ~35 game-seconds, so time survived is the objective at finer grain. Use potential-based shaping (Ng, Harada & Russell 1999), F = γ^Δt·Φ(s′) − Φ(s), with Φ tied to elapsed wave time and the same discount as #81. This gives the boss wave a graded signal: dying 50 s in scores above dying 5 s in. It follows #81. Refs #80

comments.text: Design (specialist): invariant potential-based shaping with Φ(terminal)=0 cannot grade 'died later in the wave' (Ng 1999 Th.1; Grzes 2017 Eq.3): action gaps at the wall stay 0. Waves are clock-driven (~35 s each, measured), and in-wave time is observed (wave_timer_log, run_state.py:146). Recommended instead: a survival-time reward r̃=(1−d)/(β·35), exact under the #81 discount (Bradtke & Duff 1995). It orders trajectories that end on different waves exactly as reward v1 does, but it is not objective-invariant, so it needs the developer's decision under task.md:304. Awaiting that decision.

Developer decision (2026-09-25): implement the survival-time reward, r̃=(1−d)/(β·35), behind --survival-time-reward. It requires --discount-per-game-second and is off by default. The objective change is accepted and will be stated in task.md and the pre-registration. Review tier C (reward semantics).
Developer (2026-09-25): standing approval to run the M3-P004 single-seed training and evaluation (~2 h) without asking again, once the change is landed and pre-registered.

Cause: /tmp is a tmpfs with usrquota, and ~23 GB of stale repo copies in the session scratchpad filled it. The copies are being removed and training relaunched once as a recorded deviation.

M3-P004 results (0646613, single run): eval 18.270 [17.640, 18.900], n=100 valid, vs M3-P003 17.076. P(≥20) 0.54, P(≥21) 0.02, P(≥22) 0. Mechanism check S2 falsified: in-wave seconds at a wave-20 death were 16.8 vs 18.7. Value-fit 0.796 < 0.8 → DO NOT ADOPT per the pre-registered rule. The wall at 21 holds. Also: value-fit misses 0.8 by the same amount in both M3-P003 and P004, so the threshold itself may need scrutiny. A text correction to a 'first-ever wave 21' claim is pending.

Done. The flag landed at 3360666; M3-P004 was pre-registered in b6a92e2, results are in 0646613 and corrected in 5b76b42. Verdict: DO NOT ADOPT (value-fit 0.796 < 0.8). Eval 18.270; 0 episodes reached wave 22.

items.title: stacked-dqn: temporally-extended exploration (ε-z-greedy, change B)
items.body: Uniform per-decision dithering cannot find multi-wave builds, and the ladder's exploring actors die before wave 12 (#80 diagnosis). Use ε-z-greedy (Dabney, Ostrovski & Barreto, ICLR 2021): repeat the exploratory action for a heavy-tailed duration. It follows #81 and change C. Refs #80

comments.text: Developer (2026-09-25): implement ε-z-greedy if it is a proper, literature-based fix. The goal is for the agent to discover a turtle-like strategy through experience; the developer expects more training to be part of it. Plan: #83 at the standard budget (one change per run), then a separate learner-stability item for the post-peak decline, then a longer-budget run.

Design (specialist, from arXiv 2006.01782 v1, 2026-09-25): --ez-greedy, with μ=2 and n_max=10000 as fixed constants (§4.2, App. B). Duration is counted in decisions; the ε coin is flipped only between options; the action is drawn from the valid set; the Ape-X ladder is kept. Deviations: n=1 counts as plain ε-greedy (per the text rather than Algorithm 1's off-by-one), and a masked option action is replaced by WAIT and resumes when legal. The per-episode options_started and longest_option counters are included so the mechanism can be observed. Implementation dispatched (tier C).
Finding for the post-peak decline (future item): M3-P004 sampled each replay sequence ~336 times, and replay never evicted (2,858/4,096) → suspect primacy bias / plasticity loss (Nikishin 2022; Lyle 2022–23; Fedus 2020).

Developer approved (2026-09-25): after M3-P005's results, add a research-log index at the top of docs/experiments.md. One row per pre-registered experiment (question, change, control, result, verdict, learned), plus a short narrative paragraph. Docs only; done after the device run.

items.title: Scale-up: 1M-decision runs for stacked-dqn (frozen recipe) and DreamerV3 (official defaults)
items.body: Developer approved (2026-09-25): two runs of 1,000,000 decisions each (~16 h each), one after the other, starting after M3-P005. The same budget for both. Checkpoints are evaluated at ~250k, 500k and 1M for the learning curve. An early stop rule is pre-registered for a flat 250k→500k segment. stacked-dqn's recipe is frozen after M3-P005's verdict; DreamerV3 runs with official defaults. Preceded by a fundamentals audit (no premature optimisation) of every non-default choice against its published source.

comments.text: Fundamentals audit (read-only, 2026-09-25; full table in session scratchpad fundamentals-audit.md). Findings for the 1M recipes: (1) DreamerV3 replay capacity defaults to 4096 windows (~131k decisions), which would drop ~87% of a 1M run; official replay.size is 5e6. Proposed: --replay-capacity 40000 (~20 GB RAM). (2) Selection period 15000 is fitted to 120k; proposed 50000 at 1M (~0.23 wave SE per period). (3) stacked-dqn keeps 4096 windows, passed explicitly (FIFO after ~200k, as in DQN). (4) Dreamer train ratio 256 is the atari100k preset; the paper uses 512 at 500k-1M steps. Keep 256 as a compute-forced choice, or use 512 (~22 h learner time). Everything else is sourced (BBF n-step/EMA, Ape-X ladder, Bradtke-Duff discount). Simplify after the runs, not before: the inert PER path at alpha=0, the weight_decay 1e-5 'BBF' claim. Awaiting the developer's decision before freezing the recipes.

Developer decision 2026-09-25: DreamerV3 train ratio 512 for the 1M run (paper Table 2 setting for 500k-1M-step budgets; ~22 h+ learner-bound run accepted). Lead-applied, reversible: Dreamer --replay-capacity 40000, --selection-period-decisions 50000 for both arms, stacked-dqn --replay-capacity 4096 stated explicitly. The code and doc change is dispatched after M3-P005's eval ends (no gates while a device run is live).

2026-09-25: DreamerV3 train_ratio 512 implemented on branch worktree-agent-a0a9eb44920ee70c7 (3fc67ef), sourced to paper Table 2 (proprio 500K / visual 1M steps, replay ratio 512) and the crafter preset (1.1e6 steps, train_ratio 512). Gates pass in the worktree. Research-log index landed as 6c9feb0. Dispatched: land 3fc67ef, pre-register M3-P006 (stacked-dqn, 1M decisions, M3-P005 recipe; changes: 50k selection periods, 25k checkpoints, explicit replay 4096, early stop at 5 periods / 0.2 waves), then run as one continuous stage with a single allowed resume and evaluate at n=105.

M3-P006 (stacked-dqn, 1M budget) done 2026-09-26: early-stopped at 752,118 decisions (period 15; peak at period 10, 500,143). The arm eval is 17.010 (n=104, 95% CI [16.21, 17.81]), P(≥20) 0.50, P(≥21) 0.20, P(≥22) 0. Verdict: 'more training did not cross the wall under this recipe'. Descriptive: one training episode (1791, near-greedy actor) reached wave 22. Lead grep of all of state/ confirms it is the only wave-22+ episode in any record. Commits: 1c95210 (512 merge), f6ad3d1 (pre-reg), 1af730c (results). Next: M3-P007 DreamerV3 1M.

M3-P007 (DreamerV3, 1M) pre-registered in ce9c2e0 and launched 2026-09-26 07:55. Confirmed: the train ratio is enforced synchronously (training.py:1217-1246), train_ratio 512 gives 0.5 gradient steps per decision, and the replay/early-stop/period flags are honoured for dreamerv3. Memory at 1 h: 48 GB available, about 16 GB more replay projected by the end, so no risk. The rate at 1 h was ~23.8k decisions/h, projecting ~42 h against the pre-registered 34 h timebox. Lead decision (reversible): run to the natural end (budget or early stop) and record the overrun as a deviation, unless the developer asks to stop earlier. The finishing worker has been dispatched.

2026-09-26 ~09:12, at the developer's direction: M3-P007 attempt 1 was stopped at ~29k/1M decisions (1h16 in; no arm read, no eval) so the DreamerV3 learner can be optimised first (bf16 autocast, matching the official compute dtype, plus torch.compile; profiled and parity-tested). It will be relaunched under the same M3-P007 ID with an amendment recording the stop and the learner change.

Incident 2026-09-26 09:15: the original M3-P007 launcher misread the deliberate SIGINT stop (exit 130) as a crash and invoked the pre-registered one-allowed resume. It launched stage m3-p007-dreamer-train-resume (pid 1587817) from attempt 1's latest.pt, and the lead's stand-down arrived after that. Its sandbox denied its own attempt to stop the stage, so the stop is escalated to the developer. Treatment: disregarded (mistaken premise), no results read. The optimised relaunch is a fresh attempt. Lesson: a deliberate stop must be signalled to every worker holding a monitor on the stage BEFORE sending SIGINT.

2026-09-26 ~09:38: the developer SIGINTed the stray resume stage (pid 1587817). It exited 130 with 'cleanup ok' after 23:05 wall and ~35.5k decisions. The lead verified 0 qemu processes and empty adb. The run is disregarded, as recorded above.

Dreamer learner speed-up done on branch worktree-agent-ae97ab2e0a270eafd (c77f70d + merge e821a3f): bf16 autocast (RMSNorm in f32) + torch.compile with CUDA graphs on _observe/_imagine_rollout, LaProp foreach, and a sample_index fix (a draw landing on a zero-probability entry moves to the next positive entry; this fixed a NaN policy loss at update 82 under bf16+compile). Idle measurement: 29.5 ms/update vs 101 ms (3.4x). Parity rel diff 3.7e-4 over 300 updates; checkpoint compat verified against attempt 1. Gates: pytest 1036, ruff 0, mypy 0. Risk: ~4 min cold compile on first update (cache now warm). Next: tier-B review -> land -> relaunch M3-P007 fresh with amended pre-registration.

Speed-up review (tier B): approve-with-fixes, nothing blocking. Verified: acting stays f32 and uncompiled; bf16 boundary correct (heads cast to f32 before losses, optimiser state f32); sample_index change is a no-op for exact cumsum and only fixes inexact compiled/bf16 cumsum; learn() is serialized by the Learner lock and syncs before returning, so CUDA-graph buffer reuse is safe; checkpoints load into a plain CPU backbone; solution.md figures are consistent. Accepted risk: ~4 min cold compile blocks actors on a fresh inductor cache (the cache is warm; recorded in the M3-P007 amendment). Landing + fresh M3-P007 relaunch dispatched.

Speed-up landed: merge da7a7bd (pytest 1038 passed, ruff 0, mypy 0; pushed). M3-P007 pre-registration amended in f263b7b (attempt 1 and the stray resume disregarded, learner change, 20 h timebox). Fresh relaunch started 2026-09-26 10:32 with the identical recipe (verified verbatim against attempt 1's launch line): stage m3-p007-dreamer-train-r2, run_stage pid 1821108, training build render-interval-16.

M3-P007 r2 (stage m3-p007-dreamer-train-r2, started 10:32) is an aborted start and is disregarded. emulator-5564's bring-up failed with an adb port clash ('cannot bind listener: Address already in use'), so training ran on 6 actors against the pre-registered 7. It is being stopped at ~4 min and relaunched as r3. Early timing shows ~630 ms per decision per actor in the bridge (the game itself), which is ~5k decisions/h per actor. So after the learner speed-up the fleet is likely actor-bound at ~30-35k decisions/h, and the 20 h timebox in f263b7b may be too short for 1M. The timebox will be revised from the measured steady-state rate.

M3-P007 r3 (stage m3-p007-dreamer-train-r3, launched 10:40) is running with all 7 actors ready, no bring-up failures, and log lines reading 'on 7 actors'. The steady-state rate reading is pending (~45-60 min in).

M3-P007 r3 steady-state rate: 899 decisions at 10:48:54 and 35,776 at 11:25:39, so ≈56.9k decisions/h across the fleet, on 7 actors (pid 1848394). At the same phase, attempt 1 ran ≈23.8k/h, so this is ≈2.4x faster. Latest line: bridge 254.5 ms, learn 58.3 ms wall per decision per actor; the learner lock is shared, so the learner is ~25-35% utilised and the fleet is actor-bound. No compile stall. At this rate, 1M decisions ≈ 17.5 h. Correction to my earlier comment: the 'actor-bound at ~30-35k/h, 20 h too short' estimate was wrong; it came from r2's first minutes, when per-decision bridge time was 630 ms. The 20 h timebox stands, and I will review it at 20 h rather than stop the run automatically.

M3-P007 r3 at ~214k decisions (14:50). Selection periods (near-greedy mean final wave): P1 10.70 at 50k, P2 14.81 at 100k (best), P3 14.80, P4 14.78. Under patience 5 / min-improvement 0.2 the run stops at ~350k unless a period reaches ≥15.01. Proposed to the developer: drop early stop and train to the full 1M, as a recorded deviation. Decision pending. Mechanics (scout): early stop cannot be turned off in a running process. After a stop, it can be resumed with --resume latest.pt --early-stop-patience-periods 0; weights, optimiser, counters and plateau history carry over, but replay is not persisted and restarts empty (a discontinuity). A clean alternative is a fresh launch without early stop.

DEVIATION from the M3-P007 pre-registration, decided by the developer on 2026-09-26 at ~15:10 at ~220k decisions (before any early-stop trigger): early stopping is dropped and the run trains to the full 1M budget. Reasons: fixed-budget training is standard practice (the DreamerV3 paper trains to a fixed step budget); plateaus followed by late gains are common, and M3-P006 stacked-dqn kept improving until 500k; the early-stop rule was our own budget-saver, not part of the method. Known in advance: the curve had plateaued at P2 14.81 / P3 14.80 / P4 14.78. Mechanics: r3 continues. If its old rule fires (at ~350k), it will be resumed from latest.pt with patience 0; replay then restarts empty, which is a recorded discontinuity. The arm is chosen over the union of periods under §9.2b. For comparability, the #85 stacked-dqn PER run will also train the full 1M without early stop. The durable experiments.md amendment will be written with the results.

M3-P007 r3 ended as the old pre-registered rule predicted: early stop at period 16 (800,124 decisions), exit 0, cleanup ok, wall 14:55:41. Periods 8-16 (near-greedy mean final wave): 15.09, 15.40, 15.51, 16.04 (P11, best), 15.73, 15.64, 15.47, 15.63, 15.69. Per the developer's decision (drop early stop), the continuation m3-p007-dreamer-train-r3-cont started at 01:37 from latest.pt with patience 0 and budget 1M. Replay restarts empty (this run predates #87); that is a recorded discontinuity.

Continuation m3-p007-dreamer-train-r3-cont (pid 3890664) resumed from latest.pt sha256 088574cffb59842b4a12d5f7bcc976ce8683a6c69928a34f42a065300e0fc0ff (sidecar verified), on 7 actors, no bring-up failures. Host was verified clean between segments. The arm will be selected over the union of both segments' periods.

M3-P007 training complete: the continuation ran to the 1M budget (1,000,076 decisions, exit 0, cleanup ok, wall 03:49:11, host verified clean). Continuation periods: P17 14.32 (the first period after the empty-replay resume: a dip), P18 14.96, P19 15.59, P20 15.49. The continuation's summary.json holds only P17-20; the union table was built from both logs. The arm under §9.2b over the union is P11 at 550,069 decisions (near-greedy 16.036), checkpoint-d0550069.pt, sha256 18b1743fe44a5a9aec9c5ca12b2cb6ac0480e76d387d4fb5a49505e5f11d740b (sidecar verified). The arm predates the resume, so the replay discontinuity does not touch it. Evaluation m3-p007-dreamer-eval-arm launched (default build, n=105).

M3-P007 evaluation (lead-recomputed from state/records/m3-p007/eval-arm): n=105 valid, mean 15.695, SD 3.533, 95% CI [15.02, 16.37]. P(≥20) 19/105 = 0.181, P(≥21) 2/105 = 0.019, P(≥22) 0. Histogram {9:1, 11:20, 12:15, 13:1, 14:2, 15:6, 16:9, 17:8, 18:10, 19:14, 20:17, 21:2}. No wave ≥22 episode anywhere in training or eval. Against M3-P006 stacked-dqn at the same budget (17.010, SD 4.163, n=104): difference -1.32, Welch 95% CI ≈ [-2.36, -0.27]. The pre-registered verdict is that DreamerV3 did not cross the wall under this recipe. Host verified clean (0 qemu, 0 adb). Next: write the results into experiments.md, then close this item.

Done: both 1M-decision runs are recorded. M3-P006 (stacked-dqn) is in 1af730c. M3-P007 (DreamerV3) results are in afcdf2a; the pre-registration is ce9c2e0 plus the amendment f263b7b, and the speed-up is da7a7bd. Closing.

items.title: stacked-dqn: turn on prioritized replay at published Ape-X/R2D2 values
items.body:
The developer's direction (2026-09-26): prioritized replay should be on. It has been off (--priority-alpha default 0.0, chosen so the loss is readable) since the first runs. It was flagged as deviation D4 in the #53 review and deliberately left unchanged to avoid confounds, then never revisited. Ape-X is literally 'Distributed Prioritized Experience Replay'; R2D2 uses sequence priorities with a max/mean mix (eta 0.9, alpha 0.9, IS beta 0.6).

Plan: one pre-registered single-change run on the M3-P005/P006 recipe, with the priority exponent, IS schedule and priority mix set to the cited published values, run after M3-P007 (DreamerV3) frees the devices.
Done when: the run is pre-registered, run and evaluated (n=105), with the results in docs/experiments.md.

comments.text: Developer decision 2026-09-26: prioritized replay is ON by default for stacked-dqn, and the option to turn it off is removed entirely (no --priority-alpha flag). DreamerV3 keeps uniform replay, which is its official setting. Values are fixed to the published R2D2 sequence-replay setting (the replay stores sequences with a max/mean priority mix); the implementer verifies them against the paper. Review tier C (replay semantics). Implemented in a worktree now; landed only after M3-P007's device run ends.

2026-09-26: bundled with #85, approved by the developer. Episode records (training and eval) gain the upgrades purchased per wave plus the upgrade levels and cash at episode end, so policies can be compared by what they buy. Implemented in a separate worktree (review tier B); lands together with the PER change after M3-P007 ends, so the first PER run records it.

Episode-records change: branch worktree-agent-ab1c17a241cef18ae @ 5e4ed52. The tier-B review APPROVED it (the family:slot identifier is stable by the action-space design; purchases are charged only when executed; one serialization point, evaluator.episode_record; old records still read). It is waiting to land after M3-P007 ends.

PER branch worktree-agent-a50a20ce2073dcf11 @ 4c18815 is done. Values α 0.9, β 0.6 fixed, η 0.9, from Acme's r2d2 config (the paper PDF was blocked). It fixed a latent IS-normalisation bug (buffer-wide max changed to batch max). The tier-C review is dispatched; it also investigates a test slowdown (a greedy loop on a zero-time action).

Tier-C review APPROVED 4c18815 with should-fixes, sent back to the implementer: the FakeRunPort rounding mismatch caused the slow test (fix the fake and revert the test workaround), a stale architecture.md line, and doc nits. Values independently confirmed in SEED RL's r2d2 learner (α 0.9 'from R2D2 paper, table 2', β 0.6 fixed, η 0.9, batch-max IS normalisation). Environment guard follow-up filed as https://github.com/Furkan-rgb/tower-rl/issues/86.

Review fixes landed on the branch as fd22178: the fake port compares rounded cash (the checkpoint-cadence test is back to ~5.6 s CPU-only on the loaded host), the test workaround is reverted, and stale docs are corrected. Gates: pytest exit 0 (CPU-only), ruff 0, mypy 0. Ready to land with 5e4ed52 (records) once the device host is clean.

Landed 2026-09-26: 6d22750 (episode records, merge of 5e4ed52) and aadf8f4 (PER always on for stacked-dqn, merge of 4c18815+fd22178). Gates on main: pytest exit 0 (1012 passed, CPU-only), ruff 0, mypy 0. Public scan clean; HEAD == origin/main. Remaining for the done-condition: the pre-registered stacked-dqn PER run and its evaluation, after the M3-P007 relaunch.

Decided 2026-09-26: the stacked-dqn PER run trains to the full 1M decisions without early stopping (patience 0), to match the M3-P007 DreamerV3 deviation on #84. The recipe is otherwise that of M3-P006.

M3-P008 pre-registered in aae14ee (M3-P006 recipe verbatim, early stop removed, PER always on, replay persistence active). Training stage m3-p008-stackeddqn-per-train launched. Doc nit to fix after the run: experiments.md line 51 cites '#87, aadf8f4' for PER; it should be '#85, aadf8f4'.
M3-P008 training started 2026-09-27 at ~06:16: stage m3-p008-stackeddqn-per-train, all 7 actors ready, no bring-up failures, first decision-time line 'on 7 actors'.

2026-09-27: The developer cut the M3-P008 run at about 241k of 1M decisions, so it gets no evaluation. The stacked-dqn run will restart under the Workshop runway profile (#80, baseline v2); the PER arm is unchanged. The stop is being executed by the run's worker, and the details will be recorded here.

M3-P008 stopped 2026-09-27 09:00 (SIGINT; exit 130, cleanup ok). Lead-verified: 0 qemu processes, empty adb devices.
- 278,966 of 1M decisions; not evaluated.
- Near-greedy means for P1-P5: 8.38, 13.36, 15.22, 15.01, 16.14. P6 was incomplete.
- The replay dump was written (4096 sequences, 0.85 GB, 7.7 s); first on-device confirmation of #87.
- Run dir: state/runs/session-20260927-061547/stacked-dqn-20260927-061547-8fb82c/.
- Superseded by the restart under the Workshop profile (#80). This result is recorded in experiments.md at the next landing.

Dispatched implementer-m3-p009-landing-run (2026-09-27): merge the #88 and #80 branches with gates and push; experiments.md entries (the M3-P008 stop, the Workshop device verification, the line-51 fix, the M3-P009 pre-registration: M3-P008's command plus --workshop-level 5, 1M decisions, workshop-render-interval-16 for training and workshop-default for eval); launch training with an early-signal check, then arm selection and eval n=105.

M3-P009 launched (pre-registered in adc0f0e); the Workshop landed in 42b605c.
- Early signal after about 29 min: 7 actors, bridge 53d346ae confirmed on every instance, about 26k decisions and 81 episodes.
- 7 episodes were invalid, all within the first 3.5k decisions (bring-up); their reasons appear in the summary at run end. None have been invalid since.
- Valid episodes: mean final wave 23.8, range 13-36.

M3-P009 at 11:40: about 100k of 1M decisions, 204 episodes (about 490 decisions per episode, against about 179 in M3-P008), about 77k decisions per hour, so about 12 h remain. 7 qemu processes are live.

M3-P009 interim at 173,619 decisions (12:31). These are training-time near-greedy readings, not the held-out eval. Period means: P1 26.31 (n=65), P2 35.73 (n=41), P3 37.74 (n=35). Rolling mean over the last 150 valid episodes is 32-33. Best episode reached wave 52. Validity 302/312; 7 of the 10 invalid came during bring-up, and the reasons are recorded only in summary.json at run end. For reference: scripted at Workshop L5 reached 21, 21, 21; M3-P008 (v1) periods were 8.4-16.1.

M3-P009 was stopped deliberately at 325,493 decisions (14:23, exit 130, cleanup verified). It is superseded by the corrected configuration (#92/#93). Near-greedy period means:
- P1 26.31 (n=65)
- P2 35.73 (n=41)
- P3 37.74 (n=35)
- P4 37.92 (n=37)
- P5 34.48 (n=40)
- P6 41.85 (n=33); the arm at stop.
Validity 535/556; the invalid reasons are unrecoverable (no summary.json, see #91). The checkpoints d0025285 to d0325171 and the replay (0.81 GB) are kept under state/runs/session-20260927-102908/. No eval.

M3-P010 launched 14:42 (pre-registered in 5bd8eaf); run folder state/runs/m3-p010-stackeddqn-v2-20260927T124233Z/. First 7 episodes were all valid, final waves 19-23. Config verified from the manifest.

M3-P010 throughput check (scout, read-only, ~40 min in). Fleet decisions per hour fell from ~77k (0-10k decisions) to 38-66k, but game-seconds per decision rose from 2.7 to 4.3-5.8, and decisions per episode fell from ~290 to ~134-187. Game-time throughput is therefore equal or higher: ~221-282k game-s/h, against M3-P009's ~176-191k.

Inference (the lead): the early M3-P010 policy waits less (window-0 log shows wait 44%, against 83% in M3-P009's late replay). A buy that exhausts cash folds the following advance into its step, so it makes fewer, longer decisions. That is not slower emulation. CPU has headroom (load 19.5/32), and no qemu process or train.py is swapped.

Consequence: a decisions budget is a policy-dependent amount of game experience. An ETA of ~20 h or more is plausible.

M3-P010 at 308k decisions (15:28 UTC, 2h40m). Near-greedy period means:
- P1 23.71 (n=147)
- P2 26.28 (n=53)
- P3 27.04 (n=48)
- P4 27.51 (n=49)
- P5 27.18 (n=50)
- P6 27.16 (n=50)
M3-P009 at the same decision counts: 26.31, 35.73, 37.74, 37.92, 34.48, 41.85. M3-P010 is flat at ~27 from 150k to 300k, about 10 waves below.

Validity 735/770. Wait share rose from 44% to 84%, and game-s per decision fell to 1.58, so the fleet rate is now ~115k decisions/h. Best episode 51 (exploratory, at 7k decisions).

Lead's leading hypothesis: 9x fewer gradient steps (0.114 vs 1.0 per decision; ~34k vs ~300k updates at 300k decisions). Candidate contributors: AdamW eps 1.5e-4 damping small-gradient updates, and the longer horizon slowing credit assignment. None has been tested yet.

M3-P010 plateau diagnosis (2026-09-27, specialist, offline on mlflow and checkpoints; scratchpad p010-plateau.md):
- Root cause: 9x fewer gradient steps (ratio 0.114). At 300k decisions M3-P010 had 33.8k steps against M3-P009's 296k. At matched steps the two runs track within 2.5-4 waves.
- AdamW eps 1.5e-4 damps 41% of parameters by more than 2x, and would cut even M3-P009's step by 36%.
- Q scale is correct for gamma 0.999. Huber is not a bottleneck.
Decision (developer chose option 2):
- Stop M3-P010.
- Revert gradient steps to 1.0, eps to 1e-8 and replay capacity to 4096.
- Keep gamma 0.999, refresh-100 and left-padding.
- M3-P011 is screened at 150k decisions with kill-bars, then continues to 1M if it passes.

M3-P011 (merge 30ea762; run m3-p011-stackeddqn-v2-20260927T155835Z; mlflow 813cd2b6) stopped itself on its pre-registered kill-bar at 100k decisions: near-greedy mean 31.84 (n=44) over (50k,100k], below 32.
- Periods vs M3-P009 at the same points: 25.35 vs 26.31; 31.86 vs 35.73.
- Gradient norm: 22/20 vs 13.5/6.9 (above the clip of 10).
- Value-fit: 0.87/0.77 vs 0.92/0.88.
- Validity 204/205. Cleanup verified.
Remaining differences from M3-P009: gamma 0.999, refresh-100, left-padding. The larger Q scale at gamma 0.999 fits the elevated, clipped gradient norm.
Per the pre-registration, next is M3-P012: same config at gamma 0.997.

Developer delegation (2026-09-27): the lead compares and iterates the screens, and approves committing a run to the full 1M only after it passes the pre-registered screen.
Iteration order if a screen fails: γ 0.997 (M3-P012) → revert refresh-100 → revert left-padding. Each change is one screen.

Revised iteration order: if M3-P012 fails, consult the specialist before any further revert. Refresh-100 and left-padding are not blind-revert candidates:
- Refresh-100 is Ape-X's published cadence (actors pull parameters every 400 frames, i.e. 100 agent steps).
- Left-padding fixes a real bug (#92: opening decisions were never learned).
Also judge screens against M3-P009 with single-seed variance in mind; M3-P009 is one run, not a law.

M3-P012 (γ 0.997; run m3-p012-stackeddqn-v2-20260927T172101Z; mlflow cf08b3fd) stopped on kill-bar 2 at 100,279 decisions: near-greedy mean 28.44 (n=70) over (50k,100k], below 32. Periods 26.14 and 28.55. Validity 255/257. Cleanup verified.
- The mechanism check passed: gradient norm 8.5/7.4 and value-fit 0.89/0.83, against M3-P011's 22/20 and 0.87/0.77.
- Performance did not recover: 28.4 vs M3-P011's 31.9 vs M3-P009's 35.7.
So γ fixed the gradient symptom but not the waves; γ is not the cause.
Open question: is M3-P009 a favourable single seed? Specialist consult is next, before any further change or revert.

Specialist (scratchpad p009-gap.md) findings:
- Sampling noise of a period mean is 0.3-0.7 waves, but between-run path noise has SD ~3-4. M3-P011's and M3-P012's gaps to M3-P009 are 0.8σ and 1.5σ, so not significant. M3-P009 is plausibly a favourable draw.
- Left-padding is near-inert: filler sits only in a burn-in, and the mask is verified.
- No bug in refresh-100. It is the only lever left with a plausible mechanism: churn from tracking a fast-moving net.
- The kill-bar at 32 was too tight for n=1 screens.
Decision (lead, delegated): stop n=1 recipe screening. Launch M3-P013 as the stacked-dqn 1M arm: M3-P012's config with --parameter-sync-decisions 0 (M3-P009's cadence; M3-P009-equivalent apart from inert padding).
- Collapse-only kill-bars: 50000:25000:25, 100000:50000:27, 150000:100000:29, 300000:200000:30.
- The (50k,150k] mean is read at 150k for information only.

Parameter policy (developer direction, 2026-09-27): stacked-dqn and DreamerV3 run on published values or values known to work on this game. No single-run tuning: single-run screens cannot resolve gaps under ~10 waves.

Developer decision (2026-09-27): stop M3-P013, fix the three parameters not grounded in theory, and rerun at 1M. The three: reuse ~500:1 with no resets, batch 8, actor staleness ~3,850 updates.
Agreed approach: adopt one coherent published recipe for the sample-efficient regime (BBF-style: high replay ratio with periodic resets, and a fresher actor refresh), not guessed numbers. Lowering reuse to Ape-X levels is excluded, because M3-P010 showed that performance tracks gradient-step count.
A specialist is designing the recipe from the fetched papers.

M3-P013 (run m3-p013-stackeddqn-v2-20260927T185504Z; mlflow 9b9c8ecb) stopped by developer decision at 11,174 decisions (SIGINT 19:09 UTC), before period 1, so there is no performance evidence. Validity 46/47. Stage exit 130, cleanup verified. latest.pt kept.
The experiments.md row still describes M3-P013 as launched; it gets updated with the next recipe's pre-registration.

Recipe design (specialist, scratchpad dqn-recipe.md; every value derived as principle → quantity → our value):
- Batch 8 and 1.0 steps per decision are derived, not odd. The earlier '~500:1 reuse' overcounted correlated positions: effective reuse is 9-82 per decision, which is BBF's RR-8 level. The critical batch from the McCandlish noise scale is 3.5-15.6 windows, and the learner is compute-bound.
- Refresh every 10 decisions: lag ~70 updates, against Ape-X ~53 and BBF-EMA 199.
- SR-SPR resets every 100k gradient steps, none in the last 100k: 9 resets, interval ≈ 4× the offline-measured recovery of 20-30k. Core and heads are re-initialised; trunk shrink-and-perturbs at 0.8/0.2; target ← online; optimiser state for reset parameters is cleared; the n-step anneal restarts.

- Final waves are wide, not a wall: after 100k SD 12.9, range 11–72; 29% of actor-6 episodes reach ≥55.
- Under γ 0.997, the value of one more wave survived drops to 0.015 at 40 waves out, below the TD noise (~0.22). Action gaps are 0.006–0.05, and greedy behaviour on identical early states changes between checkpoints (WAIT share 0.29–0.95).
- Reset cycle: near-greedy peak at 20–30k steps after a reset (50.6), falling to ~38 by 80–100k in 7 of 9 cycles.

- Purchase-to-death delay (median): Thorns 1264 s, Defense % 1054 s, Health 853 s, Defense Absolute 800 s, Knockback 619–750 s. Credit delay τ ≈ 1050–1630 s.

The signal-to-noise optimum is γ* = exp(−k/τ) ≈ 0.9994 per game-second. At 0.999 we keep ≥69% (mean 88%) of it; at 0.997 ≤26%.

items.title: Environment: guard against a repeated zero-time rejected purchase looping to the decision cap
items.body: Found in the #85 review (2026-09-26). The environment's _classify treats a bridge-rejected purchase (precondition_failed) as a normal zero-game-time transition. If the mask says a purchase is legal and the bridge rejects it, a greedy policy sees identical features and repeats the action until the actor's 20,000-decision cap (the episode ends MAX_EPISODE_DURATION). This was triggered in tests by a FakeRunPort rounding mismatch, which is being fixed on the #85 branch. On the real path the mask and the bridge precondition agree exactly (%.17g serialisation, identical preconditions), so real-device risk is judged low. Not verified: whether the world stays paused between commands. A guard (for example, treat a repeated rejection of a mask-legal action as an invalid episode with a classified reason) would make a disagreement fail loudly. Done when: a mask/bridge disagreement ends the episode as invalid with a named reason, under test.

comments.text: Implemented within the #88 package (b179203/b6e5c5f): the first mask-legal rejection ends the episode as MASK_LEGAL_REJECTED. Moved to In progress for the landing merge.

items.title: Replay memory survives a resume: save it at run exit, reload it on --resume
items.body: Today a resumed run (scripts/train.py --resume) restarts with an empty replay buffer and re-warms it. That is a discontinuity in the learner's training distribution, and it matters most for DreamerV3's world model. The official DreamerV3 implementation persists replay to disk and reloads it. Done when: at run exit (budget end, early stop, SIGINT, or exception), the run writes its replay contents together with a latest checkpoint at the same decision count; --resume from that checkpoint reloads the replay exactly (contents, priorities, cursor), and refuses a mismatched dump; stacked-dqn and dreamerv3 both use it (one PrioritizedSequenceReplay class); tests prove a save→load round trip is exact; gates are green; Tier C review passes. The live M3-P007 run cannot use it (its code is fixed).

comments.text: Implementation on branch worktree-agent-a121b34cfd0544776 (3b2b0b2): <run_dir>/replay/ holds .npy step table plus sequence indices (shared steps stored once) and replay.json, written atomically. It is saved once at run exit (normal end before the final evaluation, and in the finally-path on exception/SIGINT) under TrainingRun.held_still, alongside latest.pt at the same decision count. On --resume it is reloaded only when decisions, capacity, sampling and identity match; otherwise the resume is refused. Gates: pytest 1029 passed / 27 skipped (CPU), ruff 0, mypy 0. Estimate for a 40k-sequence Dreamer buffer: ~6.4 GB, 1-2 min save/load (extrapolated from 500 sequences). Follow-ups requested: a finite-weights guard before the exception-path save, and unverified doc wording removed. Tier C review next.

Tier C review: approve-with-fixes. Blocking: on Ctrl-C the pool's actor threads keep running after the save, so they can rewrite latest.pt at a later count than the dump and the resume is then refused. Fix: a halt flag set in held_still stops actors from recording, learning or checkpointing. Should-fix: the normal-path replay save must catch any Exception, so the final evaluation always runs. Nits: range-check sequence_episode, resolve the --resume path, a progress line before the save, drop the unneeded .previous swap. Exactness, lock order, exception propagation and the resume guard were verified OK. Fixes dispatched to the implementer.

Recheck of 46b21c2: approve. The halt flag is read only in _collect_until, so the final evaluation (which calls evaluate() directly) and the summary writes are unaffected. After a halt, nothing writes latest.pt, numbered checkpoints or replay. The last small fix (test hang guards, and advance() refusing after a halt) is in progress. Landing waits until the live M3-P007 device run and its evaluation end.

Final fix be1635f: the interrupt test has a daemon thread and a deadline; advance() raises after a halt. Focused tests 172 passed / 1 skipped, ruff 0, mypy 0. Branch worktree-agent-a121b34cfd0544776 (3b2b0b2, 3ff3702, 46b21c2, be1635f) is review-approved and ready to land. It lands after the live M3-P007 run and its evaluation end, before the #85 run. The done-condition's full-suite gate will be rerun at landing.

items.title: Episodes end only at game over: remove the per-episode decision and wall-clock caps
items.body:
The developer's direction (2026-09-27): there should be no per-game length limit. Two caps exist today:
- actor.py:54 `max_decisions_per_episode = 20_000`. The last step is stored with done=False and the episode ends as MAX_EPISODE_DURATION.
- run_environment.py:126 `max_episode_wall_seconds = 900.0`. The environment classifies this as MAX_EPISODE_DURATION as well.

With the Workshop profile (#80), episodes are expected to reach w50-110, which is roughly 5-10 min of wall time per game. The 900 s cap would cut exactly the episodes that matter.

Hang protection should detect a lack of progress (no game time advancing, or the repeated rejected purchase in #86), not limit the length.

Done when: neither cap can end a progressing episode; a stalled episode still ends with a named reason; tests cover both; the scout's check of past records for any cap-truncated episodes is recorded here.

comments.text: Scout: 0 of 2692 recorded episodes ended with max_episode_duration; the live M3-P008 session was excluded. MAX_EPISODE_DURATION counts as an invalid episode (VALID_TERMINATIONS = {GAME_OVER}, episode.py:32). Apart from the two caps, there is no stall or liveness detector. Sequenced after the #80 Workshop package, because both touch run_environment.py.

Started 2026-09-27 (implementer-no-length-caps, worktree). The package also covers #86 (a mask-legal rejection ends the game invalid) and per-row in-run cost logging at wave entry (#80). It runs in parallel with the Workshop package, with its run_environment.py edits kept apart from reset() and availability.

Implemented in b179203 (branch worktree-agent-ae642d3c5f2287a99, not merged); gates green, exit 0 each.
- Both caps are removed, and MAX_EPISODE_DURATION is gone.
- A STALLED outcome fires when game time hasn't advanced for 120 s of wall time; it is checked every step.
- MASK_LEGAL_REJECTED fires on the first mask-legal rejection (#86).
- Per-wave upgrade_costs are recorded (family:index to the raw cost).
Tier B review is running.

- Should-fix: reconcile rl-candidates.md:412/944; fixes directed.
- Accepted risk: first-rejection MASK_LEGAL_REJECTED (#86's pause assumption is unverified); its real-device rate will be read from the records.
- Merge with a83c20f: one trivial additive conflict of constants in run_environment.py.

Review fixes in b6e5c5f (branch worktree-agent-ae642d3c5f2287a99). The stall check now also runs on every internal advance in _advance_to_decision, with a test for zero game time inside the choice-points loop. rl-candidates.md is reconciled, and the upgrade_costs test checks against the fake port's raw costs. Gates exit 0. The lead inspected the diff. Ready to land together with the #80 Workshop branch.

items.title: Record each run's full upgrade setup explicitly: per-row in-run availability and Workshop level, as read back from the game
items.body:
The developer wants a run's setup recorded well enough that future variations (e.g. fewer in-run upgrade options, a different Workshop set) stay distinguishable and comparable.

Today (verified in the M3-P009 manifest): `upgrade_availability` is recorded as a mode ("all"), `workshop_level` as a number, and `workshop_rows` as the requested names. The checkpoint identity checks the mode and the level only. Nothing records WHICH in-run rows were actually available, or the Workshop levels the game read back.

Done when:
- every episode record, and the run manifest, carries an explicit per-row table for all in-run rows: family, index, name, whether available in the run, and Workshop level, taken from the bridge's read-back after the setup is applied, not from the requested config;
- the checkpoint identity carries a digest of that table, so evaluating under a different setup is refused;
- tests cover it; docs are reconciled.

items.title: stacked-dqn never trains on an episode's opening decisions
items.body:
Found 2026-09-27 (specialist audit; the lead verified the code). In actor.py `_windows` (lines 212-215), window 0 starts at step 0 and its burn-in prefix covers steps 0..burn_in-1 (7 for stacked-dqn). So an episode's first 7 decisions are never a learning target. Only episodes shorter than one window get left-padded (line 211); at baseline v2, where episodes run ~550 decisions, essentially none are.

Fix (specialist recommendation): left-pad every episode with burn_in filler steps (reuse `_left_padded`'s filler) before cutting windows. The padding flag already keeps filler out of the loss and the priorities. Stored data changes, so this applies to new runs only, not resumes.

Done when a unit test shows step 0's transition is a learning target in a long episode.

items.title: stacked-dqn configuration deviations from Ape-X/R2D2/BBF: horizon, replay ratio, actor staleness, Adam eps
items.body:
Specialist audit, 2026-09-27. Full detail and sources are in the session scratchpad dqn-config-audit.md; the arithmetic is below.

Matches the papers: the Ape-X epsilon ladder formula, PER alpha 0.9 / beta 0.6 and eta 0.9 (R2D2), double + dueling, and lr 1e-4. Justified via BBF: n-step 10 to 3, EMA target tau 0.005, and Huber without h-rescaling (because V is small).

Deviations, each unmeasured:
1. gamma 0.997 per game-second gives a 333 s horizon (~9.5 waves; V_max 9.51). Episodes now last 25+ waves and the target is 50-110, so from early states a wave-35 death and a wave-70 death look nearly identical. Candidate: 0.999/s (~28.6 waves), plus R2D2's h if returns grow.
2. Replay ratio: 1.0 gradient step per decision, about 560 replayed transitions per new one (Ape-X ~0.8, R2D2 ~0.4, BBF 256 with resets, which we lack). solution.md 9.4 still says 0.25. No recorded rationale.
3. Actor weights refresh once per episode, ~3,850 learner steps stale (Ape-X ~50). stacked-dqn has no recurrent state, so a refresh every K decisions (e.g. 400) is safe.
4. AdamW eps is 1e-8 (Rainbow 1.5e-4, R2D2 1e-3); this is #53 D5.
5. Minor: 8 sequences per batch, 4096-window replay (~16% of budget; the DreamerV3 recipe uses 40k), and 100-sequence warm-up.

M3-P009 runs unchanged as pre-registered. Any change is a pre-registered new run or a single-variable ablation.

items.title: An invalid-cut mid-game no longer cascades: the cut game recovers or ends, and the first invalid reason of every episode is visible live
items.body: Found during M3-P016. After an invalid end, reset resumes the same frozen game as a new episode (instrumented_run_adapter.py:215/231/285) at wave 22+, which re-trips within a few decisions (bursts of up to 20; M3-P015 actors 2-5 had 44-86 invalid each, 256/1009 overall; M3-P016 8/101 at 20.7k). The invalid step is stored as truncation, not death (actor.py:139). Its tail windows are dropped from replay (replay.py:223). Invalid episodes are excluded from means and kill bars (training.py:583,1399,1430); there is a plausible late-game bias, not measured. The trigger is unknown: reasons persist only in end-of-run records (#91). game_ms 1926/2568 = 3/4 x 642 ms recurs across runs. Evidence: session scratchpad m3-p016/invalid-diagnosis.md.

comments.text: M3-P016 at ~350k: collection window 5 (episodes 500-599) had 18 of 61 invalid (30%) mid-window, spread over 6 actors (a6 7, a5 4, a0 2, a2 2, a4 2, a1 1). Earlier windows: 8, 7, 5, 5, 3 of 100. Not a single-actor cascade; it could be time-correlated or tied to late-game states. The reason is not visible live, so the end-of-run records are needed.

M3-P016 relaunch: a SIGINT at 09:29:08 did NOT stop gracefully. train.py raised KeyboardInterrupt from arm.training.run() (training.py:1027, the ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown join), so no summary.json, no episode records and no invalid reasons. Device cleanup passed 7/7. M3-P015's SIGINT had stopped gracefully, so this is a regression or depends on timing (a resume pair was written 29 s after the SIGINT). Graceful SIGINT is now part of this item's scope, alongside live reasons and the cascade.

Evidence (M3-P016 relaunch, from MLflow): 103 of 284 invalid, in 12 chains. Each chain starts with a long normal episode (370-920 decisions, w16-32) that ends invalid, then 1-32 episodes of 1-10 decisions, ~2.5 game-s each, continuing the same game (wave +1 every 1-2 episodes) until a tiny valid GAME_OVER. Resume saves are ruled out as the trigger. Reason text unrecoverable. Dispatched in parallel, both Tier C: (B) environment: after an invalid end, recover to a fresh game instead of resuming, with cause analysis and a <=30 min device check; (A) learning/experiment: graceful SIGINT at any moment plus live per-episode invalid reasons (#91 if small).

Package A done: 39d2eb7 on worktree-agent-a73c05cac36d2b8ed. Cause proven: train.py had no SIGINT handler. The KeyboardInterrupt hit the main thread in the executor join and skipped the summary. Correction: M3-P015 ended with the same traceback and no summary; it did not stop gracefully as I had claimed. Fix: the first SIGINT sets a stop flag (a kill-bar-equivalent end), the second forces exit. Tests cover real-subprocess SIGINT at warm-up, mid-episode, mid-learn, mid-save and final eval. Live invalid-reason line, MLflow episode_termination code, per-reason window counts, and per-segment episodes.jsonl (#91). pytest 1228 passed; ruff and mypy exit 0. Open: SIGTERM is unhandled; B's EpisodeSummary fields are not yet wired.

Developer decision (2026-09-30): 'the world is held whenever the agent is deciding' becomes a guaranteed environment invariant. It is enforced at the single point where control returns to the agent and covered by a contract test on every path (reset/fresh/retired/recovered, advance, non-advancing purchase, WAIT, speed/lifecycle presses), plus a device check. Added to package B. Snapshots are now allowed, including a writable instance to create a pinned snapshot.

Package B done: c843f85 on worktree-agent-abf97a3bbcd39c608 (ADR 0015). Proven on device: the cascade (a reset continued the same run 2/2) and the wave-1 stale race (0.3 s think: 3/3 stale -> 0/220 after the fix). Fix: reset retires any live run through the death-to-new-run path (WAIT until game over; 19-30 s at w7-12), then a fresh wave-1 round with settings re-verified. Round start ends with the game's own pause, and the world_held check at the single handoff point refuses a running world as WORLD_NOT_HELD. The mid-game chain-starting cut is still unexplained (inside an episode the world is held 100/100); A's live reasons will name it. pytest 1242 passed; ruff and mypy exit 0. Tier C review of B+A integrated is running.

Tier C review of B+A integrated: ready with concerns (1251 passed, ruff 0, mypy 0). Must fix before an overnight run: 1) retirement measures progress on game_ms instead of round_ms and has no wall-clock ceiling, so it could loop under GAME_TIME_DEFLATED; 2) the docs say a second SIGINT exits at once, which is false; 3) the world_held mirror is wrong after clock_unavailable or a reconnect; 4) the window line misses WORLD_NOT_HELD and GAME_TIME_DEFLATED, and failed starts are not logged live. A fresh implementer is integrating these fixes on p95-integration. A bridge-reported world_paused is deferred to #98.

Landed in b699ee7 (pushed 65a1c29..b699ee7). A reset now retires a live run to game over, bounded by round-clock progress and a 300 s ceiling. The world is checked held at every handoff, and a running world is refused as WORLD_NOT_HELD. Device evidence: 4/4 cuts retired, and the 0.3 s stale race went from 3/3 to 0 in 220 decisions. Each episode's first invalid reason is logged live, and all 14 reasons are counted. Gates: 1267 passed, ruff 0, mypy 0.

items.title: A stacked-dqn run identical to M3-P015 except with resets off is pre-registered, run to 1M decisions and recorded, and it or M3-P015 is named the DQN comparator for Dreamer
items.body: Rationale: resets (Nikishin et al. 2022; BBF) counter primacy bias at high replay ratio. Ours is ~1 gradient step per decision with a 4096-sequence buffer and a 128-wide network, so the premise is weak. M3-P015 evidence: the period after each reset scored lower than the one before (100k: 30.77->29.82, 200k: 32.35->28.93, 300k: 34.38->32.00). That is 3/3 in one run, about p=1/8 by chance, with 25% invalid episodes. Change: omit --reset-every-steps (default 0 = off); all other M3-P015 flags unchanged. Runs after M3-P016 frees the devices.

comments.text: Capacity check (read-only, MLflow): M3-P014 also ran with resets (9 logged); M3-P015 had 4. In P015 the loss drops fast, then plateaus flat at |TD| ~1% of Q, with value-fit corr 0.85-0.90 and recovery within 10-20k steps after each reset. That shape does not suggest a capacity limit, but a loss floor cannot separate noise from capacity. P014's fit degrades as play improves (corr 0.9 -> 0.6-0.75), likely harder targets. Keep width 128 for #96. The decisive test is an offline 128-vs-256/512 fit on the P015 replay dump with held-out loss. Evidence: session scratchpad m3-p015/capacity-check.md.

More reset evidence from M3-P014 (resets every ~100k): the period right after a reset dipped vs the period before in 7 of 9 (periods 3,5,9,11,15,17,19; rose at 7,13). Non-reset periods: 4 up, 5 down. Combined with M3-P015: 10 of 12 post-reset periods dipped. That is suggestive, not conclusive, because period means are noisy and alternate.

Design note: #96 (M3-P015 config, resets off) vs M3-P014 changes two things at once, reward/discount (0.999 + survival bound vs 0.997, no bound) and resets, so it cannot attribute a difference. Accepted for the wave-100 goal. If #96 lands within ~1 CI of M3-P014, add an isolating run: M3-P014 config with resets off.
Retired by developer decision: stacked-dqn has no resets. They come from a pixel-regime recipe whose premise doesn't hold here. Removal is folded into #110. No resets-on vs resets-off run.
Retired: the developer decided stacked-dqn has no resets. The code removal lands under #110; no run needed.
